keys.dialogue: Mother Mystra, you are remembered!  Even now, your token is known.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: This medallion is a welcome sight to me. I had feared that the spinning centuries had put an end to our Lady's worship in this land.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But none of you are strangers to the Mother of Mystery. The touch of Mystra is upon you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn
keys.desc: spoken to the party, with glad surprise

keys.dialogue: For her sake and for yours, let me give what aid I can. But speak swiftly children, for without the place-binding of my bones, my foothold in your time is light. The past summons me back to face my death again.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The priest sees clearly. Our Lady mourns the corruption of that which was her delight, the greatest spell ever to be raised in Faerun: the Mythal.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The new foe. Yes, I feel them, even through the years: there is a shadow spitting flame and a soft voice. Know this: their strength is stolen from the strength of the Mythal.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: They have raised an abomination under the very seat of the Coronal. An abomination that cracks stone and earth in its hunger, reaching ever outward to feed. But as I look forward I see only back...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Mythanthor's overmantle. The guardian spell...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The Armies of Darkness cleft its strength asunder in the Weeping Wars, foiling the magical gates that could have been our escape. But the Mythal's weave is deep.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: It sings yet in the air around you, though the tune is off. Some corruption warps the Mythal to its will. Can you not find Miroden to tune it?  Whose voice? Who calls?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Ah, the beauty of those times... the Serpentspires, the Glim-gardens... We floated on the air!  But then the wars. The blood. The keening flameswords...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. I know him well. A master of lore and the keeper of our hopes. Before he relinquished his mortal life, he was a great mage, an elven lord. Now he is a Baelnorn. An undead guardian.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: His existence is bound to the Sapphire of the Weave, through which he can tune and repair the Mythal.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: He guards it deep within the catacombs, in a lair sealed with the Glyph of Safekeeping. This Word will allow you to pass...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell teaches you Kehelben, the Word of Necessity.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Use it, children!  Find Miroden and restore the Mythal, before the Armies of Darkness beat down our gates. No... no... those armies have come and gone...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: I am little help here, trapped between now and gone. Since the desecration of my grave, my spirit only flickers in this time. I beat my fists against the centuries, but still the past recalls me and I die again...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: For centuries, my bones bound me to this plane. My spirit moved freely in this city and I fought darkness where I could. But such work draws enemies. A lich I battled sent his minions to disturb my grave and break my bond with this sacred shrine.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: They undid the charms that bound my tomb and stole back to the catacombs with my skull for trophy. Without it, I am a feeble shade. Ah. I can hear their laughter...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Miroden's Sapphire is tuned to the Mythal. With it, he can restore the fraying weave of old Mythanthor's spell.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: He is bound to the gem as its Communicant: a vessel for its cleansing fire. Find him!  My time grows short...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Her intentions for you, I know not, but you are known to her. It is she that weaves your path: her will is the loom, your deeds, the thread. But hark: trumpets...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. He is the Mythal's Protector. Before he relinquished his mortal life, he was a great mage, an elven lord. Now he is a Baelnorn. An undead guardian.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Restore it? That magic is beyond the living. Seek out the baelnorn Miroden. His bond serves to tune the Mythal. His strength can aid you. In time past, his wisdom was a beacon to us all...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Elminster Aumar lives yet?  Time, your hand crushes some but never all.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: How can I help the friends of the Chosen of Mystra?  We of Myth Drannor do not forget our debts. We do not forget...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Forgive me, children, in my ears, the din of Myth Drannor's fall drowns out your voices. Ah, the thunder!  I will strive to hear you. Speak again.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The tide moves back again... Eltargrim, oh Coronal, where are you?  Are the Tel'Quessir to be uncaptained in this dark sea? We must fortify the Mythal. Trasaal... Ailos... summon the armathors!
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: No, that time is gone!  The Towers of Song have crumbled. I must face the living moment...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Night falls again on the eve of my destruction. The spellfire comes... Who will shield us?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Children, my death revisits me. Speak quickly now before I am caught up in its blaze again.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The clouds burn!  Flee, priestesses, we are undone!  Mother Mystra, hear me - so long as my bones rest in your temple, let my spirit walk this plane to do your will!  I...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Oh, the silence...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: No!  Do not leave me to the past. The future is in need!
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The Mythal is black with corruption. The Protector must tune its weave. Seek out Miroden Silverblade, baelnorn of the Gem.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: His lair is deep within the catacombs, sealed with the Glyph of Safekeeping. This Word will allow you to pass...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell teaches you Kehelben, the Word of Necessity.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: My time is done... Hear me!
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Mystra's will is with you, but my hold on this plane fails me.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Base creatures have stolen my skull into the catacombs. Without it here on my altar, I slip...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: My grip fails, this time slips from my grasp...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Elminster was an armathor of Myth Drannor, a favorite of the Coronal. But that was long before the Weeping Wars, when the streets were lit by elven laughter and our city was the jewel of great Cormanthyr's crown.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Ah, how the nobles would have shuddered that any human, even the Chosen of Mystra, could outlive all our glory...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Ill tidings indeed! You must free him, children. But beware! For anyone with the power to imprison Miroden Silverblade is a formidable opponent indeed... but hark...

keys.dialogue: Again my fate calls me... I slip away! Farewell!

keys.dialogue: You tell Anorrweyn about the many drow you defeated, deep within the Catacombs...

keys.dialogue: But still the drow hold my skull - I know this to be true. But harken, children! I have only moments left...

keys.dialogue: Remember what I told you! You must free the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade... or the Mythal's corruption will overwhelm us again, in living fire...

keys.dialogue: Go now. May Mystra keep you - and bring you here to me again when the Baelnorn is free.

keys.dialogue: Worry not about Kya Mordrayn. I will hold her attention, for the moment. You must set yourselves to the great task of freeing the Baelnorn, Miroden Silverblade.

keys.dialogue: Come back here when you have talked with him, and I will meet with you again. Until then, may Mystra guide you...

keys.dialogue: He has the power to restore the corrupted Mythal. Have you no news of him?

keys.dialogue: As soon as you place the skull, you feel a ghostly presence.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The place-binding is sealed. My spirit stands firm in the present moment once again.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: You have striven much to restore me. Let Mystra's blessings comfort you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn
keys.desc: Spoken, generous, she heals & resurrects the party

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds and restores life to the dead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your deeds have brought hope, but the corruption within the Mythal grows.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: You must find the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade. He can tune the Mythal and bend its strength to guardianship again.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: It lies deep within the catacombs. Deeper than your path has taken you. Look beyond the Glyph of Safekeeping. The way is open to you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Such valor! The dark Children of Lloth are pitiless foes. Their presence here is ill news indeed.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Then you must free him!  Without his aid, we cannot cleanse the Mythal of its corruption.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Even now the darkness is spreading. The evil under Castle Cormanthor reaches out across Faerun. Its hunger will not be slaked until we wrench the Mythal from its grip.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: There are dark paths here in the city, where none but the dead may walk. I will walk them. Thus may the minds of our enemies be distracted away from you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Return to my shrine when you have news from the baelnorn, and I will come forth again to meet you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Move quickly, children. The Mythal is once again a shield about the city, but one that weakens good and shelters evil.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Its spell was woven by faith. And faith can redeem it. But if it is lost to hatred and despair, then so are we all.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Find Miroden. With him lies our salvation.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Rescue Miroden. With him lies our salvation.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May the Goddess refresh you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds and restores life to the dead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May the Goddess refresh you.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May you find ease in Mystra's holy shrine.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The air about us still reeks of the Mythal's corruption. Have you not found Miroden Silverblade?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: You carry a Gem of the Weave - but it is not the Sapphire. What has happened?  And what has become of Miroden Silverblade?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: No one in this time, I fear. Its ways are deep. The intricacies of its web would overpower mortal minds. Why do you ask this?  What has happened?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: How can this be?  Miroden's wards and traps have made his lair impregnable for centuries. No mortal could enter that labyrinth uninvited.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Your service will not be forgotten. But why has he not restored the Mythal?  The darkness is about us yet...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Madness!  Can he have done such a thing?  Without a Gem of the Weave, the Mythal cannot be tuned.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But why?  Why would he?  And how?  For surely his own existence is bound to the Gem. Can he have destroyed it and survived?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Better that, I suppose, than letting the Gem fall into the hands of his captors.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Yes... His bond would demand such a sacrifice. And yet he survived to tell this tale. I wonder...
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: So he destroyed the Gem to prevent it falling into the hands of this Cult.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Your service will not be forgotten.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But surely his own existence is bound to the Gem. He must have destroyed it rather than let it fall into the hands of his captors.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: The Mythal holds Myth Drannor's hope... and its doom.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Corrupted, it feeds evil as surely as it once nurtured good. Until it is restored, the darkness under Castle Cormanthor will reach ever further.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: So Miroden is powerless?  Then I must step forward, and dare the fire of the Mythal.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: If Miroden is powerless then how can we proceed? The Mythal must be cleansed.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: I remember when this city rose like a song of joy into the sky. What would I not sacrifice to hear even a strain of that song again?  But to enter the heart of the Mythal?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Do you know what it is you demand?  The power of the weave is great, greater perhaps than strength left in my spirit.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But how can I refuse?  For the sake of hope, you have braved the depths of the catacombs and beaten back the abominations that defiled our holy places. I will do what I can.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: So you hope I will become its Communicant, and brave the Mythal's fire?
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: What you ask may be beyond me. The power of the weave is great, greater perhaps than the strength left in my spirit.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But how can I not try, when you've already risked life and limb all for the sake of hope?  I will do what I can.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: No!  The fire of the weave would consume you. You have fought bravely and well. This last sacrifice is not yours to make.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: I shall speak the incantation, and offer myself as the new Communicant. It may be that communing with the Mythal requires more power than I have left in my spirit.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: But if you can brave the depths of the catacombs, all for the sake of hope, then I can gather hope to brave the Mythal's fiery web.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Long ago, the Coronal entrusted the Onaglym dwarves with the Gems of the Weave. Their fortress hides one yet. I will seek out the dwarf spirit Harldain Ironbar and tell him of our need.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: Fetch the Gem from him to the Speculum and scale the dragon's back. Antarn's gate will open to you now.
keys.speaker: anorrwyn

keys.dialogue: I am Athan. And my breath is short. Hear me.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: The Cult of the Dragon has possession of Castle Cormanthor. They have raised a Pool of Radiance beneath it.

keys.dialogue: The Pool sucks life from New Phlan, Mulmaster, all the port cities. With it, the Cult can put all of Faerun under their thrall.

keys.dialogue: The Gauntlets of Moander. Elminster entrusted them to my band, but the Cult overpowered us and captured them. The Gauntlets can destroy the Pool. They must be regained.

keys.dialogue: Kya Mordrayn leads them, with her creature Pelendralaar. He is a dracolich. Vicious and immense in power. Their minions mark themselves with the dragon scars.

keys.dialogue: She has taken command of the Mythal. She controls it, and the Pool of Radiance, from a cavern deep beneath the castle.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Pelendralaar is the master of Mordrayn's army. It was he who drove the most powerful of Myth Drannor's monsters from the city Heights so Mordrayn could make her nest.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Devils. Alhoon. Phaerrim. They all scattered before him. Mordrayn bends the Mythal around him like a shield. While she controls it he is invulnerable.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Mordrayn's mages have been hard at work sealing even the most secret entrances from within. I saw only one flaw in their defense.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: The dragonkin have made an aerie of the throne room of the Coronal, which is open to the sky. If you can find a way to climb the battlements, you may be able to gain entrance there.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: I saw such a gem in the Pool cavern when they brought me before Mordrayn. When she stood beneath it, the Mythal's magic enveloped her and she was heedless of all else.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Healing?  Let me join you, and your healing spells will not be wasted! But if you cannot take me in your party, save your benisons. You will need them yourselves soon enough.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Yes! If you can heal me, then give me the chance! My friends in ashes... The weeks of agony... Through all this shame, only the hope of justice kept me sane. Vengeance! Let us strike at them together.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Athan joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If you can heal me, then give me the chance! You bear your slain, which is noble, but the deeds before you call for the might of the living.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Only give me the chance!  If any of your band would step aside, I will join you to rip vengeance from the Cult.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Shall we march on?
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Will you march on?
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Lay the dead to rest and I'll avenge them with you. Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find a way to strike at the Cult myself.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find my own path to strike at them.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Listen. All through the Cult's torture, they pried into my mind. Your deeds came to me through their fear of you. The destruction of the spawn pools, the freeing of the baelnorn...You have struck them to the core.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: You have the strength and the cunning to destroy them. Here, I am nothing. With you, I can be my comrades' avenging wrath. Let me join you. Let us rip this power from their grasp together.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Their games have left my body a ruin, but heal me and my fury will be a weapon in your hands. If any of your company will step aside, take me with you that we may tear vengeance from the Cult together.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: You have the strength and the cunning to destroy them. If you can heal me, let me join you on your quest. Bury your dead. Together we can be their avenging wrath.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find my own path to strike against the foe.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Go with the gods. I will find my way out to the Nightingale Court, and heal upon the blueglow moss. Healed, I will make my own way against the Cult.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Come, time is short. Let us be off. Our enemies and our destinies await us.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Enough, time is short. The Cult's hold on Faerun tightens by the hour. If you will have me, my strength is yours. Otherwise, my prayers go with you.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Then let us be off. Mordrayn and Pelendralaar await.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Athan joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Dracolich slayers! All of New Phlan thanks you for your deeds.  The Pool is dead, and for now, its evil is beaten back to hell.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Your deeds are sung up and down Faerun, my friends. They say the crack of Pelendralaar's bones was heard in the Far Reaches. All of New Phlan thanks you.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Dracolich slayers! All of New Phlan thanks you for your deeds.  The Pool is dead, and for now, its evil is beaten back to the dark place it came from.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Friends! My blade sings all the sweeter since we sent Mordrayn to Hell. But never so keenly as when I walked with you. Let us join company again, and cleanse the darkness from this place together.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Friends! My blade sings all the sweeter since we sent Mordrayn to meet her masters. But never so keenly as when I walked with you. Let us join company again, and cleanse the darkness from this place together.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Let me take up arms with you, if you would have another companion. I would be honored to walk by your side.
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: If you will have another companion, let me take up arms with you again. Together, we can overcome any foe!
keys.speaker: Athan

keys.dialogue: Freedom, at last. All is not lost.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Whoever you be, your valor has freed me from a terrible enemy. Let us be quick.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: We are safe here. For a time.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I am Miroden Silverblade. Protector. Baelnorn.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Centuries ago, I was an armathor of the realm. A confidant to the Coronal, and a mage of the high court.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: When Myth Drannor fell, I sacrificed all that was my life to bind myself to the Mythal. To tend it through the Sapphire of the Weave.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I have lain undisturbed in these lairs since, communing with the Mythal, knitting together its fraying weave as the years fell away.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Myth Drannor crumbled. All that I knew withered and died. Rivals, enemies, lovers, even the trees that held our towers to the sky. But I remained. Tending the Mythal. Protecting what was left of our majesty, our hope.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Until now. They came. The Cult of the Dragon. I had... grown weak in my solitude. I succumbed where I should have stood fast...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: But you have freed me. There is hope yet.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn survives?  I thought the years had claimed her spirit. She would come to me, not so many decades ago. She knew her visits lightened the burden of my time.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: We would speak of the old days, the golden days before the Weeping Wars. The fashions, and the intrigues, the arrogant and the beautiful...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: No. My time is done. Another must lift the burden now. I am Protector no more.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: My time is done. Another must lift the burden I have carried. The Mythal needs a new Protector.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Live? I have not lived since the Year of Doom!  No breath. No blood. What life could they take from me?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Pain is their delight. Bondage. And humiliation.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I cannot.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: They came to me. They wanted the Sapphire. They pried into my mind.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I had to prevent them...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: There is no Sapphire!
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Do you think I would let them have it?  Do you think I would betray centuries of trust?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I have destroyed it!  It is no more!
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I cannot... I cannot... Do you not see?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Forgive my outburst. I am... unsteady.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: I have destroyed that which I swore to protect.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: But the Mythal must be restored. A new Communicant must be found. A new Gem dedicated to the Weave. I have failed, but you can succeed.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The Gems were a gift from the dwarf lords.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: They mined the deepest reaches of the Far Hills to find them. A Ruby, a Sapphire, and an Emerald.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The Ruby was destroyed by the nycaloth, when the Armies of Darkness besieged the city. But if the House of Gems still stands, the Emerald survives. It was hidden for safe-keeping in the hoard of the Onaglym dwarves.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Ha!  Arrogant younglings!  Do you think you could withstand the Mythal's fire?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The incantation alone would wither your tongues. No, the Communicant must be versed in the ancient ways.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: It is a dire role, but Anorrweyn Evensong will rise to the task. She is as bound to the dying dream of this city as I am. Beg her in my name to be the Communicant of the Weave.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: There is a spirit, frail in appearance, iron strong in heart... Anorrweyn Evensong. She would come to me in years long past and ease my loneliness. If she survives, she would take up the task.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Do you question me?  What can you know of my regrets?  My hopes?  You who have walked on this earth mere moments to my centuries?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: How can you know what strength it takes to destroy that which you gave all to preserve?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: You are young. You cannot know. The centuries have exhausted me. But Myth Drannor has need of you.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: They are cunning. And she most cunning of all. Soft words... Promises...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: But it is done. And the cost is too high to repay.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The Cult grows stronger by the day. Their mistress whips them into a frenzy of destruction. She calls up drow from the Underdark to further her ends, and under Castle Cormanthor...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: They speak of a terrible Pool of Radiance that shreds the soul from flesh. It draws life from its hungry mouths throughout Faerun. Without the Mythal's strength, we cannot hope to stop them.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Claim the Gem. Find it a Communicant.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: My treasure I give you, to aid you in this cause. Weapons and armor the likes of which have not been worn by flesh since the empire's fall.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Take them, for my work in this world is finished. When you have restored the Mythal I will sleep at last....At long last.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The hoard of the Onaglym dwarves holds the last remaining Gem of the Weave. An Emerald which can be tuned to the Mythal.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: A new Communicant must take on the role I left behind. No mortal, but one as untouched by life as I.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. Where is the Sapphire of the Weave?
keys.speaker: Anorweyn
keys.desc: spoken, infinite sadness, she suspects the truth

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn - Do you remember the silvertrees in the courtyard of the Maerdrym?  How the Windsong Towers brushed against the stars?
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Speak plainly now, Miroden. Your lies have cost these children dearly.
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: She... came to me. She begged me to use the Gem, to raise a Pool of Radiance under Castle Cormanthor. She swore the Pool would bring life to Myth Drannor, to the Mythal.
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: Who?
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: Kya Mordrayn.  The glory you knew will come again, she said. The Windsong Towers will rise again...I believed her.  I taught her the incantation.
keys.speaker: Miroden
keys.desc: spoken, defeated, despairing, explaining, feebly, finally confessing

keys.dialogue: Oh Miroden...
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: The Pool brought life, yes,  stolen life. From Phlan, from everywhere...  I have destroyed our hopes.
keys.speaker: Miroden
keys.desc: spoken, doggedly continues his confession, grieved, somber

keys.dialogue: Hope lives. We have created a new Gem of the Weave.
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: Then I can be redeemed.  You must break her link with the Mythal. Find the Sapphire I gave her. Destroy it with this Word...
keys.speaker: Miroden

keys.dialogue: The Baelnorn's spell teaches you Ethgonil, the Word of Redemption.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Children, your place in this weave is clear: enter the Castle and find the Gem. Speak the Word, and when the Sapphire is destroyed, I will turn the Mythal's power against our enemies.
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: What we ask is not easy. Only your strength stands between us and despair. Mystra's blessing go with you, children, as do all our hopes.
keys.speaker: Anorweyn

keys.dialogue: The time I knew is past. It will not come again. But the future... That you can still save. Go!
keys.speaker: Miroden
keys.desc: spoken, almost to himself, to the party, intensely

keys.dialogue: The baelnorn opens a Gate to take you into Castle Cormanthor. Now the fate of Myth Drannor and all Faerun rests in your hands.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them what we learned.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Travellers, I have heard a rumor from Nottle, concerning the scarred mages.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We have been waiting patiently for you to return.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Beriand had been patient, maybe. But I have not! Come, come, tell us your news.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It has been quiet here, perhaps too quiet.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I tire of looking at these walls, and pacing this floor, and swinging my mace only at the air!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Travelers - while you were out, we have been gathering tales about places in the dungeons.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them what I saw.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Oh no, Faeril, if they want to hear it they must hear it from you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am glad you have come. The shelter has been under attack.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By orogs I think, and behind those ugly beasts, some dark hand urging them on.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I wished to slay them! But Beriand said nay, and eventually they moved on, to batter at other doors.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Friends - I must tell you - we have had a narrow escape.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By the Lady! Death was close to us.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But once again Faeril's great heart saved us.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Tell us, travelers, what has happened to you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And you bear dead. If only the staff Deathbane was back in Beriand's hand!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Friends - we are worried - Nottle seems to be missing.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Welcome, friends.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Greetings, travellers.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Orcs took it, and fled down the Main Halls. If Beriand had Deathbane back, once again he might raise the dead - if the Lady Mystra wills it.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: He thinks they belong to some kind of secret brotherhood. Some power is behind them - a deep and dark power indeed, he says.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Of course, that does not prevent him from trading with them, the scurrilous sandwag!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Not so harshly, Faeril! He gives them trinkets, yes, but he takes their secrets. Not every hero wields a sword, or wears shining armor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I do not know what to think! I was outside, near Nottle's wagon, and I saw... I saw... I do not know what I saw.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: She was a serpent, a great serpent, all shimmery in silver, gold and green. She smelled of flowers!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: She looked right at me - how her eyes flashed! But then she was gone, into a cleft in the rocks. I wonder who she was.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I opened the door to the outside - it was foolish, but all seemed quiet, and I wanted to smell the air and hear the wind in the trees.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: There were three of the lizardfolk there - who came fast for me. But Faeril stepped forward and fetched one of them such a blow...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Lady guided my hand, and strengthened my arm! I am sure of it!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It was enough for them, and they ran. Beware the lizardfolk, my friends, they too walk with a dark purpose these days, darker even than their usual love for human flesh to eat.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He did not say. But he had recently returned from the Deep Halls of the dungeon, and he said he had met some of the scarred mages there, and talked about trading.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: There is not much to tell about the small area we're in, a place we call Stillwater.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: This is a quiet area, overlooked by everyone except the orcs and undead. But there are very few places indeed that those swarming creatures overlook.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: As we told you, the Ring of Calling was on the Skeletal Arm, which the scarred mages took from Athan's band...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Nottle says there are many scarred mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the dungeons. One of those mages may have the Arm.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Ah yes, and the Ring is bound fast to the bones. Athan could not get the Ring off, no matter how hard he tried...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It will take great magic to release that Ring. Maybe you should go to the Hall of Wizards!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But how to get there? I believe all the normal routes were blocked up centuries ago. But maybe there is a magical path that remains - Athan thought so, and so does Nottle.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Then you must use it to escape the foul dungeons!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Yes, it is said that the Ring will open the Seal of Mythanthor, which is somewhere in the Halls of Light, I believe.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And through the Circle, you may at last reach the City Heights, and walk through the glorious ruin of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We have news for you! We have had a visitor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes. Some fast-talking friend of Nottle's.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I have news for you! I have had a visitor - a friend of Nottle's.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Travellers! You told us earlier that our adversary is the Cult of the Dragon....
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We have learned something about that fell company.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Tymora help me, if I could crawl back into my boulder, I would!
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: Travellers, I have heard some dire news - about the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Good news! There may be friends nearby who could aid you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I have felt the presence of the Silver Fire!
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: Have you seen Nottle? He seems to have disappeared!
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: I am concerned about Nottle. He has been gone a long time.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope you are able to help Anorrweyn Evensong - she is much beloved by Mystra.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It has been quiet here. I crave your news.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Quiet, yes. But I sense great magics in the air, spells laid with deadly skill.
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: Travelers - enemies have been battering at our door!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Until I cast a spell! And raised such a stinking cloud that many of them were overcome!
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: Friends - I must tell you - we have been hard pressed here.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I was sure our time had ended.
keys.speaker: Jarial

keys.dialogue: Welcome back, friends. You have a question?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Travelers! Mystra's servant greets you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: His name was Tudo, and I like him not at all!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: He is a rogue, I gather, of no small ability - and quite comfortable plying his trade, picking at the bones of old Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Cult is a very secretive organization, as you may know - usually divided by factions and infighting and backstabbing. This keeps them from ever strking out with their full power.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: A Pool of Radiance is a mighty thing, however! Faced with its power, all the Cult seems to have come to an agreement - to protect the Pool and nurture it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am afraid the Cult forces here are going to grow in strength very rapidly. Soon, no one will be able to stand against them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He did not say. But he had recently returned from the Deep Halls of the dungeon, and he said he had met some of the scarred mages there, and talked about trading.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I think they were orogs, but they seemed strange to me. They seemed dull, as if the souls had been ripped from them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Undead, dozens of them. Perhaps hundreds.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You seek a spirit? Myth Drannor is overrun with the ghostly remnants of the dead.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But since it is a dwarf lord you seek, I suggest you look in the great dwarven halls of old - the Halls of Light, and the Onaglym, the House of Gems.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Something is preventing the dwarf lord's spirit from communicating with you. Some evil thing, probably.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You must find it - and destroy it!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: A torc is a neckpiece, is it not? A rare one, certainly. Almost any creature might hold a treasure like that in its lair. I do not know any more about it than that.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I never saw anything like it on our travels.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Ah, the sorrow must be almost unbearable, to be dead yet still tied to your dusty bones. What you propose to do for the Lady Anorrweyn must be a great comfort to her.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By the Mother! How I wish I could assist you!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It will be a difficult task - her enemies will have taken the skull deep into the dark, hoping it will never again be found.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: If Anorrweyn's skull is in the Catacombs, you must find a way to get into that fell place.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Welcome back, travellers.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am glad to see you again.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Welcome, travellers. I have at least one new tale to tell you, thanks to Nottle.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By the Hand of Mystery, that was a narrow escape! I am much indebted to you for your aid against the Cult.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Ask - and I will tell you what I know.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am at your service.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: As I said, I heard this tale from Nottle, so you can judge for yourself what truth may be in it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He would not tell us how he came to learn such a tale!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: A great wizard has arrived in Myth Drannor - Azmark Duathel, from the Zulkir's Court in Thay. When I heard this, I was overjoyed - here is powerful help, indeed!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He is renowned for his bravery in opposing the Red Wizards.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But what Nottle has learned is this - Azmark Duathel is secretly a member of the Cult of the Dragon. He has come to help defend the Pool of Radiance.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: So what seemed to be our great hope has turned instead to great dismay.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: A creature like that would be far underground, and his holdings well-protected and not easy to find.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Surely you do not mean me? If so, I am honored, but must tell you, such a thing would be far beyond my power, or indeed that of almost any mortal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: What of the Lady Anorrweyn, beloved of Mystra? She could wield the power, if she would.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Surely the dwarf lord Harldain Ironbar is your only hope to obtain such a thing.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Then your long task is nearly done. Mystra be praised!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Greetings, my friends. I will tell you where evil lurks, if I may.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I welcome you once again, in the name of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You have been busy, or so I have heard.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: What part of the city are you interested in?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Perhaps I can help you find treasures to aid you against the Cult.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Greetings, and the blessing of Mystra upon you all.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Have you looked in our book? It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: That door is sealed with the Glyph of Mystra. Learn the Word, and the Glyph will unseal for you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You have learned the Word of Mystra! Now try to open the sealed door. It leads into the dungeons.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Well, here is a story. When we were wandering down in the Main Halls, Faeril did a very clever thing.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Clever! Do not think so! We were desperate.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: So we were. We had hidden ourselves from a large group of orcs, but they were on the verge of finding us...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...so I threw a stone at the head of Mol, their captain.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It struck his forehead with a sound I shall never forget! He was furious! And while the brute was whacking off heads with his great lead mace, we crept away, forgotten.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Nottle told us that evil mages have taken over the stairs that lead from the Main Halls to the Upper Halls. They have undead servants with them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I remember those stairs! They are far away to the east. You pass through endless halls, and the stairs are in a room at the end.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But take care, if what Nottle said is true. For he also said that the scarred ones scare him - and our friend Nottle does not scare easily.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Here is a tale - a strange one. When Faeril and I were lost in the dungeons, we came across a most helpful fellow.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Helpful, maybe! Strange, certainly.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: He was locked away in a cell, but we could hear his voice. He gave us advice on how to stay alive.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He hates orcs more than I do! If such a thing be possible.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Up far to the northeast his cell was. I remember him mentioning necklaces, amulets and torcs. He seemed to treasure them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Well, Nottle once told Faeril and me the tale of the Crazy Laughing Man.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Surely you did not believe him, Beriand! It is clearly a tall tale.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Somewhere in the Main Halls it was, that Nottle saw this man, trading jokes with a dark naga. Do you know of these nagas? Big serpent creatures, with powerful magics and a thirst for fresh blood.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: How a man could befriend one is beyond my ken. But Nottle swears the story is true.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Have you ever met an Ormyrr? Fearsome they look, and fearsome they are indeed in battle - but they are not evil creatures.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We came upon the tracks of a group of them, when we were down in the dungeons.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And heard them, too, from a distance. How they made the stone shake!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It is unusual for them to go underground. But we never talked with them, to learn what their story may be.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them the tale of the Ways of Mythanthor!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: This tale is quite old. It is said that Mythanthor himself created portals throughout the city, great gateways of magic that the people were glad to use.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He put upon these gateways his great Seal. In days of old, the Ways were open to all. But when the Wars came, many of the Ways were sealed, and have been sealed ever since.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Well, I heard a tale once about the sorceress they called Borea.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: She was from the deep North, and what power flowed in her veins! One drop of her blood could freeze a dozen men.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But woe for her! Her power was no match for the evils of this city. She came here in glory, and was never seen again.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: How I wish I could understand the speech of orcs! For often I heard them muttering as we crept by them in the dungeon halls...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...but all I know is, they are deathly afraid of their leader, some brute named Zud, and he dwells in a great hall somewhere in the northwest section of the Main Halls.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Now here is a thing. When we were in the dungeons, Faeril and I often crept by groups of orcs...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...I could not make out all they said, but they often talked of their leader, Zud, and of the great hall of orcs. It is in the northwestern part of the dungeons, I am almost sure.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Here is a thing that Athan told us - something he heard when he passed through the south part of the Main Halls of the Dungeons...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He could sense an unearthly creature moving beyond a wall. It jingled and jangled, he said, as if it carried hundreds of keys.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But he could not figure out how to reach the creature. He heard it go down stairs, and then it disappeared.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: One of Myth Drannor's treasures is the Wizard's Torc, a great neckpiece. Supposedly it was last worn by Ualair the Silent, the city's last Grand Mage.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Wizard's Torc was lost when Myth Drannor was overrun, and has never been seen again, although rumors about it abounded in the Elven Court.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Here is a strange tale! When I was down in the dungeon, I heard three orcs speaking in the common tongue. One of them mentioned the Talking Room.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It seemed to be high upstairs and off to the east. There was something in the Talking Room, something they wanted...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...but I did not learn what it was, because then I stepped out and killed them, alas.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Nottle has told us a tale, but I am not sure I am ready to believe it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He said he came across a magical Gate. And undead beings were coming through it! More and more of them!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: An abomination! Who would create such a thing?
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Nottle said the Gate was near the center of the Halls of Stone. And he swears that that it was not there a fortnight ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It is said that of all the great books that once graced the libraries of Myth Drannor, only the evil ones remain.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: These are dangerous books, but the guardians of Myth Drannor banded them with protective spells, so that none could look at them who were not powerful enough to stand against their evil.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But woe to us if these books should fall in the hands of evil! For if they somehow learn how to remove the protective spells, they could wield terrible instruments of evil against us.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Tell them of the waters I found!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Travelers, Faeril has saved my life many times, but never so skilfully as when she brought me the healing Waters of Life.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I was at the point of death - I could not heal myself. But she found a source of healing waters, somewhere in the Upper Halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Lady guided me, I am sure. And strengthened my arm when I battled with the lizardfolk guarding the well! And there were many of them.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: And with Mystra's help she defeated the lizardfolk there. Maybe the well can aid you as well, in your travels.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Now this is a slight tale. But when we were in the Dungeons, Faeril and I once camped near a fountain. The waters ran clear and sweet then, not foul as they are now.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And in the dark I awoke once to hear a woman singing a beautiful song. Very faint it was, echoing up out of the splashing fountain.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: That is all there is to my tale - except that the song lifted my heart, and gave me courage to go on.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Faeril, you have a good memory for places. Tell them what we learned about the Dungeons, as we wandered through.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We found four floors in the Dungeons. When you go through the Tumbledown Door, you enter the Main Halls. From there, there are two upper floors and one lower floor.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: There are many orcs in the Main Halls. In the Upper Halls, we found many undead, as well as bands of lizardfolk who seem to be searching for something.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: We spent as little time as possible in the Deep Halls. That was a nasty place! And we saw orogs there, who trooped about according to some dark plan.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: In the Dungeons, I remember that there were four floors - two in the Upper Halls, one floor called the Main Halls, and one called the Deep Halls.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Tumbledown Door leads you to the Main Halls. I remember there were many orcs there, when we traveled through.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Well now, as you know, Athan was looking for a way to get to the City Heights.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He told me a story about old Myth Drannor - that the city held magical devices that could whisk you from deepest pit to highest tower, all in a blink.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He was looking for one in particular - it moved within a circle of stones, and travelled from floor to floor. It went all the way up to a building on the City Heights.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He said he was following a trail of ice! But I did not understand what he meant.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Now, Nottle once told me a tale he heard from an orc.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The orc said that deep in the Dungeons, big spiderlike creatures hunt everything that moves, and take anything that glitters back to line their nests.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Many times the orcs had tried to win back these treasures, but each attempt met with disaster.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Surely you have heard already of the Mountain Fist? A great club, or perhaps it is a mace. The legends vary.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It is a mighty weapon, but not powerful enough to save its master from the chill touch of spirits. Legends say that he was turned to shadow, and went to stalk the deep underground, taking the Mountain Fist with him.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I do not know if this tale should be believed. It came to me in a dream.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: In my dream I held something in my hand - I dared not look at it, but it was bright - so bright my whole hand glowed red as blood.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Before me there was an abyss in the shape of a grave. I closed my eyes - yes, in my dreams I can still see - and opened my hand, letting the bright object fall into the depths.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: In only a moment a great wind sprung up, such that I was borne up, away from the abyss and into the bright sky, like a bird. Then I awoke.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When we were in the Deep Halls, we met a ghost of an elven woman - a cleric of Hanali Celanil. She did not speak, but it was clear she wished to show us something up in the Main Halls.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Alas! We could not go with her, and at last she disappeared.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But alas! We could not go with her, and at last she disappeared.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I do not know what she wanted, but it sorrowed her greatly. As you walk the Dungeons, watch for her.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I remember coming across several doors that were sealed with Glyphs, placed in the floor before them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes! The Glyph of Water, and another foul Glyph I did not recognize.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: These doors are sealed with strong magic. You cannot break into them - do not even try! For some of these Glyphs will destroy those who attempt to unwrite them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: To open these doors, learn the Word of Power that unseals the Glyph. Words can be found in books or on scrolls, or they can be learned from one who knows them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Once learned, merely approach the Glyph. The Word will speak itself, the Glyph will open, and you may pass in safety.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: An Ormyrr came by, and we talked. She said that drow had taken up residence in the Catacombs. Unusual for those creatures of darkness to dwell so close to the sunlight.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: According to the Ormyrr, the drow have been raiding everywhere in the underground, seizing treasures wherever they may find them. Myth Drannor's sacred relics, in drow hands - it is horrible to imagine.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Here is a strange thing. I heard a creature shuffling about outside our shelter. I believe it was an orog, and he was fishing in our stream!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: After much splashing and thrashing, I believe he caught something. He met with another of his kind, and they agreed to go back down to their master's chambers in the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I have never been to the Catacombs, so there is little I can tell you. In days of old, it was connected only to Castle Cormanthor, and so was considered the safest place in all of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Catacombs were a stronghold where the elves laid up the city stores, studied their most dangerous magics, and buried their dead. And the dwarves had tombs there also, for there was friendship between them in those days.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I have heard tell that people were imprisoned there as well - the most incorrigible enemies of the city, of course, but also ones guilty only of embarrassing the Court. But that is just rumor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am reminded of a tale I heard years ago, when I lived in the Elven Court.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The tale concerned an eternal guardian of Myth Drannor, an undead elf. This baelnorn had a lair deep, deep underground - or so the tale said.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When I was young, there was an elf-woman who lived near me, of the great House of Ammath. - Don't worry, this tale does pertain to you!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: She wore a magnificent cloak which was said to have come from Myth Drannor, from the Catacombs deep underneath the Castle.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When I touched it, I could tell it was once the cloak of Thyaast Ammath, a mage of great power - but who is said to have died by her own magic. And I tell you true, tragedy is woven into that cloak, as much as thread.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Of all the great buildings that existed on the City Heights of Myth Drannor, only three still exist: the House of Gems, the Speculum, and magnificent Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The House of Gems is east of the center of the Heights, above the eastern end of the Dungeons. The Speculum is south of the center, and the Castle is to the northwest.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: In its glory there were many more buildings - the Noble House of Ammath, and of course a beautiful shrine to the Lady of Mysteries. But they were utterly destroyed during the Fall, and now little if anything remains.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Travelers, did you know that in Myth Drannor, the buildings themselves can be ghosts? It is true - I have felt their presence myself.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The buildings slide back into being for a moment or an hour, then fade again into the whispering shadows of time.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I have heard the city's Shrine of Mystra is such a building, but that it has not been seen by mortals for well on a hundred years.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Ah, Castle Cormanthor, my thoughts often go there. It is a cesspool of evil! And many evil things prowl its once-stately halls.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But the castle itself seeks to resist these invaders, as best it can. Ancient defenses watch and wait - I can feel them. They wait for the small stone that will begin the cleansing landslide.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Alas, friends, I have some bad news about Castle Cormanthor. I have been casting cantrips of divination, and learned something dire indeed!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You know that Myth Drannor has a very old, very powerful protective spell cast over it - the Mythal. One of the fundamental powers of the Mythal is to block any who attempt to invade by magical portal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But the Mythal has been corrupted! And portals are being opened into the Castle from all over Faerun. The Cult's greatest wizards are coming here to pay homage to Kya Mordrayn and Pelendralaar.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am remembering that a traveler told me about the Great Pump of the House of Gems... Do you know the House of Gems, atop the City Heights, off to the east?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When this traveller was there, a year ago, it made a happy thump, like a heartbeat.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But when Faeril and I passed by a fortnight ago, the heartbeat could barely be heard! And many of the waters here have grown foul. I wonder what has happened there.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The House of Gems... that reminds me. An orog came and shouted a message through our door. I think the message was for you!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It said that the orogs wish to parley with you in the Round Tower of the House of Gems. They will wait for you there.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Surely you will not do it? It's clearly a trap!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It may be a trap, so if you go, go cautiously.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan told us that if we were ever in danger, to make our way as best we could to the central part of the City Heights.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He said there was a sanctuary there, a shrine to the god of travelers, Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I have heard a tale, but do not whether to believe it, because it came from an orc.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The beast was telling another of a sword that was to be left alone at all costs. For any who took the sword would be turned into a statue of stone, adorning the coldest of tombs.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: This sword was off in the ruins to the east, or so they seemed to say. I do not know what the truth of this tale may be.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When I was in the Elven Court, I heard tell of a mysterious place in Myth Drannor, the Garden they say was planted by Fiona Casilltenirra.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Have you heard tell of Fiona? She is that rare creature, an elf vampire, very beautiful and very dangerous.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I do not know much about her garden, if it even exists. But the shadows whisper that it should only be visited by those who welcome the darkest of bargains.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Oh, travelers, don't you wish we could see the old Myth Drannor, if only for a moment? It was indeed the most marvelous of places!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am blind, so maybe I am better able to imagine what it was like. Do you know that there was a place you could go, if you had lost something, and it would tell you where it was?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Column of the Whispering Wind is what they called it. Oh, what glorious ruins they are, that surround us on every side.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It is good you ask about such places, because it reminds me of a tale that I heard long ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It was said that in the Hall of Wizards, which some call the Speculum, there was a device of great magic, a wizard's Scrying Mirror.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: In the Mirror, one could see things far away. But this was no simple stargazing ball, oh no! For it could show images to satisfy the deepest desires of the heart.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan told Faeril and me that under no circumstances were we to venture into the ruins away to the southwest.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: There was great peril there, he said, for a sorcerer he hates dwells in the ruins, among the lizardfolk.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It seems incredible that a man should live among lizards, who relish human flesh above all things. But Athan said this was no ordinary man - indeed, not hardly a man anymore at all.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: What was the name he said? -Malgi Hi. You may want to stay clear of the ruins to the southwest, or risk falling victim to the greed and wrath of Malgi Hi.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I was talking with an Ormyrr - do not be amazed, for despite their ferocious appearance, some of the Ormyrr can be friends to our kind.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: This Ormyrr said that his friend Pujik had recently become King of the Ormyrr, and invited us to visit. He said they lived in the marshes away to the southeast.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I also learned that the Ormyrr are traders, and buy and sell goods from many creatures in the area. If you earn their trust, maybe they will trade with you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: In that area, as in all areas, you must take care. Stay away from creatures that are too strong for you right now.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Come back later, when you are stronger, and maybe have found allies to aid you. Then may the evil things fall to your sword and your spell.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: A word about resting in that area. When Faeril and I grew tired, we sought out safe places to rest -  rooms that were off the main paths, with doors we could shut against spying eyes.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And Faeril made quite sure there were no monsters dwelling nearby, before we settled down to sleep.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I will tell you something I noticed, as we made our way through the Dungeons... Maybe it will be useful to you.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The old areas were haunted with undead creatures, and shunned by living things.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: If you see obelisks or spires or worst yet, coffins - beware! That is an old area, where ghouls, shadows and wraiths might be found.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I will tell you something Faeril noticed, as we made our way through the Dungeons...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...the old areas were haunted with undead creatures, and shunned by living things.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Whenever she would see obelisks or spires or worst yet, coffins - we would watch out for ghouls, shadows and wraiths, and other things darker still.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I cannot tell you any more tales now. Talk to me later, after you have gone down into the Dungeons and seen for yourself.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I am afraid I have no more tales to tell you about the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: That is all the dungeon tales I know right now, relating to the Upper Halls.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We do not know any more tales about the Deep Halls of the dungeon.

keys.dialogue: You need not say it - my heart knows it already. Faeril is dead.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: So young, so full of life - it is truly a cruel and terrible world.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. May the blessings of Mystra go with you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Farewell. Return to me, if ever you need healing.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Journey with care, travellers.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Goodbye.

keys.dialogue: Walk in Mystra's sight, until we meet again.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. Return here if you would hear more tales, or if you require blessed healing from our Lady of Mystery.
