keys.dialogue: Stand ready, Beriand! They are not of Athan's band. And I do not like their look.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Calm, Faeril. Mystra has touched them, can you not feel it?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And they are hurt.
keys.speaker: Beriand
keys.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

keys.dialogue: And they are badly hurt by the foul ones.
keys.speaker: Beriand
keys.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

keys.dialogue: And they bear their dead, and loss weighs heavy upon them.
keys.speaker: Beriand
keys.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

keys.dialogue: Friend or foe, I will heal them.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Rest easy here, strangers, and tell us your news.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Bide a moment, and give an old blind elf a chance to speak.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan is dead, you tell us, and all his band. So Athan's quest becomes your quest - is this not so? To do as Elminster asked - to find out what is twisting the Mythal to evil.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We have already guessed some of your news. Athan and his band are dead.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: So Athan's quest becomes your quest. Is this not so? To do as Elminster asked - to find out what is twisting the Mythal to evil?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Mythal is an ancient spell of protection, laid upon this city long, long ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It is one of the greatest spells ever cast in Faerun, and is thus much beloved of Mystra, the Mother of All Magic.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We are humble followers of the Mother.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You will want to get to the Heights of the city, just as Athan did. He had the Ring of Calling - a gold ring, with a silver Starstone...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...stuck fast on the fingerbone of a skeleton's arm. He was searching for a Word of Power that would release the Ring...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...the Word of Oblivion. He heard tell of a place called the Room of Words. But he never found it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Nottle says there are many red-robed mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the Dungeons. One of them may have the Arm.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You would know it if you saw it. The Ring is magically bound onto the finger of its former owner.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan tried everything to get it off! How he cursed as he struggled! But none of them knew how to speak the Word of Oblivion.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: If you did not find the Ring on Athan's body, then his enemies must have taken it. And they too may be searching for the Room of Words.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: They are Words that command magic, in a language all but lost to mortals.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Magical words, which Mystra rejoices to hear.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Learn them to unleash Mystra's power - to wield a magical object or unseal a glyph-held door.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Right now the way is sealed.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We were in the dungeons below, when orcs came upon us. They seized Beriand's mighty staff, Deathbane...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...so we fled up and out, and Beriand sealed the door behind us with the Glyph of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You can learn the Word of Power that will unseal the way to the Room of Words. I wrote it here in our book.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Your way, travelers, is clear.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: If you are indeed to shoulder Athan's burden, you must take up where he left off - seek the Ring of Calling, and the Word of Oblivion that releases it. They will unseal the way to the City Heights.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: To begin that quest, look in our book. It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Beware of orcs. They are many, and they are greedy! They seized Beriand's staff, Deathbane, right out of his hands!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But beware! They who killed Athan have also corrupted the Mythal, this city's ancient and beautiful spell...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...so there will be much evil afoot, and the city itself may seem hostile.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Heed what Athan said! Search for the Room of Words.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: East of here you will find the Tumbledown Door, which we sealed with the Glyph of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Speak the Word of Power that is written in our book, and the door will open for you.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Mystra guide you. To hear our tales, or to get healing, come talk to me again.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You may rest here without fear. To hear our tales, or to get healing, come talk to me again.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Little good will its healing do them. It will not raise up their kind!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Take heed! Nottle can be friendly, but he is not your friend!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Sly scavenger! Loyal only to himself and his purse.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Still, we are thankful he sent you to us.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We will pay for it somehow, mark my words!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: So Athan and his companions are dead. What we feared has come to be. Greatly we rue their passing.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He was a great warrior! How he sent the orcs a-flying!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Athan told us the great Mythal of Myth Drannor was corrupt, and that he sought to make it whole. What will become of his quest, now that he is no more?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We can shed some light on that story. Athan told us his band would try to open a Gate back to Phlan.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He knew evil was rising here, but he did not know what it was. Or if he knew, he did not say.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: A Pool of Radiance... you think there is one here, in Myth Drannor? This city has a Mythal, a great protective spell. It would prevent such a thing...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...unless the Mythal is corrupt! Just as Athan told us!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Woe to Mystra and her servants, then! And a double curse upon us, now that Athan is dead! For he swore to restore the Mythal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: If you seek a Pool of Radiance, his quest seems now to fall upon you. For one terrible hand seems to be at work here - bringing the Mythal low in order to raise the Pool.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Woe to Mystra and her servants, then! And a double curse upon us! For Nottle told us Athan is dead, and Athan was sworn to restore the Mythal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He did not know his enemy. 'Scarred mages,' he called them, and spat.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But it seems clear they are the evil ones who have bent the Mythal to their own ends. Or in league with them, at least.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Why else would they come howling after Athan?
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Mystra! Why, she is the goddess of magic, the lady of possibilities. Do you not know of her? She tends the Weave, which all mortals use to cast spells.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Gently, Faeril. Many honor the Mother of Magic, even if they know her not by name.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Both Faeril and I are humble servants of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan vowed to destroy whatever was corrupting the Mythal. To do that, he knew he must reach the City Heights. He had the Ring of Calling...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...a gold ring with a silver Starstone, stuck fast on the fingerbone of a skeleton's arm. He needed the Word of Power that releases the Ring...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...the Word of Oblivion. He heard tell of a place called the Room of Words. But he never found it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Nottle says there are many red-robed mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the Dungeons. One of them may have the Arm.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I sealed the way myself. When we came up from the dungeons, orcs were after us, so I laid the Glyph of Mystra upon the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You may pass through that door, if you learn the Word of Mystra. It is written here in our book.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The Word of Mystra is written in our book.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Once you learn the Word of Mystra, you can enter the dungeons. With the Word, you can pass the Glyph of Mystra that seals the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Blame the orcs! For your dead would be back with us already, if the cursed orc rabble hadn't seized Beriand's staff.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Ah, it is true, Mystra willing. I named my staff Morathil - that is, Deathbane. I cut it myself, guided by Mystra's hand. And I put much of my healing power into it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I went to take it back, but alas! Too many orcs infest the dungeons for one alone...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...although that did not stop you from trying, valiant Faeril, and nearly perishing in the attempt!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan believed he could reach the Room of Words from the dungeons below. He looked in our book, and learned the Word of Mystra to unseal the way...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But he did not live to use it. If you would take up after him, you must begin with the Word.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Mystra sent me a vision! I saw her wrapped in magic amid the ruin of Myth Drannor. So I joined a band of travelers bound for this city.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And I came along, to protect my good master from harm.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But our group came to a bad end. We fled underground, where we were hunted by drow. We escaped them, only to be hounded by orcs. They forced us up from the dungeons...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...where we met Nottle, generous Nottle, who sold us the password to this ancient elven shelter.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Considering our need, the price was not unreasonable - almost every coin and gem we had.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Mythal is an ancient spell of protection, laid upon this city long, long ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Some say it is the greatest spell ever cast by mortals!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Under its powerful weave, Myth Drannor became a city unmatched in its grace and grandeur.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Legends tell of a golden city, beloved of elves, full of peace and song. How far has it fallen!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: As long as the Mythal remains, hope remains - hope that one day, Myth Drannor will rise from ruin and once again be the most sacred of cities.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But if the Mythal should be turned - it is a horrible thought, all that ancient power set to evil.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: There is little to tell. They were wounded - I healed them as best I could. I lost my staff, you see, to orcs. Without Deathbane, my healing power is small.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Athan told us Elminster sent him here, because some ill had struck the great Mythal of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: They did not stay long. Athan did not want to bring doom upon us. The mage with him said she would try to open a Gate back to Phlan.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By the Goddess! The Weave was like silk in her hands!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Athan was determined to return to the City Heights. In our book, he read the Word of Mystra that unseals the Tumbledown Door. But he never used it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Of course. Exhaustion is written in your voice. Forgive us for keeping you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Rest here, and rest well! Then look in our book for the Word of Mystra, and use the Word to pass through the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Beriand...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I know, I know - I am rattling on and on. Forgive me for keeping you. Now you must be about your quest.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Beware of orcs. They are many, and they are greedy! They seized Beriand's staff, Deathbane, right out of his hands!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: To begin that quest, look in our book. It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But beware! They who killed Athan have also corrupted the Mythal, this city's ancient and beautiful spell...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...so there will be much evil afoot, and the city itself may seem hostile.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Heed what Athan said! Search for the Room of Words.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: May Mystra guide you. To hear our tales, or to get healing, talk to me again at any time.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And talk to us again, anytime, to hear our tales and tell us your progress.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...so we fled up and out, and Beriand sealed the door behind us with the Glyph of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Athan told us Elminster sent him here, because some ill had struck the great Mythal of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You give the staff Deathbane back to Beriand, its rightful owner.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Why, what is this? I know it at once. Look, Faeril! It is Deathbane. They have brought my staff back to my hand.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes! I saw them bring it forth, and how my heart leapt!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Haha! The Lady is smiling, Faeril, at last! By the Weave, it is good to feel her warmth again.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: If you feel pain, or if one among you hears the icy whisper of death, come to me! With Deathbane in my hand and Mystra's favor in my heart, there is little I cannot heal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Behold! With Deathbane in my hand, even for those who have died, hope blazes anew!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Oho! I bet you made them pay for their greed.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The orcs have grown greatly in numbers, it seems, and in strength. Thank the Goddess you opposed them, and not Faeril alone!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: One may only do so much against so many, even one as valiant as she.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: For us, no. You have already helped us beyond all accounting. Now you must think to your own quest.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your pursuit of the Pool of Radiance...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your pursuit of the Ring of Calling...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your path to reach the city Heights...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your search for the Baelnorn...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your quest to return Anorrweyn Evensong her skull...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yet even so, I do not regret it!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Nor I! For the Lady Mystra is glad, and that is good for all of us.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Well... I had not expected this. There is nothing of value I have, nothing I can give you. Unless...
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: ...I can offer you the service of my protector and friend, Faeril, if she would consent to it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I will not! Consent to serve such greed? Never!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Then I am afraid I have no way to pay for the return of my staff, except to use it in your benefit when I may.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And that should suffice, and more than suffice, even if you be more grasping than Nottle!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Speak no more of it. We are all caught up in Mystery, and do what we can, not to solve it, but to help others appreciate its beauty.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But I talk too much, as usual.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You need rest - and you are welcome to rest here, in our haven.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You must be on your way. May Mystra walk with you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. If you need rest - you are welcome to rest here, in our haven.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You must be on your way. May Mystra walk with you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Stay a moment! Beriand craves your news, and so do I.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: So, travelers, what news?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes! Tell us what you've seen.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I am wondering - have you seen or heard anything of the Goddess of the Weave, Mystra?
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: We are waiting for a sign from our Lady.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Travelers! Mystra has sent us a sign!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Tell us, travelers, tell us what you've seen.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes - I have had a vision. There were ruins, and a voice crying the name of our Lady... one who is lost in the past, who believes that all of the followers of Mystra are gone.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: You must take a token to her!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Better than that - can you not take me with you? For I am a Servant of Mystery, and more proof than any token that the Lady of Spells has not been forgotten!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Ugh - to understand what gargoyles say - that is magic I have no use for!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Still, the Elves of Harrowdale had a saying, 'To understand an enemy is to defeat him.'
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Ah, a follower of Shaundakul, the Wind Rider! That was a fortuitous meeting for you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: For you - and for the naga you name Odelinde. But not for the orcs, haha!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The Wind Rider is a powerful ally - no god is as keen to restore Myth Drannor. For it was here that his worshippers came, and when the city fell, so did they.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: So you toppled the great Malgi Hi! Ah, that is quite a feat, and no mistake. Perhaps Faeril could make a song of it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Bard of Kara-Tur, maybe, but not me!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I know I should not envy you - all that blood, and fear, and pain - and yet, to smite down such evil! Glorious!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Nottle told us of such a horrible place, but we did not believe him.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I would be careful about going there too often, lest its thirst become yours.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: This is very strange! Dwarves do not often become ghosts. It is not in their nature.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: They loathe spirits, that is commonly known.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Still, you did well to free him. Even ghosts have their uses.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: I had forgotten about the gargoyles! Even now, their cruelty fills me with rage.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It is hard not to envy the Old Ones - while we struggle against evil, she worries only about the music of splashing water.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: That is the hand of the Cult at work, or I am a fool. And we will see more of that - more of our friends will become our enemies - as their power grows stronger.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: A strange circumstance. I wonder who he is, and how he came to be caught in such a cold and empty trap.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: When he is released, what stories he may tell!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: We encountered such a naga, deep in the dungeons. We barely escaped with our lives!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: It spared us - I do not know why. They are deep creatures, I have heard, and do things willfully and for reasons none can fathom. Their gods are mysterious gods.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Preybelish? I have not heard that name.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: But if he has been dwelling in the dungeons long, he is probably not your friend!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Perhaps you should bring him a gift of some kind. Once he knows you mean him no harm, he may open the door.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I've heard it said that the nagas came here as servants to far more evil powers. That must have been a dark time indeed!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You were wise not to redeem him! Thieves make me nervous.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Ah, present company excepted, of course!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Nervous! I have never known you to be nervous, Faeril, and you've had better cause than thieves.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Thieves are not dear to the Mother of Magic, but all creatures have their place in the Weave. You should consider well whether this thief Tudo may be of use to you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Dear Faeril - do not worry - see, they take no offense.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Thieves are not dear to the Mother of Magic, but all creatures have their place in the Weave. You should consider well whether another thief will aid you in your cause.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: It sounds like the drow have arrived in force.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: They were only scattered bands when we were down there.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: They are fierce, and cunning, and relentless! Expect no quarter from them.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The Mythal! Perhaps the greatest spell ever cast by mortals. Under the protection of its powerful weave, Myth Drannor became a city unmatched in its grace and grandeur.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Legends tell of a golden city, beloved of elves, full of peace and song. How far has it fallen!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: As long as the Mythal remains, hope remains - hope that one day, Myth Drannor will rise from ruin and once again be the most sacred of cities.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: The Mythal - the Mythal is fading. Tell them, Faeril.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Yes. Have you seen the blueglow moss? There are patches of it here and there in the city.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: In the old days it glowed strong - and healed those who touched it, because the power of the Mythal was behind it.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But when we arrived the moss hardly glows at all. So...
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: ...so we think some ill has overtaken the Mythal.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And we believe the Mother of Magic wants it restored.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But that - that was in my vision, the one that brought me to Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: I dreamed that such a cry wafted up from the ruins, and Mystra herself appeared, wrapped in magic, and walking lightly under crumbled archway and over toppled stone, to answer it.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Can you find your way back to that place? And take with you a token of Mystra? For someone must answer that call!
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Better than that - can you not take me with you? For I am a Servant of Mystery, and more proof than any token that the Lady of Spells has not been forgotten!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: One thing only I ask. Someone should stay here with Beriand, to guard him, else I will not go.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: That is not necessary -
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: - but it is wise. I will leave you, Beriand, if Mystra wills, but I will not leave you alone!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: You must decide who will stay behind. I will join you when that is settled.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: But first, I give you the token - our Lady's Medallion. Give it to the one who cries out for Mystra, if I do not make the journey with you.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: First, I give you the token - our Lady's Medallion. Give it to the one who cries out for Mystra, if I do not survive the journey.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Faeril joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The vision came to me some weeks ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: As I told you, I saw Mystra walking through the ruins. There was magic streaming all around her - the air was alive with possibility.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Ahead was a place where her shrine once stood. And a woman's voice cried out, despairing - 'where are the followers of Mystra?'
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: And our Lady grieved, or so it seemed to me. She bowed her head and look! There were bones on the ground, all of them missing their heads; but a path went through them and into the ruin of the shrine.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: That is all. Somehow I knew that the ruins were Myth Drannor - I recognized them, although I have never been here and am blind besides.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: So he decided to come here, and I could not convince him otherwise.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Why, I am a cleric of Mystra, with some small skill in healing. But I also am a fighter who wields staff, mace and maul, and such hurtful spells as the Lady has taught me.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: And I may add that she has the heart of a lion, she is shrewd in the melee, and a glad soul and a healing hand at the campfire. Full of song is my Faeril, and I will miss her, if she goes with you.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Not much has happened. Nottle came by, and asked about you, but that was some time ago.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: He wondered if you were rich with plunder. I told him no!
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: He sold us a medallion of Mystra. He said that he bought it from a lizard-man who had found it 'at the foot of a cloud-house.'
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: By which he meant 'ghost building.' Nottle says Myth Drannor has many.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: The medallion is a relic of the old years, when Myth Drannor was a dream city and many, many followers of Mystra dwelt here.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? Orcs stole it from us - they may still have it.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? His heart sinks without it, and even I cannot cheer him up.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? His healing gift would be great again if he could get it back.
keys.speaker: Faeril

keys.dialogue: Alas, without my staff Deathbane, I cannot raise your dead.

keys.dialogue: I feel the Lady was with us.

keys.dialogue: We who follow the Lady Mystra honor you for this great deed.

keys.dialogue: Travelers! I have heard that Kya Mordrayn has fallen by your hand, and the Pool of Radiance is no more.

keys.dialogue: All who follow the Lady Mystra honor you for this great deed.
keys.speaker: Beriand

keys.dialogue: Travelers! We welcome you most warmly.

keys.dialogue: Beriand has seen it all! The death of Kya Mordrayn, the great fall of Pelendralaar, the destruction of the Pool. Oh! it was glorious!

keys.dialogue: The Lady blessed me with a vision. We who follow Mystra honor you for this great deed.

keys.dialogue: How I wish I could be venturing with you, a humble warrior in the hushed service of the Lady.

keys.dialogue: But we should not detain you. Rest here, if you are tired, for here no darkness will enter.

keys.dialogue: Kellan is dead. Much though I miss my sister-in-arms, I also rejoice - for she died as she would have liked, in brave company, smashing a foe who deserved to be brought low.

keys.dialogue: Rest easy here, under our protection. And if ever you seek a comrade, consider me. You were Kellan's companions, and I would be honored to call you my own.

keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now, let me announce you... Caalenfaire my sweet, the Veiled Ones are here again.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Aaaaah! Aaaah! It is coming apart, it is slipping away! What on Faerun is happening?
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Master, it is the Veiled Ones. They are here, and they spoke to you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: It is torn, Volun, will we ever be able to mend it? -Bid them begone, Volun! Before the rest of their fortunes end up in tatters!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: You had best leave, and come back to us later.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Eeeeeeek! By the grace of Tymora!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What - what is it, Volun? I see nothing!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Pardon, master, and do not fear. I saw a shadow - I thought - I thought it was the Emissary of the Lady Shar! But now I see it is only the Veiled Ones.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: They must learn not to creep up upon us that way! So for now, Veiled Ones, begone!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: What? What is that? The thread, Volun! I have lost it. -No, no, here it is.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Again the Veiled Ones have interrupted us, my master. Their need must be very great.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Aaaiiieee! The thread! The thread, Volun! It is broken.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: What? Who is there? Oh, I see. Master, it is the Veiled Ones.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What? What is it? Ah, yes. Master, the Veiled Ones stand before you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Eh? -Master, it is the Veiled Ones. They seek another audience with you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire - they are here again.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What is that? Who is here?
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Calm yourself, my love. It is only the Veiled Ones, come to us once again.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Don't tell me - not again?
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Yes, master, the Veiled Ones have returned.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Hold, master! Hold your spellweaving! For the Veiled Ones stand before us once more.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: You wait only a few minutes. Then Caalenfaire speaks up.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But wait, Volun. Something is amiss... The bowl is clouding...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Let me look... Ah, my dear, I see the problem.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Have I poured too much krakatoac into it?
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: No, no my love, it is the Veiled Ones. They are here again.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: You cannot wait any longer.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You wait. They do not acknowledge you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your feet hurt. They are still intently studying the scrying bowl.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your arms are getting heavy. They do not acknowledge your presence.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You scuff the ground with your toe. They do not look up.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You clear your throat, loudly, several times. There is no reaction.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You say 'Pardon, good sir' about twoscore times. Nothing happens.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You announce your name in a loud and important tone. They do not acknowledge your presence.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You tug gently at Caalenfaire's sleeve. He does not respond.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You wave a hand inches from the diviner's face. His eyelids do not even flicker.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your tired bodies are beginning to exude an unpleasant odor. But Caalenfaire and Volun do not seem to notice it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Faeril emphatically scuffs the ground with her toe. They do not look up.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Jarial clears his throat, loudly, several times. There is no reaction.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Emmeric says 'Pardon, lady, and good sir' about twoscore times, until his throat is hoarse. Nothing happens.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Eadred announces his name in a loud and important tone. They do not acknowledge him at all.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Bronwyn tugs gently at Caalenfaire's ghostly sleeve - or tries to. He does not respond.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Kellan waves her weapon inches from the diviner's face. His eyelids do not even flicker.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your dead are beginning to exude an unpleasant odor. But Caalenfaire and Volun do not seem to notice it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Wait, Master. I sense a shadow... across our path... Ah. Of course. The Veiled Ones have returned.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: The vision is fading, Volun. Maybe more efreet ash will - why, what is it? There is concern writ large upon your face, Volun!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Because I see what you cannot, Caalenfaire my love. The talibund warriors are here again.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ah, there you are. -Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones have come, just as you thought they would.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ah, there you are. Have you been waiting long? -Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones are here for you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ah, here they are, Caalenfaire - the Veiled Ones. We did not expect you so soon.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Who is that? It's getting hard to - ah, yes. Dearheart, the Veiled Ones are here.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What, Volun! Hand of Beshaba, what is wrong with them?
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: The Dungeons! They must get out of the Dungeons! Send them away, send them away at once.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: You heard the Master! You best be on your way.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Once you leave the Dungeons, then we can tell you about the amazing visions we are seeing.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Never mind them, Volun. Look, look here at the self-anointed Priestess of Mystra, Anorrweyn Evensong.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: She was so imperious in court - do you remember? So full of advice for everyone. But look - look at her now, Volun.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Ah, but Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones are waiting -
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Let them wait. See, she wails for her followers - she believes them all dead - not knowing that two of them are right nearby, right here in the city! Too bad the blind healer will never live to meet her.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Ahhh. Good. Ask them, Volun. Ask them about Plinshree.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Good. Tell them what I told you - that they should stay away from the one called Malgi Hi.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: You heard my master! We have seen the lizardfolk dining merrily on one of his victims.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What? Unpredictability settles over them, Volun. Soon we may not be able to see the talibund ones at all.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Well, what brings them here this time? Tell me what they say, if you can still hear it!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Oh, but my love, look in the bowl, look what is happening in the bowl!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: We have said enough to them, maybe more than we should.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now it is time for them to go on, to continue on their path. -Farewell, Veiled Travelers. May your path be ever your own.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: O Veiled Ones, did you have another question for my master? Ask wisely, now - his time is precious.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, they do not know of the naiad!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, they returned the waterbells to the naiad!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, they wish to know who Malgi Hi is.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, they said they would avoid the evil sorcerer.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, they refuse to take your advice!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, woe to you! They have already met Malgi Hi - and killed him!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones inquire about the goddess Shar.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones inquire about Anorrweyn Evensong!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones want to know more about the dwarf-lord, Harldain Ironbar.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: My love, the Veiled Ones are asking about the Golden Serpent, the Shrinekeeper of Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: There is a shocked silence. Then Volun whispers to Caalenfaire something you cannot hear.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Volun and I knew her, of course, back in the days before Myth Drannor fell. I did not have a high regard for her...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: She was good at predicting the future, very good, but not clever enough to avoid it.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: She thought her goddess would save her. And maybe the Lady will. But the ways of Mystra are notoriously inscrutable.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Now she languishes in the ruins of her shrine, too defeated even to call out for her followers, believing them all dead. A sorry end, but not entirely undeserved.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: At least her spirit is grounded in the present once again. The Veiled Ones have seen to that.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: No, my love, that was the future you saw, not the present.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Oh, I cannot be bothered right now with that - you tell them, Volun.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Harldain Ironbar was lord of the dwarves during the glory days of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Under his direction, the city's dwarves built some great marvels - an ingenious system of 'liquid fire' for illumination, waterworks that fed refreshing fountains and pools - and of course the Orrery that powered the Spinning Spires for transportation.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now, these wonders lie in ruins or have been turned to evil, and his spirit haunts the House of Gems, hoping for the day when the corruption ends.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: We knew that day would never come for him - until you came. And set  our hoard of knowledge aflame, and reduced all our old predictions to ashes!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now I think that his ghost will see a turn in the tide of corruption, and his ghost will find peace at last in the halls of his fathers. But that is not a soothsaying - just a guess.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Odelinde? She is fiercer by far than her mother, and even her mother's mother, all of whom were guardians of the Wind Rider's shrine.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: And her daughter will be fiercer still - as great as the Shrinekeepers of old...
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Yes! It was exciting to see that new future emerge in the scrying bowl.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Assuming she has a daughter - that outcome is in doubt, now that orcs are in her Shrine.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: You ask for too much. What I know was well-protected and dearly bought.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: But nevertheless I will tell you the tale - what I know of it, anyway.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Of Kya Mordrayn herself I know very little. Honored as a hero, she was secretly rising quickly in stature within the Cult of the Dragon. When Pelendralaar the Dragon disappeared, she was thought to have helped defeat him...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: ...but in reality she was the archmage who persuaded him to transform into a dracolich. And since that day they have been as one.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: The utter destruction of Mocthrinul, and the great tower he resided in, was done by them - but blamed on others; so was the ransack of the Far Holes. And of course they have been ruthless in seizing this city for their own, for purposes that are hidden even from me.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: There is not much to tell. Back in the glory days of Myth Drannor, we were rivals, enemies even, in those days when power at court was everything.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire pursued his art without mercy, and I did not - so eventually he defeated me, and I became a skull upon his writing desk.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And when Myth Drannor fell, Caalenfaire died and became a ghost, just as he had foreseen. And by my choice I became his familiar, and only companion.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And so the centuries have passed. He still pursues his art without mercy, as you have seen, but it has come to pass that we love each other, an outcome that despite our arts neither of us had foreseen.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master! They have spoken with the naiad!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: What is this? Plinshree usually has no patience for mortals - and little regard for them, either.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: She looks on them the way we looked upon mayflies, once upon a time. Her thoughts and concerns are like the water she swims in, ever flowing and ever changing.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Have you found the Glyphs of Water? Have you learned the Splashing Word? Once we saw great treasures come to one who unlocked their secret...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: ...but that is a future which now will not come to pass, unless you fulfill it.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ah. Of course. That is in the future - if it exists at all.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Curse them, Volun! By the forelock of Beshaba, they have astounded me yet again.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: This is one more thing I had not foreseen - and it changes everything. Now the phaerrim will have their hands full - now the alhoon may stay away, in the dark holes to which they fled...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Now you will have to recast all your soothsaying incantations, and recalculate all the possibilities. And I know how much you HATE doing that, Caalenfaire my love.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ah - you have felt the touch of the Lady of Loss, have you? No mortal is ever free from her embrace...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: ...when a beloved companion dies, Shar is there. Pain or forgetfulness is what she offers you, and either choice suits her dark whims very well.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Do not tell them! It is better if they do not know.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: That is wise. He is human, but he abhors humankind, for reasons I will not divulge. For decades he has gathered dark spells from creatures that shun the light of day...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: ...and now he moves like the breath of pestilence through villages and towns.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: His will to destroy is ironwrought, and now his form echoes it. A mask of iron hides a face from which all kinship and mercy have fled.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Then they are fools, because Malgi Hi eats up his enemies as an elf-child savors dreamberries. The lizardfolk obey him absolutely, and his spells can turn his fanatic troops into warriors with skins of stone.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: But I waste my breath, laying wisdom before the talibund. You will go your own way, come what may. I wash my hands of it.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Then you were right, curse you, Volun! The human the lizardfolk were eating...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: ...that was Malgi Hi himself, just as I told you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: That is enough, Volun! We have given them guidance. Now they must go.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, you must depart. My master is eager to return to his spellweaving.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: That is all we will say for now.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Achh! Now my bowl is all cloudy. Send them away, Volun, send the Veiled Ones away!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: What it all means, I do not know. But that is all we can tell you right now.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Images twist and writhe deep in the sloshing fluid of the conjuring bowl. But you cannot make any sense of them at all.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Images flicker in the scrying bowl. You glimpse howling undead mobbing a hapless orog, predatory lizardfolk running through the darkness - and all the while, a Cult Mage stands next to an evil-looking Gate, laughing hysterically.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Images flicker in the scrying bowl. You glimpse predatory lizardfolk running through the darkness, a troop of orogs herding some howling undead down a corridor - under the watchful eyes of two Cult Mages.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Images dance in the scrying bowl, and the sound of footsteps wells up from its oily surface. You see Beriand offering up a simple prayer to Mystra, while Faeril paces impatiently in front of him, swinging her weapon.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The bowl seems to be entirely dark.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But then you dimly see a figure - she is swimming - you catch your breath - she is indescribably beautiful.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But then Volun screams at you, and you jump back!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Fools! Imbeciles! That vision of loveliness you see is the naiad Plinshree. And one good look at her would take your breath away forever.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: You only catch a glimpse - of reptilian jaws snapping rapturously at animal meat. Then the vision flickers away.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You see vague shapes moving in the bowl's depths - a gargoyle? A dragon? You hear something - a spell being cast? Everything seems dim and distorted.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire and Volun return their attention to the scrying bowl.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire and Volun attend once again to the scrying bowl.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Oh yes. And next time, do not stand there so quietly! Let us know as soon as you approach.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: With that, the diviners turn their attention once again to the shifting scenes in the scrying bowl.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Well, Volun, it has happened, just as I feared.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: The Veiled Ones - they have disappeared entirely?
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Yes. And I fear it may be forever.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Veiled Ones - if you can hear me - my master says you must walk your own way. Unless the pall on this city is lifted, we can help you no longer.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Volun takes something away from you - it is the Backwards Key!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You for is this, Ones Veiled, here. Master, yes.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now Caalenfaire seems to answer her. He also is talking backwards.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Volun, them to it give, ahead, go! Wizards of House the into, here leads that door magical the unlocks it.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: There. Now that the Backwards Ritual is done, Veiled Ones, is there something else you wish to ask my master about?
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Wait politely
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Wait politely some more
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Sneak a peek into the bowl
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: The images in the bowl are dazzling and incoherent. You cannot even begin to understand them.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Leave them alone
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Tell them about meeting Plinshree
keys.speaker: Protagonist

name: caaq1010
selections: Ask them about the Song of Faerun
Tell them you seek the Ring of Calling
Tell them you seek the Word of Oblivion
Ask them what 'talibund' means
Ask them what the Path is
Ask how you return to the Path
Ask them what your future holds
Ask them to finish their wise counsel
Bid them goodbye

keys.dialogue: And now orc-arrows pierce the Golden Serpent.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Do not disturb the Master. Here is the wise counsel you seek. Your coming has been foreseen.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Seek out Odelinde, the golden serpent. Seek out the spirit of the Dwarf Lord, Harldain Ironbar. You will find them beyond the Circle of Mythan -But hold a moment!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: You do not have the Ring of Calling!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: You already have the Ring of Calling!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And there is a man among you, one of Athan's companions!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And that sorcerer, Jarial, has joined you!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And you haven't yet looked into the Scrying Mirror!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master! Despair and woe! Your prediction has gone awry.
keys.speaker: Volun
keys.desc: spoken, calling to her master, excited and intrigued

keys.dialogue: What? What? Hand of Beshaba, where are they? I cannot see them. I cannot hear them. The fools!
keys.speaker: caalenfa
keys.desc: spoken, coming briefly out of his trance, irritated

keys.dialogue: They are talibund, I tell you! They have left the Path.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Volun! They know all they should. Give them guidance, and let them go.
keys.speaker: caalenfa
keys.desc: This line is no longer spoken, brisk

keys.dialogue: Master! They seek the Ring of Calling. Is that not according to the Path?
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: I will look into the bowl.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: I am looking... It is unclear. They are Veiled Ones now, and their shadow darkens anything they might touch or anyplace they might go.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: There are many possibilities... the Tulun Wall... the Corridor of Salg... but... first they should go to the House of Gems, in the Room of Words. Yes. But look!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire's spell teaches you Rhesheshannen, the Word of Oblivion.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: I have taught them the Word of Oblivion, so that when they find the Ring, its once-proud bones will release it.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: The Master knows much that is hidden. Remember that.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, it is time for you to go.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, it is time for you to go. Here is the Ring of Calling.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Master! They have the Ring of Calling. But behold! Its owner clings to it, even after death. They seek the Word of Oblivion.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Yes, Volun. I will speak the Word of Oblivion, and give these bones peace.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: There - I have freed the Ring. Bring it before the Seal of Mythanthor, to open up the way to the City Heights.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Return? You cannot. Do not even try.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: We will peer ahead as far as we can, and give you such help as we can.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: But if Caalenfaire could see you, maybe others could also. People of power. Maybe it is better for you to walk alone in the dark...
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And yet - not quite alone, Volun. For there is a hand over them... whose hand, and for good or ill, I cannot tell.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones seek your guidance.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: I will look into the bowl. Let me see...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: The Path is dimming now... it twists. Still, the signs are clear. You must get to the Heights of the city. If you remain in the dungeons, you will die.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: To get to the Heights, there are two paths... no, now there is only one. You must wear the Ring of Calling, and stand before the great Seal of Mythanthor.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Beyond the Seal... Odelinde... Harldain. These are your allies. Befriend them or die. But wait, who is this? Ancient... trapped... The Veil of Mystra descends. I cannot see more.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Augh! I hate it when that happens.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: I will not tell you. No mortal should glimpse their future. It is never happy enough, or long enough.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Take a look at my master! Would you become like him? Do not seek out the future! It will find you soon enough.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Talibund. The Veiled Ones. What soothsayers call those whose destinies cannot be foretold.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: How one becomes talibund, I do not know. My master says it has something to do with foolishness. I believe it has more to do with courage.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: My master Caalenfaire had worked out a destiny for you - a path you should walk. For the eventual good of Myth Drannor, if not your own.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: But instead you have become talibund. Now you walk your own path, which none can see. May Tymora help us! This is an unsettling turn.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Hoho, Volun! What do I see now, in my bowl? The Veiled Ones will be writ into the Song of Faerun!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Why, it is the great tale of this world, sung by the Bard of Kara-Tur. Master! Tell us more about the Song!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Listen, Volun, and be amazed.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: In Cormanthor did mage Mordrayn / speak spells of greed in Words of flame; / with poison troth she soon unmade / proud treasure of the Silver Blade; / and by her side, Pelendralaar, / their minds as one, come from afar; / dark creatures drown the city bright, the dragon's kin, the elf of night; / The Pool! The Pool! It grows, and yet, / one small band against it set.
keys.speaker: Bard
keys.desc: spoken: LOCALIZERS:  plays Song of Faerun Stanza 1 which should be saved as faerun1.wav

keys.dialogue: Yes, yes! I am amazed. This is not what we had foreseen! It gives me hope.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Yes, yes! I give you guidance now. Then you can go.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Seek, as I said, the serpent Odelinde and the dwarf spirit Harldain. They are your natural allies. Heed well their counsel!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To reach them on the Heights, you must go to the Seal of Mythanthor. Do you know where that is? Look for a purple crescent arc on the wall, in the uppermost part of the dungeons.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To reach them on the Heights, you open the Seal of Mythanthor. You have seen it - a purple crescent arc on the wall, in the uppermost part of the dungeons.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must find the Ring of Calling. -Master, look into your bowl. Can it tell you where the Ring of Calling might be?
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must find the Ring of Calling. My master says it may be in the House of Gems, which is east of here.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must wear the Ring of Calling. My master has released it from its bones for you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must wear the Ring of Calling. My master will speak the Word of Oblivion, and release it from its bones for you.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Ask them about the Song of Faerun
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Tell them you seek the Ring of Calling
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Tell them you seek the Word of Oblivion
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Ask them what 'talibund' means
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Ask them what the Path is
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Ask how you return to the Path
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Ask them what your future holds
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Ask them to finish their wise counsel
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Bid them goodbye
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Now watch, the omens change. Watch them, Volun; they pirouette.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: I tell you, something is happening!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: And the Ring of Calling... what of the Ring? It enters the Room of Words!
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Bones stay silent, but their silence speaks.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: She has put the Mark on them...
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Their doom is foretold!
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: The Path is the Path, Volun.
keys.speaker: caalenfa

keys.dialogue: And in Zhentil Keep?
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: ...Riots. Seven Cult leaders unmasked and killed. Wailing and consternation!
keys.speaker: Caalenfa
keys.desc: spoken, he describes what he sees in his bowl, to Volun

keys.dialogue: Haha! -Ah, Caalenfaire my love, the Veiled Ones are here.
keys.speaker: Volun

keys.dialogue: Yes, yes, they muddy my scrying bowl. Tell them, Volun, then send them away!
keys.speaker: Caalenfa

keys.dialogue: Your great deed will be celebrated all over Faerun. And Phlan will erect a monument in your honor!
keys.speaker: Volun
keys.desc: spoken, to party, relaying official info

keys.dialogue: But think not of returning to Phlan! For that is not in your future - not yet. Farewell.
keys.speaker: Volun
keys.desc: spoken, lowers her voice, whispers secret info

keys.dialogue: You have successfully entered the mighty Castle Cormanthor. The air reeks of smoke and the rank musk of mating dragon-kin.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This once-stately elven hall is now given over completely to the barrack-rookeries of the dragon-kin.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: History is written by the victors, so there is no epitaph for the nameless thousands who are at rest here - their lives, loves and sacrifices forgotten, their names lost to quiet eternity.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Immediately the Cult Mages begin to dispel their magic Gates.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Underneath the Cult Overseer's battered body, you find a curious treasure - a jawbone talisman made into a necklace, and electric with the mysterious ensorcellments of the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you pick it up, it summons a Gate.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Lashed to a horn in the Tusk-Lord's forehead, you find a sturdy iron key.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense that watchful eyes are upon you...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...but they find you lacking, because the drawbridge stays up.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense the presence of a magical guardian.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It examines you, and then with joy hurries to lower the drawbridge.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The aura of evil is strong here. You can sense waves of evil sloshing back and forth - from the orc idol to the dark Spawn Pool, and back again.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you shatter the orc idol, you break an evil spell.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: With its minions destroyed and its token in pieces, the Spawn Pool retreats to the foul place it sprang from - the Pool of Radiance.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door is solidly set and well-crafted, obviously by dwarves. It is firmly locked, but you see signs it's been opened recently. Through an unusually large keyhole, you smell the stale air of the dungeons, and the rank odor of orcs.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The chest once held a  proud silken banner, the centerpiece of the legendary Midsummer Firemeet of Myth Drannor. But now the banner is in decay, pawed and torn by greedy hands.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There is nothing of value inside.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You are in the presence of untold thousands of anguished souls. The pain of their unending death agonies grips your heart and lungs, making each heartbeat painful and each breath a gasp.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You lay the common battleaxe in the basin...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again phantom hands rise, eager to accept the token of your respect.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You lay the common dagger in the basin...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again unseen hands seize upon your token of respect.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Congratulations! You defeated Kya Mordrayn, and so she was claimed by her dark masters. And you slew the dracolich Pelendralaar, and used the Gauntlets of Moander to destroy the Pool of Radiance.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You have dealt a terrible blow to the mighty Cult of the Dragon, and all the free peoples of the Realms salute you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You lay the common warhammer in the basin...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again your tribute vanishes, seized eagerly by unseen spirits.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You lay the common long sword in the basin...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again the watchful spirits show their approval of your gift.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You lay the common mace in the basin...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again the phantom hands spirit away your gift.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: An inscription reads, 'If friend you be, and in need, these treasures are for thee. Use them as my companions no longer can.  - Jelde Asturien, Priest of Lathander, Knight of Myth Drannor'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The ground gives way beneath your feet...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As you approach this door, a chill settles upon your soul.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You have fallen at least 30 feet. You can see a ragged hole above you, but no way to get back to the surface the way you came.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Mellen, the Singing Word, unseals the Glyph of Song.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You recognize the magic seal in front of the door - it is the Glyph of Song. But you have not learned the glyph's Unsealing Word.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There is nothing left in this chest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the spectre's chest you find a grotesque gargoyle's mouth, carved in stone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Every time you speak, it repeats what you say in the harsh gargoyle tongue.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: And if gargoyles speak, it will translate what they say for you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There is nothing left in this chest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: ...and he was right. Look, Kalannar! Their company is half dead.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Ah. We were wondering who it was, making so much noise out in the hall. Foluben said it must be rats...
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: ...and he was right. You're far from home, little rats. And wounded, too!
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Ah. We were wondering who it was, making so much noise out in the hall. Foluben said it was rats... I said it was some light-loving rivven...
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: I will know next time that Foluben is always right.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: I suppose you are here seeking the Bodach Swan. If so, you come in vain.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Ibrith! What thick heads you light-lovers have! I told you, you seek it in vain.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Although, by the Ancient Eye, it would be a powerful ally for you.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: I tell you, forget the Bodach Swan! I am Greyanna Faeurdyn, malla ilharess of Myth Drannor! Focus your wits on me, if you can.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Very well, I will tell you, although I assure you, you will never meet the Swan.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Every drow child knows of the Bodach Swan. For it is the one who lurks around the corner, up near the surface, right at the edge of hearing, just out of sight.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Pale it is, with eyes that flash light into the darkest crevice, and a mouth like the inferno of the cursed Sun.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Yes, the Bodach Swan is just a story, a child's fable. I only brought it up because my warriors needed a moment to surround you.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Oh, the Bodach Swan is just a story we tell to scare our children. I only brought it up because my warriors needed a moment to surround you.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: What of them? Do not try to tell me they are your allies!
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Only fools, mindless thralls and the proud in chains ally with the Cult. Which are you?
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Go ahead. Call for help! I doubt the Cult or anyone else will come to aid you.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: What do I care? Kill them all, and welcome. We of the House of Freth have no more use for the Cult.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: They helped us destroy our blood enemies, the drow of the House of Kilsek.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: But soon we will chase the mighty Cult screaming off into the sunlight, where they belong.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: You, however - you will never see the cursed sunlight again.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Do not concern yourselves about the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Worry instead about the drow of the House of Freth.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Why do you care? In a moment, one or the other of us will be dust! What will a name matter then?
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: You seek to put off that moment, when one or the other of us will die. Ah, but I relish it! And that is the difference between us.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: Come, waerogglin! You gain nothing by waiting! The Bodach Swan will not come to save you. Lift your swords! Throw your spells! Act now! Save yourselves, if you can.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: I am Greyanna Faeurdyn, Qu'Daharil of the House of Freth, malla ilharess of the Catacombs of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Greyanna

keys.dialogue: The Rhonglyn room is mysterious. At its center, a large green gem has five jeweled pedestals arranged around it, coated in ice.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The air is chill. You sense there is an old power lurking just out of sight, waiting to be called forth again.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You re-enter the mysterious Rhonglyn room. It is still bitterly cold in here.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to other Rhonglyn rooms you've seen - and just as frigid inside.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to one you've seen before. It too is bitterly cold.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Fresh air flows down the stairs going up. You listen carefully, but all is quiet.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The book is bound in iron. Etched into the iron is a note: 'Torvassin: Insidious evil is writ here. Toss this book without delay into the Pyre of Silence.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The water has an acrid smell and an unhealthy color.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door is uncommonly ornate and fixed with a platinum lock. It has also been defaced with crude orcish symbols.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This is an ancient taproom. Something here reeks strongly of drink.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A ladder in the well hangs down into darkness. Cool air and faint rustling sounds float up.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door was once painted with the dwarven rune of brewing. Only the faintest of outlines remains.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The tap is now empty and the beer has long since evaporated.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you turn the tap, out drops a precious necklace! The massive gemstone is the color of dark beer, and scribed with runes of safety and protection.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door was once painted with a rune, but it's now too faint to make out what it was.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The air here is stifling hot, and smells of beast.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The body of a dwarven warrior lies here. His remains have endured long after the bodies of his opponents have crumbled to dust.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The scroll bears a crude image of a female orc holding an orc baby.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You find an old note here that reads, 'Drake: I pray you can claim our keepsake. I hid it where we so often sat to play at chess. -Durlin.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A horrible stench assails your nostrils.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You notice at once that this door is unusual - it has no handle or lock.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This is the tomb of the legendary champion of Myth Drannor, Arms-Captain  Hachaam Selorn.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Everyone has heard how he gave his life turning back the Armies of Darkness as they first breached the city walls.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The day of his burial, the Forces of Darkness rallied and took the city.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The books here have arcane symbols on their covers, and all their pages are entirely blank.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You make out a sigil of warding written on this wall. The sigil prevents whatever may be on the far side from tearing down the wall.

keys.dialogue: A magic mouth speaks. You recognize the voice as Faeril's.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: First she warns you not to drink from this fountain.

keys.dialogue: Then she tells you that it is possible to parley with the orogs to the south.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: They are brutish creatures, yes, and disgusting to look upon, but they dealt honorably with Beriand and me. Fare thee well!'

keys.dialogue: It is a heavy key, ornately made in the style of the dwarvish smiths of old. You notice a sigil on it - a gem hidden in a mountain - the sign of the dwarf god Dumathoin, Keeper of Secrets.

keys.dialogue: You put the key into your pack.
keys.speaker: DM
