keys.dialogue: The silence here is uneasy, as if watchful beings lurk just out of sight.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can tell someone lives here - but they've been gone for some days.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The stones all around it are well-worn, but the fountain itself is dry, empty save for a bit of dust.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This looks like it was once a library.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You stumble upon some old armor, battered and worthless. From the size of it, you guess it was once worn by a derro.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Someone or something has been clawing mindlessly at this door.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You hear a ghostly giggle, and sense rather than see someone disappear to the northwest. A jasmine scent hangs in the air.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The ancient waysign is scarred but legible. It indicates the 'Turgild Square' can be found to the south, and the 'Great Hall' lies directly north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The waysign indicates 'Turgild Square' to the south, and 'Great Hall' to the north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You catch the scent of jasmine, and sense a form sashaying away to the northeast, through the wall to the room beyond.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: From here, the ruins of a grand thoroughfare disappear into the gloom to the east.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well. Your ranger can tell that most of them are skeletons and other undead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well. Your rangers can tell that the skeletons and other undead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There is a sudden whisper of movement among you - the grumble of dwarves and the clunk of rusty armor. It fades out to the north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Ahead of you, in the gloom, is the city square. But the arched hall no longer rings with laughter, and it seems likely the public wells have long since gone dry.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but you can tell that orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but your ranger can tell that six orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but your rangers agree on this: six orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The prison cell seems to be occupied.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This great room seems unusually tidy. Even the floor has been swept clean in spots.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Something very heavy just shook the ground to the south!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The ancient waysign indicates that 'Bedlam Prison' can be found to the south, down the stairs.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It warns visitors 'not to bring keys into the prison, by order of the Warden of the Keys.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's likely the Warden has been dead for centuries, however.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The waysign indicates 'Bedlam Prison' to the south, and warns visitors not to bring keys into the prison.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Suddenly you feel dwarf ghosts among you, clanking in their rusty armor. A lock thuds shut. Then they are gone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again you hear the grumble of dwarves and the clunk of rusty armor. A lock thuds shut. Then - nothing.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Suddenly you hear dwarves among you - their rusty armor faintly clanking. They murmur approval, and then are heard no more.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You enter the dwarven tombs. Dust lies heavy in this once-great hall, but you sense its dead sleep uneasily, if they sleep at all.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You step again into the dwarven Hall of the Dead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The floor here seems to have been swept clean.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your ranger can tell that someone has carefully swept away all the footprints in this area.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your rangers can tell that someone has carefully swept away all the footprints in this area.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense that a powerful creature recently held court here - maybe an alhoon.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But it is gone now and its lair plundered.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A ghostly presence glowers in the doorway. It raises a cautionary hand...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A ghostly presence glowers in the doorway. It raises a cautionary hand...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again a ghostly presence fills the doorway. It cautions you not to enter....
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A ghostly form is hovering here. It bows to you, then disappears.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A faint track here leads out the door to the northwest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your ranger notices a faint track here. A humanoid carrying something heavy stayed here for a while, then left through the door to the northwest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One of your rangers notices a faint track here. A humanoid carrying something heavy stayed here for a while, then left through the door to the northwest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You hear the crunch of dainty footsteps, which pass right among you heading to the northeast. A brush of gossamer, a whiff of jasmine, then - nothing.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In a gossamer flurry a ghost flits off far to the west, leaving only a trace of jasmine in the air.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Someone giggles softly with anticipation - but there is nothing here but the faint scent of jasmine.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Some creature has marked this doorjamb with a particularly nasty scent.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You see ruined walls and gaping doorways. Generations of creatures have plundered this area for stone and wood to fortify their lairs.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You arrive at a crossroads. Over the years, untold thousands of creatures have died trying to win control of this strategic spot. Of their struggle, nothing remains but bits of bone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Avenue of Smiths.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To the north is the Grand Avenue; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Stone Flower Halls lie to the west.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Stone Flower Halls.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To the north is the Grand Avenue; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Grand Avenue.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To the west are the Stone Flower Halls; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from Apothecary Row.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To the west are the Stone Flower Halls; to the north, the Grand Avenue. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The signpost indicates the Grand Avenue is to the north; Apothecary Row is to the south; the Avenue of Smiths is to the east, and Stone Flower Halls lie to the west.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Of these once-happy places, almost nothing remains.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: These halls have been torn down and rebuilt many times - most recently, by someone with little skill.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The orc chief, Zud, has a crude iron key in his clenched fist. It is a small key, such as those used for treasure chests.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Looking into the chest, your eye is immediately drawn to an ornate staff.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Looking closely, you see the staff is laced with intricate runes, writ in a fine elvish hand, and more plainly, the name 'Deathbane.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Although the chest holds a fine warhammer, a potion, and some gold, you find your eye drawn first to one small, pale blue key at the bottom.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Tumbled with the remains of a human woman, you find a pair of enchanted boots, made of snakeskin.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Branded on one of them is the name 'Ozama.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When the naga dies, the darkness in his lair lifts.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: On the naga's body you find a rare necklace indeed - the Wizard's Torc, a great sweeping arc of gold, finely inscribed with arcane symbols.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As you lift it up, you notice that something is missing from its center.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Suddenly the Starstone you bear leaps from its pouch, and shoots through the air over to the Wizard's Torc!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You have restored the Starstone to the Wizard's Torc. The Torc will now open the Circle of Ualair the Silent, just as Harldain told you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Harldain told you the Torc was missing its Starstone. To restore the power of the Wizard's Torc, you must reunite it with the Starstone he gave you - which is now probably in the greedy hands of Nottle the Scavenger.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the ormyrr's pouch you discover his 'magic twig' - a magic wand, its power all but gone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As he died, the orc captain Mol dropped his lead mace - it clattered to the floor cracking some of the stones it landed on.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the coffin you find a necklace of breathtaking beauty - and it glows with the blessing of Haela Brightaxe, the dwarven goddess of battle.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It was the prized possession of the dwarf lord Onglore, who prided himself on being first into battle.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'Higbin: The ceremony ended too soon. The man's name is Faldis. Wait a fortnight, then take what he no longer needs. And do not fail to give me my share. -K'
keys.speaker: Tscroll

keys.dialogue: You are worthy. I will help you bring rest to the Lifespring Guardian.  Look for me... at the Fountain of Stone...
keys.speaker: Garras
keys.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: This text line combines 1.0 and 1.1: First line spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect; second line spoken, ethereally, fading out with ghost effect

keys.dialogue: Many thanks, strangers, for this small kindness.
keys.speaker: Garras
keys.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect, fading away

keys.dialogue: You have made a friend. I will help you bring rest to the Lifespring Guardian.  We will meet again... at the Fountain of Stone...
keys.speaker: Elena
keys.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: This text line combines 1.0 and 1.1: First line spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect; second line spoken, ethereally, fading out with ghost effect

keys.dialogue: You have given me peace... and I thank you.
keys.speaker: Elena
keys.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect, fading away

keys.dialogue: As you approach, many-legged small things scurry back into the barrel.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'Juliban Genshihir, Wizard of Air, is at rest here. He was the last Keeper of Shaundakul's Gift, the Earthborn Wind.'
keys.speaker: Jcoffin

keys.dialogue: Blessing winds begin to flow from deep underground, up into the three Channel openings overhead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You hear healing energy flow again, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As Elena's ghost fades away, you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As Garras' ghost fades away, you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Reunited at last, the two ghosts fade away, and you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It seems this sturdy door can only be unlocked from the other side.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The foul air here has a familiar chill. You have returned to the deepest part of the dungeons.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Shashakiro, the Splashing Word, unseals the Glyph of Water.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This Glyph seems to have something to do with water.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Shashakiro, the Splashing Word, unseals the Glyph of Water.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A Glyph seals this door. You think maybe it is the Glyph of Water.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The Rune on the floor is the famous sigil of the god Clangeddin Silverbeard, the dwarven Father of Battle.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Someone has flanked it with crude arrangements of sharpened sticks.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'Faldis - Who Never Fell In Battle.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Above the door is carved a gem in a mountain - the famous sigil of the dwarf god Dumathoin, The Keeper of Secrets.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The sign of Dumathoin is carved overhead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The sign of Dumathoin is carved overhead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This is the diary of Faldis, a warrior of old Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'Here in my last days, all honor me for my courage. I bury my secret here with me: courage had I none! What I had was... '
keys.speaker: fdiary

keys.dialogue: '...a stout shield, and the wit to have it enchanted.  May any who find it show more courage than I did.'
keys.speaker: fdiary

keys.dialogue: Under the smith's table you find something wrapped in rags. It is still warm to the touch.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The air is heavy with the smell of cooked meat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There is an inscription on the tomb, 'To Aeseder, brother and planeswalker, at rest but not forgotten.  --Kluusar'.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This private crypt bears the sorcerer's symbol of the blood moon.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you grasp the ruby, a vision flashes into your head: a man's hand releasing the ruby, a man's face watching it fall into a bottomless well.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Find the Well. Release the Ruby. Restore the Wind.
keys.speaker: Juliban

keys.dialogue: You see that the Well is dark and silent, and not a breath of air comes up from it into the Channels overhead.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The Rhonglyn room is mysterious. At its center, a large red gem has five jeweled pedestals arranged around it, coated in ice.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The air here is electric with the magic of old Myth Drannor - with power idle for centuries. And it's as cold as the North Wind.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You re-enter the mysterious Rhonglyn room. It is still bitterly cold in here.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to other Rhonglyn rooms you've seen - and just as frigid inside.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to one you've seen before. It too is bitterly cold.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The symbol painted on this door is almost too faint to be made out - a masked dwarf with fiery eyes.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This could only be Gorm Gulthyn, the dwarven god of guardians, watchfulness, and justice.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The well is dry, but you see signs that someone has rested here fairly recently.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your ranger can tell it was a party of humans, and soon finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: After a lengthy investigation, the rangers in your party uncover a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your rogue finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One of your rogues finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'Thumtal, Emmeric: we killed the creatures laired here - a dark naga and many minions - so the rooms around here should be safe for a while. No sign yet of the Room we seek. We will go up the stair far north of here - follow us as soon as you can. -Athan
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Charred scraps litter the area around the furnace. It seems many books have been burned here.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The flame in the furnace gleams a little brighter in anticipation.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Far off you hear keys jingling.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can make out the name 'Shaundakul' and the words 'gift' and 'Earthborn.' That is all.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...but your sharp-eyed ranger manages to read the inscription nevertheless.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...but working together your sharp-eyed rangers manage to read the inscription nevertheless.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...but by running a trained hand over the stone, your rogue manages to coax the message forth by touch.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...but by running their trained hands over the stone, your rogues manage to coax the message forth by touch.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'THIS IS THE WELL OF THE EARTHBORN WIND, a Gift given unto the Dwarvenfolk of Myth Drannor by Shaundakul, the Windrider, the God of the Helping Hand.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'May the Blessing Breezes it brings up from the untrammeled Depths ever refresh the Peaceful Peoples of the City of Song.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When the ice shatters, you free the Rhonglyn! You feel the ancient magical devices coming back to life throughout the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Under the ice you find a strange item: a knife sculpted from a sliver of blue ice, chill and electric to the touch.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The chest is now empty.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You find a heavy club, with words spun of silver embedded in its haft...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'Root split stone, leaf drink mist, twig grow into Mountain Fist.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It looks like this prison guard starved to death at his post.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When the spectre is destroyed, his prized key ring becomes corporeal again, and falls to the ground.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But the keys have all been worn smooth by centuries of mindless locking and unlocking of doors. You throw the useless thing away.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This wall once had painting on it. You see faint outlines of what might have been a ceremonial scene...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...maybe set in Turgild Square, up in the Main Halls. Try as you might, no one in your party can make out the details.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...with some effort, your ranger traces out the details.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...with some effort, your rangers trace out the details.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...your rogue soon skillfully traces out the details.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...your rogues soon skillfully trace out the details.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The commemorative painting is in two parts. The lower scene shows elves gathered around a wondrous fountain, casting spells on it while great golems stand guard.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the upper scene, elves, dwarves, gnomes, humans and other peoples frolic in the sustaining waters of four public wells. You recognize the place: Turgild Square, up in the Main Halls.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Stand away! Heed my warning! Do not touch this sword, unless you are willing to take my place in the Tomb of Eternal Sleep. I, Eadred son of Endoros, have spoken.
keys.speaker: Mouth
keys.desc: spoken, stern, in Eadred's voice, but enhanced and magical

keys.dialogue: The voice seems to emanate from the sword itself!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: So - at last someone dares to wake me. Your need must be very great!
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Those twisted madmen are here? Then what I dreamed is true - all true. Myth Drannor did fall! I thought - I hoped - it was just an evil dream.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Speak no more of evil - but let us avenge it!
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Who am I? My name you know. I am a man of arms, as my father before me - trained with the sword, the shield, the mace, and the bow.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Cleverness - I have none. But no man sees his duty more clearly.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: As to how I came here - do men still speak of Arms-Captain Hachaam Selorn? And his elf-sword Faervian? Now there was a bladesinger!
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: It was he who slew the lothwight Forgrond, and unwisely tried to claim that foul one's weapon for his own. That is how this cold Tomb claimed him.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: But - the City needed him - the Weeping War was going badly - do you understand? So I came here and took the sword for my own, and released him. It was my clear duty.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: And then - what? Selorn must have died, for he never returned to release me. But now you are here in his place, and once again I take up arms to defend the glory of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Why, I believe one of your company touched the cursed sword. Thus the Tomb released me, but claimed your companion.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: But you need not fear! Any time you wish - I will be honored to take the sword again, and free the brave soul that took my place in the cold Tomb.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Certainly! Do you think I lack courage? It has only grown stronger over the years.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Any time you wish - I will be honored to take the sword again, and free the brave soul that took my place in the cold Tomb. Just bid me take up the blade.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: As I told you - bid me take up the cold blade, and your companion will be freed.
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Even if my destiny is to die and be forgotten...
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Until you bid me to grasp again the cold blade of forgetfulness...
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: For as long as you will have me - I, Eadred son of Endoros, am one of you!
keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Eadred joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.speaker: Eadred

keys.dialogue: Now I can say, the centuries in the tomb were not in vain. No, by the Hand of Helm, I am glad the Tomb preserved me, so that I could live to see this day.

keys.dialogue: What news? Have you found new evil? Say the word, and I, Eadred son of Endoros, will raise swords with you once more!

keys.dialogue: By Helm's Hand! Beriand told us you had succeeded in your quest. And a good thing too!

keys.dialogue: For the Cult had come here in force, and hard pressed was I to keep Nottle's head upon his shoulders.

keys.dialogue: But then we heard Kya Mordrayn scream! I tell you, everyone on Faerun heard it! And the Cult slogs scattered like leaves on the wind.

keys.dialogue: 'But through some foul treachery the beasts came up the stairs from behind, and so we were undone.'

keys.dialogue: 'Now we will rest, and trouble you no more.'

keys.dialogue: That you found a full count of six burned bodies, I doubt not. But fireballs leave friend and foe looking much alike.

keys.dialogue: Athan was beset by winged beasts, vile things under the mages' command. They dragged him into the sky as I woke from the damnable sleep spell.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: I saw him struggle even then, flailing his axe at their wings as they lifted him to the Castle ramparts.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: The great mage Elminster handpicked Athan and his band to venture here. He bid us uncover what evil taints the city's guardian spell, the ancient Mythal.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Since Myth Drannor's fall, the spell has faded some, but of late, a dark corruption has possessed it and twisted even its last remaining boons to curses.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Elminster sent us here to discover the cause of the corruption. That we did, but at great cost:  my companions are dead, and the priceless Gauntlets of Moander are stolen by their murderers.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Some new force has entered Myth Drannor, driven out the laired and lesser evils, and taken possession of Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: The corruption of the Mythal is their doing. They have twisted its power, and used it to raise a Pool of Radiance whose evil might spreads throughout Faerun.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: The Gauntlets hold a singular gift: the power to destroy Pools of Radiance.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Their palms are graven with eye runes, which have slumbered since the destruction of the Pool at Phlan. A season ago, they snapped open once again, to warn of a new Pool rising.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Elminster feared that this new Pool could be at the heart of the evil changes newly come over Myth Drannor. He sent us with the Gauntlets to uncover the truth.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: If his fears were founded, and we found such a Pool, we were to use the Gauntlets to destroy it. But rather, we have let them slip into the hands of our enemies.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: My feet may have been bound, but my ears were open: the mages serve a dark mistress who's taken hold of Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: It was to her they took the Gauntlets of Moander, which Elminster himself gave into our keeping.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: I listened for a name to curse, but they spoke of their masters only as 'She' and 'Her'...and sometimes 'Him'....and trembled at the words.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: The mages took from me a ring of great power, sealed onto a skeletal arm.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: They've taken it to the Room of Words, in the hopes of unsealing the ring from its dead wearer's hand.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Athan believed that that ring, the Ring of Calling, holds the key to attaining the city Heights, where our quest lies.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Athan believed that the Ring of Calling holds the key to attaining the City Heights, where our quest lies.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: But to wield it, and thereby open the gate at the Circle of Mythanthor, he searched for the Word that will release the ring from its dead master's hand.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Legend has it that such things can be found in the Hall of Wizards. The portal between these dungeons and the Hall is a ring of colored stones whose magic can bear you from floor to floor.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: He said that only one who wears the ring can open the gate at the Circle of Mythanthor and use it to move freely between the dungeons and the Heights above.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: It was Athan's firm belief that the evil guiding these mages lies at the heart of Castle Cormanthor. He sought to find a way to attack their stronghold there and abolish the threat they pose to Faerun.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: That I will, and gladly.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: A party of so many would be a danger to itself in this cursed place.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: But if any of your number chose to step aside, I'd gladly take up arms with you. Until then...
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: The slain comrades you bear are not yet past saving. But should you see fit to bury them, or if any of your number chooses to step aside from our quest, I'd gladly take up arms with you. Until then...
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Then I will make my way back to Stillwater. The elves there were good friends to us - Faeril led us bleeding out of these dungeons, and Beriand tended our wounds.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: I don't want to bring my bad luck upon them, however, or give away their secret shelter to our enemies. Nottle said he could use someone to guard his wagon...
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: My companions are dead and my quest failed, unless it lives with you.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: I admit, I was no match for any in Athan's band when I slipped into their midst. Elminster laughed that I made bold to join them on so dire a journey.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: But my arm has been the end of many a foul creature since then. And my peacock's pride, reborn as watchfulness.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Let me join with you against this evil, and wet my blade in the blood of those who slew my friends.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Your numbers are many now, but should any of you choose to step aside from our quest, I'll gladly take up arms with the rest against this evil. Until then...
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Your numbers are many, though some lie between this world and the next. But should you find yourselves few, I'll gladly take up arms with you against this evil. Until then...
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: You'll not regret the company of my blade: vengeance makes a fine sharpening stone.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: Emmeric joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Then I thank you for my life and for my freedom from this carrion.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: May whatever gods you hold dear watch your backs. Find me with Nottle, if ever you need another eager blade.
keys.speaker: Emmeric

keys.dialogue: What goes on inside this House, I be aware of - I feel it, aye, just as I once felt air in my lungs and blood in my veins.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: So I have seen ya and know yar tough mettle, with the arraccats, aye, and the orogs, and the glaveens from the Cult of the Dragon. Ya cleansed the water, ya did. And so I know ya be the ones to bring back the City Spires, or none will.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, I know, ya young ones, so impatient. Well - if ya want to get going aroun' this city, listen up!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: About the only use that tomfool of a mage ever be. Except the Spires. The Spires be the rarest of the rare - magic that be useful!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ya seen the tall Spires here and there in the city, have ya not? And the Orrery, the big tickamatock in the Speculum?
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The Orrery, 'twould use the motion of the planets to move ya between Spires in a twinkling. Ah, 'twas easy to move around then - the Orrery spinning like a top, and children chasing each other from Spire to Spire to Spire, crossing the whole city in the shake of a stick.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: We dwarves carved five stones for the Orrery, beautiful stones - green, blue, red, orange, and white, the colors of the planets.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But during the Dark Days, we stopped the Orrery, and took out the stone Planets, and bound them in metal. Because, if not bound, the Planets fly back to the Orrery, so strong be the life we carved in them.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, the Planet of Trees. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Tulimatar, the orange one, the Angry Planet. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Veelaar, the red one, the Planet of Luck. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. Or bring them here to me. So the Spires may live again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: If ya find any of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. Or bring them here to me. So the Spires may live again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I have seen ya carry one of the Planets with ya. Here, I call it forth.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Kharop-bazun!
keys.speaker: Harldain

keys.dialogue: Now, I break its bonds and...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery! Back to the Speculum, where it belongs!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. So the Spires may live again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Nothing - unless ya be tired of walking. Free the Planets, and the Spires will make it easy for ya to get from anywhar to anywhar.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Tulimatar, the orange one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Tulimatar, the orange one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For three of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Tulimatar, the orange one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah, 'tis selfish, or maybe not so. I be bound to this place, as I said. What goes on outside these walls, I know nothing of it.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But if the Orrery runs like tops again, and the Gates open, and the Spires return... Maybe my soul will stretch farther... maybe I will live in my City again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Maybe then the part of me I gave to this city will remain here forever... and the part that be Harldain Ironbar will at last join his kin in the Long House of the Dwarves.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For ya, the Spires will be handy, eh? Ya had enough of walking? For me, they would be peace. Truth be, I grow tired. One day follows another, and I long for sleep.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Wait now, ya ungrateful glaveen. Ya must receive a gift from me first.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The last Planet be down in the Catacombs, or so I heard from someone who dwells there.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: At least one of the Planets be down in the Catacombs, or so I heard from someone who dwells there.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ya know the Catacombs? The elf warrens under the castle? Of course ya don't. No way to get to 'em now - all the common ways blocked up long ago.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But there be an old way, eh? To use the Wizard's Torc, and pass through the Circle of Ualair. But to make the Torc work for ya, I must give ya the Starstone.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But there be an old way, eh? To use the Wizard's Torc, and pass through the Circle of Ualair. And I see ya have the Wizard's Torc with ya, that which be lost all these years!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis a neckpiece, a great pondering arc of gold.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: It used to have the power to open the Circle of Ualair, 'til its Starstone was wrenched out. Now it's naught but a ringly slibslab of gold.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Why, 'tis outside the Speculum, the spiraling circle in the amphitheater - if it not be trampled to dust by the long march of years.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis one of Myth Drannor's greatest treasures.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For the Torc be not complete, ya see. Ualair the Silent wrenched the Starstone from it, so that it be useless to the enemy.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: If the Wizard's Torc be mended, a true heart may stand in the Circle of Ualair, and open a Gate to the catacombs under the Castle.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: No one has used that Gate since the fall of Myth Drannor. It be time someone did, to be bringing light to places dark for too long. And that is why I be giving up the Starstone.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I will give it, aye, so when ya find the Wizard's Torc ya be able to make it complete, and so ya enter the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Sirra, I know not. Without the Starstone, it be only a pretty bauble for the neck.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: After the Weeping War it disappeared into the dungeons, where it be gathering dust in some forgotten corner or slavering thing's lair.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah, ya people of flesh and blood, such a hurry ya be in. Hurry all ya like, ya'll be like me anyway. -Here's what ya should know.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ya can start up the City Spires if ya free the Planets. Then the Spires can move ya across the City in a wink. Ya know the Orrery Planets, don't ya? Five glowing stones, bound up in metal.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But one of the Planets be in the Catacombs, eh? Under the castle. And to get down there, ya need to put the Starstone back into the Wizard's Torc.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But one of the Planets be in the Catacombs, eh? Under the castle. And to get down there, ya need me put the Starstone back into yar Wizard's Torc.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: And then ya use the Wizard's Torc at the Circle of Ualair, right? And that be all.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: So let me have yar treasure, so's I can combine it with one of mine - the Starstone.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For the Torc be not complete, ya see. Ualair the Silent wrenched the Starstone out from it. He knew the Speculum be lost, but he hoped against hope the Army of Darkness would not take Castle Cormanthor, once the Torc be made useless.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: With the Wizard's Torc complete, a true heart may stand in the Circle of Ualair, and open a Gate to the catacombs under the Castle.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Why, he be the Grand Mage of Myth Drannor in those dark days before the Fall.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: No one has used that Gate since the fall of Myth Drannor. 'Tis time someone did, and brought light to places that been dark for too long.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: In the Dark Days, after Ualair the Silent plucked it from the Wizard's Torc, aye, he gave it into my keeping. And now thankful will I restore it to its place.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aya, goodbye, I'll keep ya no longer.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, goodbye, I'll leave ya in peace.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Except to say, I have a collection, eh? Excellent weapons, fine armor - prizes plucked from unlucky travelers, or from the stiff hands of robbers who thought our hoard unguarded.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For ya, I might be persuaded to part with a piece or two - for a price.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Well, don't leave without the Starstone! Without it, the Wizard's Torc be naught but a pretty necklace.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: And see me also about my collection. Excellent weapons, fine armor... for ya, I be persuaded maybe to let go a piece or two - for a price.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: First, I must tell ya, I have a collection, eh? Excellent weapons, fine armor - prizes plucked from unlucky travelers, or from the stiff hands of robbers who thought our hoard unguarded.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Sirrah, time to go.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For ya, I be persuaded maybe to part with a piece or two - for a price.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now here be the Starstone. Keep it well, until ya find the Wizard's Torc, so the Starstone can make it whole again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now I take the Wizard's Torc and tap in the Starstone, where it belongs.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: There! With this, ya can enter the Circle of Ualair the Silent, and open the Gate to the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Find the slot just inside the doorway, aye, and put the Passkey in. The traps will fall silent, and ya be safe crossing the hall.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: When ya want to turn the traps on again, put the Passkey back into the slot. Then beware! Traps be deadly once again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: That pool, that foul cess that erupted by my pumphouse. It be like a fell hand squeezing the life out of my heart.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I thank ya for removing it, and cleansing the city water, aye, I thank ya most warmly.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aya, there be a Passkey around here somewhere, turns the traps off. There not be a reason to use it for over a hundred years.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Devilish, the traps! Aye! We employed the services of Kilgorash the Cunning, a kobold lord. Yes, even kobolds be living peacefully in Myth Drannor, before the Dark Days came.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: This be the Onaglym, the House of Gems. Huge wealth we dwarves held here in our hoard - and one day will hold again. The traps be always standing guard over that wealth.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Sadly depleted, aye, ransack and ruin! But I be building it up, so one day my kin be led back to Myth Drannor - if not by their beards of honor, then by their greedy noses!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, I know it well! I be aware of everything that happens here in the House of Gems. But I be caught, as ya know, by the foul Pool, and could not come to your aid.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah - a joke! As if I be telling you where the hoard lay! Ho ho! The fabulous Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves, which thousands have sought at the cost of their lives! Ho ho ho ho ho!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis a device that shows how the planets move in the sky. The mages use them to harness celestial motion, or some such fool notion.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Once I knew every stone and slab of this city. But then the wars came, and I died, and helpless I am, cursed ya might say, to watch others tumble my great works into folly, ay, folly and ruin.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Pool of Radiance? I know naught about it, except that 'tis another plague conjured up by tomfool mages, aye, who brew naught but trouble always for the solid folk of the earth.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah! Now there be a spell even a dwarf finds beautiful - an ancient protective spell that be woven into stone and spire, rock and road of this city.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: We dwarves played a proud part in its creation - for we cut and polished the Gems of the Weave, the huge precious stones that allow mortals to touch the Mythal's mighty magic.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But lately it seems to me that the Mythal falters, aye, or goes astray. Maybe the current Gem be taken, or maybe no guardian be left to guide the Mythal.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, Mystra be a goddess much beloved by the people of this city, at one time. And kind to dwarves, I may add, though few dwarves loved her.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: She cries out for her followers, ya say? I know not where her followers may be.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The building ya speak of be a shrine to Mystra. The lady Anorrweyn, a fair elf - she be priestess there when I were alive.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Whatever aid ya can lend her, ya should do.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: They entered my House about a fortnight ago. By then, the slowness was upon me, and naught I could do - naught but smile when I felt the traps go off!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But then they be moving into the tower, and sitting longtimes in the Room of Words. Until ya came and taught them what swords and spells be for!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now I feels the rude boots of orog, trampin' up and down my Round Tower, aye, even as we speak.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I do not know why I linger here, when all my kith and kin entered the Long House years ago. The folly of some wizard, or the cruel whim of some human god, aye, no doubt.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: By the Beard! Ya found one of the Orrery's Planets, and ya carried it here. By yar leave, I call it forth, to ma hand.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Well! Ya have been busy, or so I have heard.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn came to visit me. She told me of yar exploits, aye, and our great need for a new Gem of the Weave.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: A Cult Mage fell into one of my traps, ya see, and told me much before he died.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Well! By the Beard! Ya have been busy!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I see ya carry an Orrery Planet. And the elf-lady Anorrweyn came to me, aye, and told me ya'd be here, seeking a new Gem of the Weave.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I see ya carry an Orrery Planet. And a Cult Mage fell into one of my traps, and told me much before he died, aye, about the Baelnorn and his Gem.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But first, yar Orrery Planet! With yar leave, I call it forth to my hand.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Kharop-bazun!
keys.speaker: Harldain

keys.dialogue: I break the iron bands and...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery! Back to the Speculum, where it belongs!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery, to join the others ya released.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, ya done well. By my count, ya but need to free one more, and then the Spires will live again!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. So the Spires may live again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Why, that stone ya carried be one of the Planets, belongs in the Great Orrery in the Speculum. I be telling you about it earlier.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: We took them from the Orrery back during the Weeping Wars, because the foe be using the Spires to invade the City.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: We bound the Planets in metal, lest they fly back on their own to whar they belong. When I took off the binding, that's what it did, aye - flew back to the Orrery.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Then there be three others out there somewheres, waiting for ya to release them as well.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Then there be two others out there somewheres, waiting for ya to release them as well.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Be ya walking up to any Spire, ya can command it, aye, and so ya travel to any other Spire in the wink of an eye.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: She be a water spirit. She dwelt in this area long before our kind raised a City here, and like as not, when its last spire crumbles, she be here still.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: A frivolous creature, but by the Father! She made beautiful music in our fountains and pools, once upon a time.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, the Red Planet, Veelaar, it be seen once in a high tower of the Castle - but none can get up there now but flying creatures.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the White Planet, Sash-pulim, down in the catacombs.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the Orange Planet, Tulimatar, in the village of the lizard-men.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the Green Planet, Dulumbarzul, over in the marshes.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now ya best be about yar business.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Farewell, and may your beard grow long.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: ...listen! Ya hear that?
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I can feel it... the Spires are coming alive. All over this part of the City.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah, glaveens, ya have done it. Now my spirit can travel beyond this old House. And ya can use the Spires to get all around the City in the wink of an eye!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, 'tis a marvel, such a marvel that I can hardly speak. Thank ya, aye, thank ya most warmly.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now must we talk on matters more grave - the new Gem of the Weave.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: From what that Cult Mage said, ya know we need a new Gem of the Weave, and quickly.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn told me how greatly we need it.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: So I be about to do something I swore I never - giving up one of the keys to the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves.
keys.speaker: harldain
keys.desc: spoken, brisk, this is a huge honor

keys.dialogue: You must go out into the open air, into the courtyard of the House of Gems.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: There be a statue out in the middle of the courtyard - or rather I say, the statue be gone, but the pedestal remains...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: There be a hole in that pedestal. That be whar ya use the key I give ya.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I be giving ya the Emerald of the Weave - a great green gem, aye, flawless and dazzling.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: It be large, eh? This be but one of the keys to the Hoard, aye, and ya shall but glimpse the treasures I have locked away.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I hoard them so that someday, when my kin return to rebuild this City, they may find them of use.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Bear it to the top of the Speculum, aye, to the top of the dragon's back, and lay it upon the spines.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The Emerald must be made into the Gem of the Weave. For that, ya need not only the Gem, but one who will be bound to it. Aye, but who among you can be sacrificed to that spell?
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: For the Gem requires a Communicant, one tied forever to the Mythal. A powerful priest or mage, or else the joining will destroy you.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: In the glory days, people would rush to take the honor! A Tyryl Wizard, maybe, or one of the Dweomerkeepers of Mystra. But now, after the Fall... I wonder if anyone suitable be left alive.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: So that is why you must go back to the lady Anorrweyn, and free her. She must be your Communicant - there be no other.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: So that is why you must go back to the lady Anorrweyn, and plead your case. She must be your Communicant - there be no other.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The key be a device called a Tumblebar. It be shafts of iron linked with bits of chain - aye, a strange and cunning contrivance indeed.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: There be a statue out in the courtyard of this House. Or rather, the statue be gone, but the pedestal remains...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Put the Tumblebar into the pedestal - ya'll find a hole atween two stones. 'Twill go all the way in - and what was hidden will be revealed.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Be ya thinking of any more questions for me, afore I give ya the Tumblebar?
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: They would do just as you! Their High Mage would attune the Gem to herself, aye! And if she be not killed, she be able to sway the Mythal.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But she would not restore it to good, eh? She would take its powers and twist them to evil. So hold fast to the Emerald of the Weave!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I be no a wizard, for which I eternally thank the All-Father, but even I can tell that it be fading - or worse, be falling under someone's sway.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I know not, aye, I do not truck in talismans of death. It be not in this House, nowhere around here, that's all say I.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Nay, I have not. The Cult of the Dragon has sent warriors against me, aye, more trap-fodder, but naught of their wizardly kitkob was worthy of the Hoard.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Hark now, I be forgetting to tell you of Plinshree.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I know the naiad right well, for 'twas I who built the water system in this city. She be a flighty creature, none worse, but become dear to me even so.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis a sorrow ya did not find her waterbells, for by the Bearded Lady! they make a pretty music.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis a sorrow ya did not give her the waterbells you found, for by the Bearded Lady! they made a pretty music. Can ya not find a fountain or a well and lighten your load?
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah, 'tis joy that ya gave her some of the waterbells back! 'Tis sorrow that she does not have all of them, for by the Bearded Lady, they make a pretty music!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: 'Tis great joy that ya gave her the waterbells back! Did ya hear them? By the Bearded Lady, they make a pretty music!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Why, Anorrweyn, as I told ya, and the water spirit, Plinshree...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: The water spirit, Plinshree, she talks me from out the water...
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: ...and the Cult be sending two or three dozen warriors, aye, but they never stay for long. They be wonderfully stupid about traps!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Ah! Some times ago, a rogue be creeping through. Ha, he were a shifty one, not a trap sprung on him, no sirrah.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But neither did he find much treasure, so off he crept again.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: I think that be all.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: And the pesky gargoyles be flocking in the garden again. I think that be all.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Aye, ya be ready. The Gem be one of our most precious treasures! Do not let the Cult get ahold it, or the Mythal be lost to us forever!
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: But I talk overlong, and of trifles. Ya must be on your way.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Now here be the Tumblebar. Keep it well, and use it as I told you.
keys.speaker: harldain

keys.dialogue: Stop! Stop please, all of you, and ponder this riddle...
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: A quest of love / Ends with me, / Yet I am made / Endlessly. / If I drop, / I say my name, / If I touch rock, / Freedom gain.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: What is the answer? Solve it, I beg you, and set me free!
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I simply cannot figure it out.
keys.speaker: jarial
keys.desc: spoken, at the end of his rope

keys.dialogue: Hmmm... something must touch the rock. But what?
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Something 'endlessly made.'
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Free me from this living tomb, and I will fight fearlessly at your side.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Ahhgh! Please! Come back soon! Free me from this living tomb, and I will fight fearlessly at your side.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Oh, you are the ones those scarred mages were talking about.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: You've probably seen them - the ones wearing red cloaks?
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: They mentioned a group of adventurers from New Phlan.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: They are newcomers. I'd never seen one until recently.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Exactly how recently, I can't tell you. I have a very poor sense of time.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: They asked if I had seen a group of adventurers from Phlan.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: But they had been cruel to me earlier, so I told them nothing.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Also, I did not like the look in their eye.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Perhaps the scarred mages found them after all.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Ozama is - was - my lover. We came to Myth Drannor together, adventuring.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Her conjuring was a sight to behold - so fluid and beautiful, with her violet eyes blazing.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: But she had a blinding temper. And so did I, at that time.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I was jealous of her skill. I said something very cruel...
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: ...and in return she spat out a spell and dropped a pebble at my feet. And the boulder grew around me.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Ozama spoke it, before she left me. Perhaps she meant it as a kindness, to give me a chance to free myself, but it has been nothing but torment.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: There is little more to tell. She continued adventuring, and I never saw her again.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Before she left, she spoke the riddle to me.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: You will say I am crazy, but I believe she intended to come back and release me.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I am afraid she is dead, and I mourn her.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Now, please, let us speak of something else.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: She went off to the northeast part of the Main Halls. We had talked to a friendly voice there, who called himself Preybelish.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: He had a necklace she thought she might buy.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: If it can be solved, I can be a free man again.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: And my sorcery will serve the clever soul who found the answer.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Oh, everything and everybody evil passes by here eventually.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Phaerrim and alhoon, beholders, orcs of course, margoyles and arraccat...
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: There was a dark naga who was fond of riddles. He and I actually became quite friendly for a while.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: The undead are the worst. Sometimes they claw at me for weeks.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Let this stone be a lesson to you - never scorn the love of a mage!
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I offended the wizard Ozama, and she gave me this stone prison in reply.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Ten hundred times I have wished Ozama dropped the stone on my head instead.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Yet, Ilmater help me, I love her still.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Oh, this cursed boulder protects me utterly. That's the evil genius of it.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I had a beholder try to kill me once. It threw spells for a week. What patience!
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: It shed tears when it finally had to give up.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Oh, the answer is not a word. I can assure you of that.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: I've been in this rock for many years. I've spoken every word there is, tried every spell I know.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: To solve the riddle, speaking isn't enough. You have to DO something, I'm sure of it.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Tell me, travelers, what news from Phlan?
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Well, that is dire news, and no mistake. I wish I could help you.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Zhentil Keep is where I grew up, and learned the wizard arts.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: But that is a long time ago. Now I think of myself as a citizen of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Aaaagh! What is the answer to Ozama's riddle? It's driving me mad.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Friends, I have said enough. Now it is up to you.
keys.speaker: jarial

keys.dialogue: Stop! Stop, stop please, and ponder this riddle...

keys.dialogue: See? It is as I told you. If they were Cult, they would not ask!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: You are right, Kellan. -Forgive us our wary ways, strangers. Since we came to Myth Drannor, we have met nothing but enemies.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: You asked about the Silver Fire. It is a Sisterhood dedicated to the dismay, downfall and destruction of the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: You asked about Sammaster. If you do not know him, you know his work - for it was he that betrayed Mystra's trust and founded the deadly Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: You wondered who we are. We are Sisters of the Silver Fire, devoted to the dismay, downfall and destruction of the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: We have reason to believe the Cult is brewing evil in Myth Drannor, and we have come to stop it.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: But our party was nearly destroyed, and we found our Shrine abandoned by its guardians -
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: - so we idle here, struggling to keep its flame alive while our enemy grows stronger by the hour.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: If the Cult knew where we were, you would be standing in a smoking ruin.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: We were sent to Myth Drannor by the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Seven of the Sisterhood of Silver Fire, to destroy a dracolich named Pelendralaar.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: There were twelve of us then.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: What the Sisterhood did not know is that Pelendralaar had been joined by a Cult mage of great power - I do not know her name.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: We found the Cult guarding a creature called the Baelnorn. We attempted to free him...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Thus to make us thirteen in number. That was ill-fated!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Many mages were there to oppose us. Our group was swept apart in a fury of magic, and I fear all the others have been destroyed.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Aye, we know where he is, only too well.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Much deeper in these catacombs, you will find great doors with an elven rune before them. The Baelnorn is somewhere beyond those doors, held in force by the Cult.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: But you can't get there now. The way is sealed with a Glyph...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: It is the Glyph of Safekeeping. I do not know the Word that unseals it.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Think carefully before you broach those doors! For such an affront is sure to arouse the full fury of the Cult.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: It must be a talisman of great power. Such a thing would be in the lair of some creature - if it has not already fallen into the hands of the Cult.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Since it is beloved of Mystra, we would gladly help you look for it - but we must stay here until its guardians return, or the Silver Fire will fail.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: We do not know who they may be. They were gone when we stumbled in here, and the Silver Fire nearly dead.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Because the flame was not dead, I think maybe they are still alive.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: So we are trapped very nicely! We cannot go and look for the guardians, for fear the Shrine will fail while we are gone!
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Yet neither can we stay here! This Shrine will not stand a minute against the black fury of the Cult.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: If you meet the guardians, or any of our Sisterhood, bid them return here to us! For we wish to make war on the Cult, as we came here to do...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: ...but we cannot, for we dare not leave this Shrine untended.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: That would explain how well equipped you are! Spoils from your war on those evildoers.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Would that we could go with you! Rather than languishing here.

keys.dialogue: If that is true, you will take me into your company!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Kellan! -You must forgive my companion. Her speech can be rough -
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Aye, because I grew up in the Cult, and their ways are not gentle -
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: But that is behind us now. It is true - she languishes here -
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Languish! Say rather I am going mad.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Take me into your company, and I will tell you about our enemy. For it is true - I walked with Dragon-love in my heart for years and years, and so I know their ways.

keys.dialogue: And now that it is restored, Kellan and I are free to resume our quest...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: ...to cleave through the Cult ranks, and banish Pelendralaar to the dead place reserved for his foul kind!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: If you will take one or both of us into your company, that is.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Ah, but the guardians have told us the tale already, of the seesawing battle and how you toppled the Skull.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: I wish I had been there! To swing a sword with you, and cleave naga necks, and cast the most hurtful spells I know.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: In a heartbeat! For our quest is the same as yours...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: ...to cleave through the Cult ranks, and banish Pelendralaar to the dead place reserved for his foul kind!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: We are Sisters of the Silver Fire! The most canny and fearsome adversaries of the Cult in Faerun! You dare much, to question our abilities!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Calmly, sister! You lash out, but no enemy is there.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Let me tell you about my sister Kellan. She is both fighter and sorcerer. She learned her skills in the Cult...
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: ...but now, her skills at summoning death and mayhem far exceed theirs. And her spirit I think you know by now.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: And Bronwyn! Dear Bronwyn. She is a ranger of great renown, skilled with sword and bow, and priest and healer in the bargain...
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: ...and I am proud to call her sister, and do whatever she may say.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: We thank you. Now our quest will not fail!
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Enough talk! Let's go.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Kellan and Bronwyn join your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You are wise. Greater numbers would draw unwanted attention. But if any of your company should falter...
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: ...or fall to the enemy, come seek us out here.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Now you best be on your way. Goodbye.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Which of us will you take with you?
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Later! You know not the Cult! There is no 'later'!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Kellan! -Forgive my sister. Her tongue is harsh, when she has no enemy to face.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: It is hard, but we will wait here. If you have need of companions, we are ready! Goodbye.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Ah! Farewell then, cruel sister. You leave me here to waste away!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: I will see you soon, dear Kellan.
keys.speaker: Bronwyn

keys.dialogue: Travelers, I am one of you now. Let us go.

keys.dialogue: Farewell then, sister - you must take care! For I will not be there to keep you from trouble.

keys.dialogue: Look at Bronwyn! Look at me! We are strong, and we are alive. We have come through dragonfire and black magic to be here. Will you not take us into your company?

keys.dialogue: Your loyalty to your companions is deep! I respect you for it.

keys.dialogue: I do not! Foolishness it seems to me, to prefer the dead to the living. But it is your choice.

keys.dialogue: Tolerate, yes. Respect, no! Foolishness it seems to me, not to accept aid so freely offered. But it is your choice, travelers.

keys.dialogue: Do you wish to take me into your company? Or do you want to talk about my life in the Cult?
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Ask, and I will answer you.
keys.speaker: kellan
keys.desc: spoken, reluctantly, she would prefer to act rather than talk

keys.dialogue: Weaknesses? They keep secrets from each other. When I was in the Cult, I never told anyone what I was doing. When I left the Cult, it took them a year to find out.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: So you can nibble at them for a while, if you are careful. Kill a mage here, a band there, and no one will know.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: But woe to you when at last they see you as the threat you are. Then you will see the Claw come down quick and hard!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: It is hard, if there are too many of them. If you can, cast spells to protect yourselves before the enemy is even in sight. And have wands and staves ready! Do not run short of magic!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Do not waste your time with spells that hold or fuddle the fighters. Their mages may undo them with a counterspell.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Be sure to hit the mages hard - if you let them cast a spell, all may be lost! Once the mages have fallen, then concentrate your fury on each fighter, one by one.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: We had many. We were careful to slaughter them every one, so no word would creep back that the Silver Fire was loose among them!
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: But then we stormed the gates where the Baelnorn was kept. That creature must be important to them, indeed! For many mages came down upon us unawares, and loosed fire and lightning, and so all was lost.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Have you ever seen a dragon? They are mighty! If so, you understand why the Cult would strive to increase the power of dragons, and then harness it for their own use.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: I was barely a woman when I first saw one. It killed and devoured most of the caravan I was traveling in, yet it spared me. Why?
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: The Cult convinced me it was my destiny to serve dragons. And so I believed for many years.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: But slowly I came to realize that Sammaster's teachings were mad, and that my destiny was not to bow to them, but to kill them and their evil. And so I left the Cult and become a humble servant of the Silver Fire.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: I am willing. You seem to be a good company.
keys.speaker: kellan

keys.dialogue: Come back to me with fewer in your company, and I will gladly fill out your number.

keys.dialogue: I am willing. You are a good company. Let the Cult beware!

keys.dialogue: Rest and heal here, whenever you need it, brave heroes. The Shrine of the Silver Fire will ever be in your debt.

keys.dialogue: Kill him. Take the staff. And stay far from me and mine.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Ha! I need no traps to rid the underearth of you. You're as like to kill each other, tripping over yourselves in the goddess' sweet darkness.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: You are nothing to me. Save this: kill the mage and clear my path.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: This would be trap enough to destroy you, should I wish it so.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: See for yourself. Take it. Cast its light upon the Freth. Watch them fry in its gaze.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: My reasons are my own. Agree or refuse. I tire of looking at you.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Hate is the song in my blood! It is all that lives in me now, the Freth have seen to that.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Because he keeps me from my prey! And from my death. That is the only joy left for me now, the Freth have seen to that.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: They lured us here with promises of glory. The Cult was to give us dominion over Myth Drannor. Titles. Riches.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Lies! We were the price the Freth paid for power! Our blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. Our souls sucked from living bodies!
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: You've seen my people - they're trapped between life and death. Slaves! Only I survive to free them.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Speak! Will you kill the mage?
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: What do you know of passion? Heat that drives life? The earth burns with it, and so do the hearts of my people.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Two hearts, joined, burn hottest. Is it the same with you in your pale beds? Are your mates of value to you?
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: The Cult has taken my mate. They have enslaved his soul. Darkness is no comfort to me now.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: I cannot restore his body to life, but I will free his soul to death. And my own soon after.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Can you understand this? I care not. Find the mage. Kill him. Agree to this and I will give you the bridge.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: If I free the souls of the Kilsek drow, their bodies can no longer serve the Cult.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Surely it is of use to you if the Cult's guards crumble suddenly to dust.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Find the mage. Destroy him. Claim the Staff. Clear my way to the Cult's nest. It is all of use to you.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Then go all the way north, then east, then south, then all the way west to find the stair. It is south of an arraccat warren - beware those fierce marauders! The Staff will do the Cult little good against you. Behold! The bridge is yours.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: But beware, sunwalkers, for the peace between us is brief. And fragile.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: That is well. I think what pleases you will be to kill this mage, and use his Staff upon the Freth. Have your bridge then.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: You have lost an opportunity, sunwalkers. Make your own way against the Cult, then.  Anesh. Belar... Z'han!
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Be quick then. Our enemies grow stronger by the second.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Prison disagrees with me - I grow forgetful. Release me and my memory may return.

keys.dialogue: Go then. What care I how your tale ends?

keys.dialogue: What I have learned will even the score. Open the door and I'll teach you what the dragonkin taught me.

keys.dialogue: What, do you doubt my resolve? You fear that outside of this cage I'll waste a breath taking your lives? The hate that sings through me is for the enemy we share.

keys.dialogue: Only the weak throw away knowledge for pride's sake.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Go then. They will come for me soon. Their dracolich craves the power in my blood. In death or undeath, I will join my mate soon enough.

keys.dialogue: Release me. I have learned much since last we met.

keys.dialogue: Little good it did me. Anesh and Belar are dead, their blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. And I am next.

keys.dialogue: You have seen my people in service to the Cult. Dead but not dead. The Cult have enslaved their souls.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Their spirits are trapped in a great urn inside the castle - a Soul Vessel.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Destroy the urn, and my kin will be freed to death. Kedar, my mate, will take his place in Lloth's web, and I will make quick to join him. The Kilsek drow will trouble you no more.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: I heard no particulars, only that it is vulnerable to a smashing weapon.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: They spoke of it in a great hall at the center of the castle, and laughed that it was guarded by those whose souls it held. I go to find it now.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: The Pool! Ssussan! I have seen it - in the great cavern beneath the castle. The Cult told us its touch would make us invulnerable to sunlight and give drow dominion over the surface world.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Ha! Hope dulls the sharp blade. The Pool's touch brought death, and worse. My mate... My kin... I saw it strip their souls from them.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: I left them there, at the Cult's mercy. For that I must answer to Lloth. But first, I'll return and end this.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: You flatter yourselves. I take aid where necessity dictates, but don't imagine I'll soil myself walking sword to sword with surface crawlers.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Let us say I must decline your generous offer.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Oh, it is I who thank you. And all the more so if you will keep far from me from now on.
keys.speaker: nathlil

keys.dialogue: Enough. The souls of my kin call to me. Lloth bless whichever of us lives to free her servants.
keys.speaker: nathlil

keys.dialogue: If I free the souls of the Kilsek drow, their bodies can no longer serve the Cult.
