keys.dialogue: Surely it is of use to you if the Cult's guards crumble suddenly to dust.

keys.dialogue: The dragonkin you slaughtered bear the key that opens this cage. Release me, and I will teach you what I learned.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Come now, release me. With a bit more breathing space I could tell you what I've learned. It is of use to both of us.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: Ssussan! You waste time - and that is precious to us now. Search the dragonkin, they bear the key to this cell.
keys.speaker: Nathlil

keys.dialogue: I may leave this life under a Cult blade, but I will not be bored to death by chattering surface dwellers. Release me or leave me to my fate.

keys.dialogue: But I suppose I do owe you a little something.

keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Now get on your way. Come back and see me if you got any gold to spend. I'll help lighten your load, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: There. That's done. Don't be askin' me to repeat it. Arh, you're gettin' a bargain - don't get used to it - it'll never happen again.

keys.dialogue: Bah, don't thank me. You can't fatten my purse if you're dead.

keys.dialogue: Plumb west of here, across the river. Just follow the orcs, heh heh.

keys.dialogue: Well now, you figured out the way to my heart, didn't you?

keys.dialogue: But you can't just GIVE it to me - where's the sport in that?

keys.dialogue: I'll get your money soon enough, heh heh. Come visit my shop later.

keys.dialogue: Ah yes. Sooner or later, everyone trades with Nottle, heh heh.

keys.dialogue: Ahhh, it's a tough life but a good one. Meet all kinds of creatures.

keys.dialogue: I've got my wits to live on, and my wagon - it's got so many blarsted spells on it, I'm amazed it don't just burst into flames someday.

keys.dialogue: Speaking of which...

keys.dialogue: ...you better go use that Word I taught you. Come back if you want to see my shop.

keys.dialogue: The Key of Dumathoin. Could you hurry? Prison makes me jumpy.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Oh, it's like that, is it? You're offering me the hard bargain?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Well, I won't do it. Shame on you.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Quite sure. You put a price on my freedom, and you'll regret it.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: I accept your apology. Now, by the rage of the Broken God, open that door.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: My freedom in exchange for information? Sure, heh heh. Just open the door.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: I say, shame. To take advantage of someone who's in a bad spot.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: A real bad spot.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Bah! You're trying to scare me into making a bad deal. That'll never work.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: All right! You win, curse you! Open the door, and I'll give you something you urgently need.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. You'll be back, key in hand.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Aaah - can you smell it? The air is fresher out here. The smell of freedom!
keys.speaker: nottle
keys.desc: spoken - he's just been released from prison

keys.dialogue: Did I tell you how much I hate cages? And only a fiend's cage can keep hold of me, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Again I find myself in your debt! Bah! If I tell you something interesting, that will make us even, eh?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Here, as I promised, I give you something you urgently need: a lesson in manners.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Now we're even, heh heh.
keys.speaker: Nottle
keys.desc: spoken, LOCALIZERS please put a 3 second silent pause before the start of this line

keys.dialogue: Now I keep my promise - I'll tell you something I learned from the mages.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: I gotta get back to my wagon, so I'll rattle through this quick. If I told you I heard rumors of a treasure, a great treasure, are you interested?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Well then, you'll want to seek out the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves. One of the most fabulous treasures in all Faerun!
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: And it's probably less than a thousand steps from where we are right now - as the worm crawls, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: 'Course, lots o' people been searching for it ever since the Wars. Nobody found even a single gem. But maybe you'll get lucky, eh?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Those mages talked about something called the Helm Cleaver. It sounds powerful, eh?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: They said they had to show it to some orogs, and so it was being brought to the Dragon Room. Wherever that is. House o' Gems, maybe?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Those mages whispered in fear about a black room, haunted by shadows. Somewheres nearby, I think.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Which is interesting, because a long time ago I hears that something called the Mountain Fist was lost to a murder of shadows.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Those mages lost a few of their pals to a den of arraccat nearby. They hate arraccat, and by the Black Hand, so do I! Hiding in shadows is no good with those bug-eyed beasts.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: You run into arraccat? Big, ugly, spider-looking beasts? You will, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: The mages were whining about all the treasure their friends were carrying. Many jewels and much gold, and magic items too, I believe they said.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: And if you should find a pair of Gauntlets there, bring them to me at my wagon! I'll give you a fair price for them, oh yes, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Right-o. Now, if I told you I heard rumors of an ally for you, someone who might join your party and fight by your side, are you interested?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: I heard tell of a rogue around these parts - a thief of great skill, if somewhat lacking in judgment, heh heh. I'll find out what it takes to acquire his services.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: The mages gabbled about some intruders they caught - people they called the Silver Fire. But I guess not all of them got killed. Some are still loose, causing trouble, heh heh.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: A long time ago, someone told me about a man in a wight's barrow. But he wasn't dead - cold and stiff, but not dead.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: I believe the mages might have another prisoner!
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: They said he had to go up to the upper floors of this dungeon. Something about a skeleton's arm? Didn't make much sense.
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Finally - if I told you about some barstly strong magic things, such as the Inferno Knife and the Spell Chain of Sarg, are you interested?
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Good! Because I'm hopin' you'll find 'em and sell 'em to me at my wagon. I'll be seeing you...
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.dialogue: Farewell. Hope you find lots of treasure, heh heh. See you at my wagon!
keys.speaker: nottle

keys.speaker: nottle
keys.desc: spoken, loudly, to attract attention, signaling the party to attack

keys.dialogue: Ahhh, go'wan, plague someone else.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Come on now, show mercy on old Nottle.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ah, I always knew you could do it, to wreck the Cult and tumble the dracolich down to the Forgotten Place.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: I always knew you COULD do it, but was never sure you WOULD. Took you long enough, heh heh.

keys.dialogue: In this cave, a dense mortar of sand and clay has been used to cement together a wall of odd-shaped stones.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is set back from the entrance, and doesn't quite reach all the way to the ceiling.  An old, earthy odor flows down from the small opening at the top.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The wall is unyielding to pressure, but appears designed to be pushed out from the other side.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your dwarf nods at the crude, but sturdy, stonework, commenting that pushing against the wall would be fruitless, since it is well supported from the other side.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your ranger inspects the patterns of the deep tracks in the dried mud at the base of the structure, and concludes that large, booted humanoids built the wall within the last few seasons.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This cave entrance is blocked by a rock wall which cannot be pushed in or smashed from this side.

keys.dialogue: Tarry a moment, favored of Shaundakul! Speak to me, and I will tell you of the places I have seen in Myth Drannor...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: ...and tales I have heard of the City Heights, and the dungeons underneath it, and of the Hall of Wizards, and the Catacombs deep below that famous ruin.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Welcome back, Wind Riders! Ask me more about our city.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken, proud to be of service

keys.dialogue: I am glad you have returned. I heard a rumor, and feared greatly for your safety.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Welcome back! The whispering winds told me you were returning, and other things besides.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I am glad to see that Beshaba has not yet kissed you. I pray she ever fails!
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken, concerned; Beshaba is the goddess of ill fortune

keys.dialogue: Travellers - I welcome you back. I have had some work to do - defending my shrine!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Tymora be praised - for if we survive this, it will be luck indeed - by luck and by grace of the Wind Rider.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: That the Cult of the Dragon had learned of you, and realized their peril, and laid a deadly trap for you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Thank the gods that rumor was false!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Beshaba is the Maid of Misfortune! How fortunate you are, never to have received a kiss from Tyche's Unpleasant Daughter.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: For those that feel her kiss regret it to the end of their days.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Some dragon-like creatures, ugly beasts, with spellflingers of the Cult behind them. But the Wind Rider taught them how to fly, ha ha ha!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travellers, I have news for you! I met someone who roams about the city - one of your kind.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travellers! I have heard a voice, crying on the wind.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Welcome back! The breeze blows strong - yet tales of your victories outfly it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travellers! What know you of the Silver Fire? A tale has come to me about them.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I tell you true - it has been hard, these last hours. Never before has the Helping Hand been so hard pressed.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: He was a trifle, little more than a gutter thief, but yet - he had a quick wit and a steady eye. He said his name was Tudo.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: It was a woman's voice, gentle yet strong - an elf high-born of a noble House, or I have never met one.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: 'The Mythal shall be free,' she said, and I believed her.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: 'My skull,' she said, 'where have they taken my skull?' And I wept to hear the pain in her voice.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: 'Mystra,' she cried, 'where are your children? I call, but none come.' And I wept to hear the pain in her voice.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: She sobbed for Mystra, the goddess of magic! I felt my heart would break, and called to her, but she did not answer, and went away wailing to the southwest.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: An eblis I know told me that twelve beings came into Myth Drannor from the South. He said they were 'Silver Fire,' but I do not know what that means.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Not that it matters. For the eblis also told me that a dead dragon found them and breathed upon them, and they all died.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The Cult of the Dragon. They came in force, and I tell you true, I would have perished, but they heard some dark call and vanished again, as suddenly as they came.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Dark nagas - four of them. They harried me, but their puny god is no match for the Wind Rider! They slunk away to the south.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travellers! Far and wide, the wind gloats over your sharp victories against the Cult of the Dragon.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Talk with me, travellers! I may know a tale or two of great use to you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I will tell you what I know of the city, and where helpful treasures might be found.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ask me what you will, O Favored of the Wind Rider. For evil yet lives in dark corners of our city, and it scoffs at your great victory.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Well, travellers! Every breeze whispers new tales of your exploits!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Favored Ones - welcome back to the Shrine of Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I see the Winds of Fortune have blown you back to me.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: What tale may I tell you this time?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The mistral winds told me you would return.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Do you seek more tales, travellers?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: See, you return, with the Helpful Hand ever at your back.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ill news, travellers! I have no more tales for you... until the mistral winds brings me more.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I can think of no more tales to tell you right now.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Now, travellers, no more tales. You must be on your way.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have told you every tale I know.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I was down in the Dungeons a fortnight ago, and I heard something strange - the sound of a jailer on his rounds, jingling his keys.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I tried to locate him, but in vain! He was behind a wall, and I could not find a crack in it big enough to slip through.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Down in the Main Halls it was, south of the round room where the Ormyrr keeps his orc prisoners.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Here is a story. A mongrelman came through here, laden with a knapsack, and rested a time at this shrine.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: His kind often say little, and he was no different. But he did mention he was on his way into the Dungeons, to the Main Halls.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: When he took up his knapsack, I saw what was inside. Necklaces - dozens of them.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: O travelers, on your journeys, have you ever found the Man in the Stone?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have never seen him, but many who stay at my shrine swear he exists, somewhere in the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: From the waist up, he is a man. But from the waist down, he is a boulder! How he lives, how he eats - that is a riddle no one has been able to solve.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Here is a tale that concerns the Dungeons. It happened to me many years ago.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Some servants of a phaerrim came to molest Lord Shaundakul's shrine. Human they had been once, although they were no longer. And the leader of them wore a great golden arc around its neck - a magnificent Torc.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I killed that human, and many of the others. But when I came to reclaim the Torc, it was gone. I can only think that someone took it back down into the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I heard a tale from one of the lizardfolk, just before I killed him.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: He spoke of a magical Gate, which dropped foul-tasting undead creatures into the Dungeons as steadily as rainwater drips off a sattern leaf.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The lizard swore that the humans of the Cult of the Dragon created this Gate. But I believe his master, Malgi Hi, actually brought it forth.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I am wondering if, in your travels, you have come upon any talking books?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I heard some orogs talking about some books such as that. Apparently these books wield such power that the orogs could not open them!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But I also heard the orogs say they were evil books, and so I fear they must be destroyed somehow.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: When I was banished from my shrine, some of the lizardfolk were taunting me - from a safe distance, you may be sure.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They claimed they held 'the secret waters of life.' And when I struck the arm from one of them, he ran back into the Dungeons, bawling for the Waters to restore him.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I warn you, beware the arraccat! Especially down in the lowest levels of the Dungeons...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: ...many a cocksure traveler has been taken by them, and his possessions added to the growing heap of treasures that feather the arraccat nest.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Here is a tale my mother told me. Once a mighty warrior strode into our city, wielding a mighty club - the Mountain Fist!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: He cast fear into the hearts of all, for he did not care whom he killed. If there was a challenge, or treasure that we wanted, he pursued and won it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But such arrogance rarely lives for long, and he was no exception. Deep underground, a chill of spirits overtook him, and drained his life, and now his name is forgotten even to himself.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Shall I tell you of the Earthborn Wind? It was a gift of Shaundakul to the dwarves of Myth Drannor...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: ...mysterious breezes to keep the city's underground air fresh and healthful. A Rillstone Ruby was at its heart, and Juliban Genshihir its last caretaker.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Alas for us! The breezes stopped centuries ago, when Juliban died, and the Dungeons became an unhealthy place.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Several orogs came to me, seeking refuge. I was sorry to send them away, but they were brought here by the Cult, and I did not trust them.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They told me they had been driven out of the Catacombs by the drow, who also took from them all their treasures - weapons, armor, and an old bone relic or two.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have been into the Catacombs many times - through cracks and crawl-holes. I do not know of a way in for those of your kind.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Adventurers do get in somehow, from time to time... but when they do, the evil denizens of the Catacombs are quick to seal the entrances behind them. In particular, watch out for the dark nagas, the margoyles, and the plentiful undead.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: O travelers, you have probably seen for yourselves the many once-splendid wells and fountains which the dwarves crafted throughout Myth Drannor...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have seen for myself that not all of them are destroyed - in the deeper Catacombs especially, there are those that still brim with blessing waters.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But beware! For some seem fair, yet are foul beneath the surface, and trap the unwary.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Why, surely you know of the Baelnorn, the protector of old, who dwells deep in the Catacombs?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: He has been here since the city's Fall. But he comes forth less and less often. My grandmother saw him, but my mother has not, nor have I.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ah! The Hall of Wizards is one of the great buildings of Myth Drannor. Surely you have seen it, revered of Shaundakul? It is in the shape of a great dragon, embracing a great Egg.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Even today it is the center of magic for Myth Drannor, although that magic has lost its purpose and drifted away from the wishes of those who summoned it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Much magic lives in the Hall of Wizards still, and I am reluctant to enter - although I have grown attached to Caalenfaire, and his companion Volun, who sometimes appear there.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Have you seen the Orrery in the Hall of Wizards? An orrery is a device to track the positions of the planets...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: ...although it always seemed strange to me, to build such a grand device to do something so simple. If you wish to know the positions of the planets, why not look up into the sky?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Sadly, the Orrery no longer functions. Some of the Stones that were its planets have long been missing, although I saw the Blue Planet not long ago, in the hands of other travelers of your kind.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There are many passages near the Hall of Wizards. Is it true that wizards of your kind are not fond of walking?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Inside the Hall of Wizards is the Rhonglyn, a device that moves from floor to floor in the Dungeons. Right outside is the Spire of Mythanthor, which now opens the way again into the Dungeons, thanks to you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: In the amphitheatre is the Circle of Ualair, which I see has been opened! I suppose that is also your doing? The Wind Rider thanks you for that - he loves to open what was shut, and let the wind do its work.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: In the center of the amphitheatre is the Circle of Ualair, which led into the Catacombs under the castle, once upon a time. Those were more peaceful days.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ah, the Castle, do not go there! For years after the city fell, the Castle repelled evil invaders. Dwarf, elf and gnome had conspired to create many a trap for them... barricades... silent guardians...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But over the centuries, these ancient defenses wore out. I do not know if any remain. Now dark things nest in the aeries and strongrooms of Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Favored ones! Shaundakul's bright wind has swirled all around Castle Cormanthor. In vain has it looked for a way for you to enter there.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The ones who hold it have closed up every entrance, save the one in the aerie where the dragon-kin come in and out.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Oh, Hand of Beshaba! I have dire news about that place. For once again the great dracolich Pelendralaar has been seen to leave the Castle, and go to hunt again among the ruins of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: He and his minions have already searched out all the powerful creatures of the city. Phaerrim, alhoon, clutch of baatezu - it mattered not, he drove them all from the city, or sent them smoking to their deaths...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But now it seems he searches for someone else. If you approach the Castle in the open air, beware!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Listen! For I heard a tale from a passing Ormyrr. She said she has seen all manner of creatures come up from deep underground - driven out into the light by the Cult.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The creatures told the Ormyrr that the Cult has sealed the underground approaches to the Castle. They do not use passageways, you see - they create magical gates, and use those to get from stronghold to stronghold.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Here is an alarming thing - something has tainted the city's water!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ever since I have lived here, the water has been pure and wonderful to drink. I think maybe a guardian of some kind watches over it - I imagined sometimes I heard someone singing.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But of late the water has been foul, and the city fountains burble no more. Woe to the dwarves, that their great waterworks should fail at last after so long a service.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Now here is a thing. Orogs approached me - respectful of my fangs, you may be sure!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They wished me to help them recover a thing called the Helm Cleaver. But what use is such a thing for me? I snapped at them and sent them running, back into the House of Gems.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: As you walk near the Hall of Wizards, beware of gargoyles! They delight in ambushes here, flying low and swooping up to appear without warning.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I wish I still had the Stone Mouth. Have you heard of it? It is a stone that enables you to understand the speech of gargoyles and margoyles.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: It was helpful in dealing with them and frustrating their attacks. But the Stone Mouth was stolen from my shrine many years ago.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: To the east of here, you might find a barrow, if it has not collapsed or been sealed.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There is a weapon there, such as your kind like to use, enchanted with a warrior's voice. Pay heed to its warning! That is all I can tell you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: East of here, there is a garden, with a patch of dark-stained earth. Approach it carefully, travelers! For that is Thirsty Ground.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Once it was a beautiful garden that gave comfort to those who watered it with their tears. But the Weeping Wars changed it forever, as wars do.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: It may aid you if your need is dire - if you have been touched by wraiths, or kissed by spectres, or fallen under a curse, or if there are many dead among you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But beware! For the payment it seeks is your bloodlife itself, and it does not sip daintily.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: East of here, you will find the great Ear of the City. It is a Pillar beloved of Shaundakul, that listens to the voices on the wind, and remembers what they say.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But it is hard to get to, for beasts surround the Pillar, and strive to drown it out with their grumbling voices and shrieking cries. And of late they have grown very strong.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Have you looked in the Scrying Mirror, there in the Hall of Wizards?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: If you do, it will show you things far away, things that are close to your heart or hanging like a sword over your life, even if you know it not.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Away to the southwest, you will find the lizardfolk village. Beware! They relish all humankind as food. Yet they themselves are not very good eating.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Once they were a friendly people - or at least not openly enemies of good. But they have a leader now, strong in magic, who styles himself Malgi Hi.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Malgi Hi has raised a great idol, and put a stone, bound in iron, in place as its one fiery eye. And under its influence the lizards seem to grow in cruelty and cunning.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Here is a sad story! Not so long ago, pilgrims of Mystra flocked to the area to the southwest, where the beautiful Shrine to Mystra stood, once upon a time.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They came here because a ghost of the shrine would sometimes appear where the building once stood. So the splendor of the shrine was not totally lost!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But the area grew more dangerous, and the pilgrims stopped coming. So the shrine faded. Now a foul Spawn Pool has risen on the spot, guarded by my dark brethren.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There is little I can tell you about the stone idol, abandoned in the ruins to the southwest. Whatever purpose it may hold is of no use to nagas.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Maybe you can ask the ormyrrs about that area. I have seen them linger at the idol, and Nottle as well. They may know more about it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I am worried about the Ormyrrs. Have you met them? They live away in the marshes to the southeast.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They have been friendly to travelers - and Shaundakul smiles on such creatures, and blesses them, even if they worship him not.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But lately I heard a rumor that they no longer follow this path - indeed, that they took up arms against some sojourning alaghi, and killed them. And friendly breezes no longer blow to me from the southeast.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Listen, travelers! Turn your hearts toward the House of Gems to the east. Too long has it been silent and neglected, the gathering-place of dust and cobwebs.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travelers, enough talk about this place and that. The Guiding Wind blows eastward. Let your feet follow the breath of Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Enough, Favored of the Wind Rider! I have talked with you long enough. You seek the Wizard's Torc, or so the winds have whispered to me...
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: ...but you will not find it by trading tales with me. Be on your way!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I know no more about that area. But I do know that your steps need to lead into the Catacombs. Go now - with the Wind Rider ever at your back.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: That is enough talk! I have places to go. And you - your steps lead again to the Catacombs, or I am a fool. Now, be on your way!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travelers, I should not say more. These matters are deep, beyond my simple devotion. Go talk to the ghost of Anorrweyn Evensong! She can help you when I cannot.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Beloved ones! Suddenly I realize where you should go. To the roof of the Speculum! There is a gate at the dragon's foot, it should not be hard to get there. Now, off with you!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Now, enough talk! You must find the Pool, and destroy it... you have a long way to go. May Shaunakul's blessing go with you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: That is all I know about the Dungeons, O Favored Ones.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: That is all I can tell you for now, about city places up on the surface.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But travelers, that is all I know about the Wizards' Hall.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I can tell you no more about the Catacombs. Maybe later, I will know more.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have told you all I know about the upper reaches of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There is little more to say about the deep Catacombs - except that it is a mysterious place, and dangerous.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have nothing more to tell you about the Castle - but I will try to find out more.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have told you everything I know about the other places of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: You need not worry about the Dungeons. Your thoughts must go back to Castle Cormanthor, and your destiny.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Worry not about the Catacombs! Your path winds back to Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: No more talk about the Castle! The enemy awaits you there - what else do you need to know?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Travelers, enough tales! You must be on your way, back to the Castle.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I have told you all the dungeon tales I know.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Favored Ones, I have already told you all the catacomb tales I know.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Wind Travelers, you've heard all I know about the City Heights.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: You've heard every tale I know about them.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Journey with care, travellers. Come back, if ever you need the Helping Hand.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Fare you well, until again I may trade tales with you, in the name of the Wind Rider.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. Shaundakul goes with you!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Goodbye.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Walk with his Hand on you, until we meet again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Goodbye, Favored of the Wind Rider!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Hold! In the name of all that is light! My need is dire. Will you rise to aid me?
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: You who wear the blood of the dark naga, I beg you - help me drive out evil from my home!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Orcs despoil my home, the temple of Lord Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I was hunting in the ruins - the lizardfolk are fat this time of year. When I returned, the orc filth had overrun my shrine. They raised an idol to Gruumsh on my Lord's altar and frolicked before it!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Sssss! My fangs dripped at the sight! I coiled to strike, but a pool of ichor bubbled up out of the ground before me. Its scent is pure evil. Hungry. Unslakable. It drew my strength from me like water from a well.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The pool basks in the orcs' foulness. While it thrives there, I am helpless to destroy them!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The orcs' sacrilege spawned the pool. It feeds on the abomination that their idol brings to that sacred place.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: If the idol is destroyed, the balance of good will be restored. The spawning pool must seep back from whence it came.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I am Odelinde, guardian naga and priestess of Shaundakul the Wind Rider. My family has watched over his temple for generations.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: My mother, her mother before her, and so on down the centuries, all of us dedicated to the Helping Hand. And I am the last. I cannot fail them!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Shaundakul is He who reaches out to adventurers in need. But now it is He who is in need, and I who must reach out to you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Orc corpses are like to yield some plunder, but when his temple is restored, Shaundakul's gifts will be more use to travelers than mere gold.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: To the north and west, in a circle of columns that lies open to the wind. Hurry, I implore you!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: To the west, in a circle of columns that lies open to the wind. Hurry, I implore you!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: My fangs only strike at the enemies of good. It is the way of my kind.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire is known to me. If he looked up from his divinations to speak my name to you, your cause must be great indeed.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But it is my Lord who aids, I am only his Hand. And aid is lost to us while his temple is fouled.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: My mother told me tales of this dwarf lord, when I was wet from the egg.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But what use are ghosts now? My Lord needs flesh, bone, and steel to rid his temple of this desecration!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I reach out to you in need, travelers.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Help me to cleanse my home of Gruumsh's filth and the hand of the Wind Rider will be opened to you. His gifts are great aid to adventurers in this harsh place.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: While the orc idol squats on my Lord's altar, the spawn pool keeps me at bay.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Go where the wind takes you, then. If it brings you this way again, look for me at Lord Shaundakul's shrine.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There I will strive to destroy the abomination that fouls it, so I can return to His work once again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Your courage has restored my Lord's temple. May you be refreshed and replenished, Favored of Shaundakul.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: Spoken, grateful for your help, she casts a spell

keys.dialogue: The naga's spell rests and heals the party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The spawn pool has retreated for now, but I must stay vigilant against its return. I have seen its kind in the ruins to the south: once they have broken ground, they seek to rise again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The Mythal once helped to keep such things at bay. But our guardian spell is changed of late. Even the blueglow moss sickens and dies.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I am Odelinde, guardian naga and priestess of Shaundakul the Wind Rider. My family has watched over his temple for generations.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Caalenfaire! If he has looked up from his divinations to speak with you, your fate must be quickwoven indeed. Only the most powerful of destinies command his interest. Where I can aid you I will.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Can it be? When I was a hatchling, my grandmother sang a song about a Pool of Radiance. The Pool that promises eternal life... But these spawn pools bring only death.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There's an old entrance to the dwarven dungeons just west of here. They must have crawled up from there.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: I was off hunting when they infested my shrine.  By the time I returned, they had raised their idol and the spawn pool had bubbled up to bask in the sacrilege. Its loathsome emanations kept me from slaughtering the orcs.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Be assured I'll be waiting if they come this way again. Orc gut is not so sweet as lizard flesh, but it suffices.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Harldain has been dead for centuries. But even now, he is not free to abandon his caretaking. Some curse or misfortune binds him to this city.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: His spirit still haunts the House of Gems, to the east and north of here. Be wary if you seek him there. Its traps and secret perils keep most living creatures from venturing inside.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: It is an ancient benison from the Mythal. When it thrives, the blueglow moss has healing properties. Gather it wherever you may find it and use it like a balm on your wounds.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Abomination and newly hatched evil draws them like a seedling to sunlight. Destroy the evil and the pool retreats.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But the pools are just symptoms of a greater ill. Like the orc incursions and the withering of the blue glow moss. Something has taken hold of the Mythal, or none of these evils would be possible.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: If the Mythal could be restored, it would shield us again. But that lore is beyond me.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: In my great-great-grandmother's time, the Mythal was a shield over the city. But its guardianship deteriorates as the centuries pass.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Of late its powers seem reversed. Harming where once it helped. As if a dark hand shapes it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The great mage Mythanthor cast the Mythal in the Year of the Soaring Stars, with the mages of the Coronal's high court.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The songs say that he gave his life in the casting of it, sacrificing himself so that elf, dwarf, and human might live together in peace under its protective shield.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Its blessings were wondrous then, if you believe the tales - flight, everlight, near immortality. But its powers have faded since the city fell to ruin.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The guardian spell had its own protectors once, souls dedicated to its upkeep and lore. In my mother's time, one still roamed the city as a spirit.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: She was elven, clad in the robes of the devotees of Mystra. My mother called her Anorrweyn Evensong.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Anorrweyn lost her life in the Weeping Wars, defending her shrine when the nycaloths sent walls of living fire through the city.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The shrine and she both fell, but through her will - or Mystra's - both returned as ghost-selves to haunt the site in the Nightingale Court where they once stood.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Servants of Mystery visited her there in decades past, but I have not seen her for many moltings. She may have faded. Spirits sometimes do.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Myth Drannor is as full of riches as it is of danger.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: They say the House of Gems, to the east and north of here, holds wealth beyond imagining. Although none have survived its perils long enough to confirm the tale.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: It is rumored that to the east of here, in the Dwarven ruins, riches lies hidden beneath the earth, awaiting the right footfall.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: There is a column to the east and south of here that whispers secrets carried on the wind. I used to go there often, for as Shaundakul knows, it tells marvelous tales!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The private garden of Fiona Casilltenirra, the elven vampiress, lies fallow to the east. If you are willing to pay a dark price, the very earth there can grant powerful boons.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Beyond the stronghold of the lizardfolk in the Nightingale Court, you may find a silent stone oracle, awaiting offerings. They say its potions and the ink of its scrolls were made from crushed ioun stones, in the desperate times of the Weeping Wars.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: The gargoyles hide much in their skytop aeries. But who can understand their gibberish? The mages of the Speculum once had a perverse amulet, called the Stone Mouth, with which they could decipher the gargoyle tongue.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But plunder enriches only the pocket. It is noble deeds and service that enrich the heart.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: May the wind be at your back, Favored of Shaundakul. I shall guard this temple while I can.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Return here whenever you like. I have tales for you, and Shaundakul's blessings if you are in need.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: But we have talked overlong. Adventure calls you. Answer it.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Ask her who and what she is
keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Tell her Caalenfaire sent you to ask her aid

keys.speaker: Protagonist

keys.dialogue: Welcome back to the Shrine of Shaundakul...
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: (Text Change) KE 4-24-01 spoken, kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

keys.dialogue: ...if your journeys wear upon you, come here, and feel the healing touch of the Wind Rider's hand.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken,  kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

keys.dialogue: ...what pain your journeys have given you, are removed by a touch of the Helpful Hand.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken,  kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

keys.dialogue: ...now feel the healing touch of the Wind Rider's hand.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken,  kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

keys.dialogue: Welcome back to the Shrine of Shaundakul, the Wind Rider.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken, kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

keys.dialogue: Now travellers, be refreshed by the Helping Hand.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Let Shaundakul, protector of travellers, make your burdens light again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Behold - the blessing of the Helpful Hand!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Again Shaundakul will touch you, and make your way easy again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Behold, travellers - the Wind Rider's blessing!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: You are the Favored!  The heroes who have rescued Myth Drannor!  My lord Shaundakul sings your deeds upon the wind!
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Favored of Shaundakul!  The wind sings with the tales of your victory!  The Mage Mordrayn is fallen, Pelendralaar is dust.  SSSsssssssss!  You have brought triumph to the city once again.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: May you be refreshed and restored, heroes of Myth Drannor.  The Wind Rider's blessing is upon you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde
keys.desc: spoken, administering a blessing, then a goodbye

keys.dialogue: The Wind Rider's blessing is upon you, heroes.  When you need healing, return to his shrine and let his servant refresh you.
keys.speaker: Odelinde

keys.dialogue: Leg-people! You go down, yes, Ormyrrs see you go down to the big stone place. Tell me where you go.

keys.dialogue: Hulu, the bad ones, yes, the bad ones try to find you. Tell Ormyrrs where you been - Ormyrrs stop the bad ones, yes yes!

keys.dialogue: Hulu, bad ones, bad ones look all places for leg-walking friends.
keys.speaker: Flem

keys.dialogue: Hulu ulaa, leg-walkers! You go big stone place, you come out, we salute the leg-walkers, yes! Where you go now?

keys.dialogue: Hulu, you walk well, you walk many places, where you walk now?

keys.dialogue: Hulu, you back, tell Flem what place you been, yes.

keys.dialogue: Dust, dirt, you smell of deep earth, yes. Where you been, leg-walkers?

keys.dialogue: I know tales, tales from places, yes. What place you come from, O leg-walking people?

keys.dialogue: You walk in earth, yes, earth speaks of places you been, blood you spill, yes.

keys.dialogue: You return, you tell Flem place you been, yes?

keys.dialogue: Huttu, see, your journey, dirt of your journey deep upon you, yes. Where you been, leg-walkers? Tell where dirt you wear comes from.

keys.dialogue: Here it is - the Pool of Radiance lies at your feet. It is quiet, but you immediately sense its enormous power.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It occurs to you that with this power, you could utterly destroy Kya Mordrayn and Pelendralaar.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The power of the Pool is great and ever growing. Once Kya and Pelendralaar are dust, you could continue to use the energy it channels...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...to root out the cells and cadres of the Cult of the Dragon all over Faerun, for example, and end their evil forever.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You realize that when you gain control of the Pool, you could make Kya's lies to the Baelnorn into truth. With the Pool behind you, you could drive all the evil things out of Myth Drannor...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...and make the city live again in glory. All Faerun would honor you!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Taking control of the Pool will be easy. Keeping control will be harder. Many in Faerun will seek to wrest its power from you...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But you realize it will be easy to fashion a trap for these fools. You can use the power of the Pool itself as bait. Mesmerized by it, your enemies will be easy prey...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You rouse yourself from your thoughts, as if from a deep slumber - to find you are not alone.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You brush aside the Pool's ensnaring spell, as a bear brushes aside cobwebs. You've escaped a cleverly laid trap!

keys.dialogue: With a whisper of footfalls the ghosts disappear, across the bridge that once stood here, into the warrens of Castle Cormanthor's deepest refuge.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But the ancient defenses failed, and the Army of Darkness invaded the refuge and collapsed its halls. Of the people who sought haven here, only the nameless ghosts remain.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The hundreds of ghosts are now thousands. With rising urgency they fling aside weapons and possessions, and press northward toward the illusion of safe haven.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You suddenly become aware of a presence. The spirit of an elf mage stands here, peering into the darkness of time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: She pays no notice to you or what you carry. She waits still for someone or something that may never come.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You become aware of a presence. The spirit of an elf mage stands here, peering into the darkness of time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Suddenly she also becomes aware of you. 'The Stone!' she seems to say. 'The defenses. All is not lost.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: She turns and disappears to the west.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Again the spirit of an elf mage appears, peering into the darkness. But now she also perceives you and what you carry.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: 'The Stone!' she says, wordlessly. 'The defenses. All is not lost.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: She turns and disappears to the west.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The ghost still stands here, intently waiting for something.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Suddenly you feel the presence of ghosts - hundreds of them. The shades of men, women and children flow around you like a river. Murmuring in dismay, they hurry off to the north.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Kya Mordrayn's passing tears a hole in the web of spells protecting the Pool of Radiance.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: That gives Anorrweyn Evensong a moment to wield the power of the Mythal.

keys.dialogue: Listen, O listen you mortals, you who washed away the poison, listen to the song of the waters.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Listen, O listen you mortals, you who washed away the poisonous Pool, listen to the song of the waters.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: My name - my name - it would take you a year to say my name, and you would say it badly, and have to say it again. Call me Plinshree.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: As to what I am - why, I am the spirit of this place. A naiad, as your kind call us. My soul smiled here out of the first rainfall, and I was ancient long before the first tree grew.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But listen - listen - are you listening to the song?
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: No, no! Do you not hear it? The song is off. Three of the waterbells are missing.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Ahh, I am laughing, you try not to hear the water song - yet it sings inside of you! Your mortal blood, sighing in your veins, makes the same song.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But do you not hear it? The song is off. Three of the waterbells are missing.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: They are shapely things, made of bone and shell, and hollowed out by sand and sea.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: In the air, they are silent. But put them in the water, and they sing!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Two the serpents took, and locked away behind the Sign of Water. The last the foulers took, the dragon-lovers, after they poisoned the water.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Then give it into a city well or fountain. Return any waterbell to the water, and it will ring! I will hear it, and come to reward you.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Then give them into a city well or fountain. Return the waterbells to the water, and I will reward you.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: For I have treasures to trade for them, things given to my keeping in the dark time, when Fire boiled the waters and the city died.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Yes, it is - for people of your kind. For if the song of water falters, then what waits ahead for you? Thirst and sand, floods and drowning, blood turning to dust...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But I care not what happens to you, you who are here one moment, gone the next. I care about my song, that is all, that is enough.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: I want the waterbells back! I have treasures to trade for them, things given to my keeping in the dark time, when Fire boiled the waters and the city died.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: If you find one of the three, give it into a city well or fountain. Return it to the water, and it will ring! I will hear it, and come to reward you.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Because silence - even a moment of it - lasts a lifetime. And music - even a year of it lasts but a moment. The waterbells make a gift of the centuries.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Oh, I do not oppose them. Why would I bother? Puny mortals, they will be dust in a moment...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: ...but even if they were creatures of living flame, or tall as mountains, eventually the rain would quench their fire, and water would tumble their bones down to the Sea.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Foolish mortals! You ask for your own downfall. One glimpse, and you will join those who sail the seas, seeking, seeking...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Seeking what? To become a creature of the water once again. To drown in my beauty.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Oh, they are such things as your kind seems to delight in - slivers of metal, and eggs of glass...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Though why you treasure such bitter and tasteless things is beyond my understanding. They seem as burdens to me, not worth the smallest part of a song.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Help? I will do more than that! I will defeat them!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: For even if they be creatures of living flame, or tall as mountains, rain will quench their fire in time, and water will tumble their bones down to the Sea.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But enough of this! Before I stopped to talk, I swam, yes, and I sang, so beautifully that aah! my heart aches just to remember it.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Maybe you think I waste my time, you who think 'struggle, struggle.' But think on this: What evil can stand up to the Sea?
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Mark my words, if you truly oppose evil, you will learn to swim and sing. Goodbye!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Ahhh, I am laughing, you are telling the wind to leave you alone, and the rain not to fall!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Yes, it is goodbye - for you and people of your kind. For if the song of water falters, then what is ahead for you? Thirst and sand, floods and drowning, blood turning to dust...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: I care nothing for your kind - here one moment, gone the next. But I want the waterbells back. Find them and return them to the waters, and I may reward you.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Otherwise, fear death by water! For evil and good, the mighty and the low - all you mortals are the same, once you enter the whirlpool.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Listen, now: in your travels you may find a waterbell, worthless to you maybe, if beauty counts for nothing.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Do not cast it aside! Give the waterbell unto the water, drop it into one of the city's wells! And maybe we will talk again about the music of the waters.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Then will I swim, yes, swim even more beautifully than before. I will swim so that the rocks weep and dissolve, and sing the songs that wash the hills and valleys, and make them be born anew.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: This I do no matter what you do or say, but now you are a part of it, and this is noble beyond imagining for those of your kind. Goodbye.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: And you can be part of this - just give the waterbell back to the water. Goodbye.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: And you can be part of this - just give the waterbells back to the water. Goodbye.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Remember! Give the waterbells back to the water! Goodbye.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: O mortals, you who washed away the poisonous Pool of Radiance...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: ...now try to win a victory more lasting! Restore the Splashing Song. Find the waterbells. Give them back to the water!
keys.speaker: plinshre
keys.desc: spoken, endlessly humored by the foolish pride of mortals

keys.dialogue: For even now evil creeps into the places you thought were clean. But the Song, ah, the Song of Water runs on and on and on.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Oyaa, the Pool is gone, the poisonous Pool, dissolved and washed away!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: And they who stole the Waterbells, you have pitched them into the whirlpool, oyaa!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: They will return - evil always returns. But always will heroes and deep water await them. And when they hear the Splashing Song, they will know their doom.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Oh! And I have been to the deepest places, and found another thing that may be of use to your kind. Farewell!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: O mortals, you who washed away the poisonous Pool of Radiance...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: ...dwell not overlong on your brief victory. Evil dies, but it is never dead. Even now, behind your back, the shadows grow long.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Do you desire an achievement that will last down the centuries? Then restore the Splashing Song. Give the waterbells back to the water!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Ahhh! This is E'lenthe, whom the waves carved from whalebone. Ah! I dance to have her back! Already it is if she had never been silent.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Oyaa! You have found Shihuala! Listen!
keys.speaker: plinshre
keys.desc: spoken, delight and amazement -oyaa! is a shout of joy, sfx of beautiful bell tone

keys.dialogue: This is the note that brings sun from rain, that makes pools glow with light and turns air crisp with joy.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: This is best of all, Jawhimishan - the Waterbell of Endless Music. O Jawhimishan, how I have missed you!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: In exchange, I have a gift for you. Have you found any of the other waterbells?
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Here - I have for you another treasure, brought up from the deeps. Did you find the last missing waterbell? O that would be a marvel!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Ah, when last we met, you barely escaped the deep water...
keys.speaker: plinshre
keys.desc: spoken, warning you made her angry when you last spoke

keys.dialogue: But now you have brought me a waterbell! And see, my anger has ebbed - and in its place, a gift!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Aaah, I am laughing, you mortals are in such a hurry!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: For certainly the waterbell would have come back to me in time.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But yet, I am happy to have it - and to get rid of this, which has no value to me.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: You have made good your promise - and I have not forgotten mine!
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: You have made me happy. So here, I give you something you mortals seem to delight in...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: You have given back to the water one of its treasures...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: And see! I have brought you one of the treasures given to me, a long blade of purest crystal...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Or no, I have it not. Oh well, no matter. Here is a shiny thing that may be useful to your kind.
keys.speaker: plinshre
keys.desc: spoken, flighty 'oops I guess I don't really have that, nevermind!'

keys.dialogue: You have restored the music to the waters, O mortals. I will swim ever more beautifully, and you will swim with me.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: It is one of the things given into my care in the time of Fire, the dark time when the city died.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: I have many such things to be rid of, if you should find more waterbells.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: I know of what you speak, but I do not know, for I do not care, it matters none to me. But for your sake I will try to remember...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Down it goes, I think, from under the spires, and its tendrils touch the deep waters.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But the waters care not. Evil always plants the seeds for its own downfall. Each evil deed spawns a hero. The waters wait - we are good at waiting.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But I must swim, and you must struggle on, in the way of your kind. Here is a thing that may aid you - but first...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Receive this rare blessing: the waters of knowledge, shaken from a naiad's hand.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Yes - I must swim, and you must struggle on in the way of your kind. Here is a thing that may aid you - but first...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Aah, you are mortals. For a moment, I had forgotten.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Aah, but you are mortals! For a moment, I had forgotten.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Mortals - and yet a little more. For the water sings, and you are part of it now. What the water knows, you know - a little bit.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Now - I must swim, and you must struggle on in the way of your kind. Here is a thing that may aid you - but first...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Ah, spoken like the mortals you are. For a moment, I had forgotten.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: You turn a blind eye to beauty, and grasp for things of death.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Very well, I have a reward for you. A woman gave this to me in the dark time, just before the flame engulfed her and her children...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Why did she not entrust herself and her children to the waters? I would have been grateful for the gift - and more merciful than the flames...
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: But no, she only gave me this. And now I give it to you.
keys.speaker: plinshre

keys.dialogue: Farewell!

keys.dialogue: The room beyond the barred window seems unnaturally dark. Out of the blackness, a voice speaks to you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Who's there? What do you want? -Beware, I warn you, I am not defenseless!
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. But say, in your travels, if you ever come upon any neckpieces - necklaces, amulets, torcs, chokers, collars and so on - show them to me.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: I am a collector, you might say, of such things. Now, farewell.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Ah, you have good in your hearts, not evil! I have seen adventurers like you before. Human, or something like it.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: No, even I can see you are not defenseless. Human, aren't you? Or something like it?
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: I like humans - most of them, anyway.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Ah, you have good in your hearts, not evil! I am relieved to know this - I have seen adventurers like you before.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Good ones. Very, very good ones.
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Prisoner? Oh yes, indeed I am, prisoner of my desires...
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: Good travels to you. But say, before you go, do you have any fine neckpieces? Necklaces, amulets, torcs, chokers, neck rings, pendants, collars, of very high quality?
keys.speaker: preybeli

keys.dialogue: I am a collector, you might say, of just about anything that goes on one's neck.

keys.dialogue: You used the Stone of Fate to bring ancient dwarven defenses to life, sealing the doom of the Cult forces defending the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You brought doom upon the Cult forces defending the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You negotiated the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor, scaled the castle walls, and entered the Cult stronghold from above.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: With Nathlilik's help, you smashed the Vessel of Souls, sending into oblivion the souls of drow enslaved by the Cult.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Against great odds, you smashed the Vessel of Souls, sending into oblivion the souls of drow enslaved by the Cult.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You spoke the Word of Redemption, allowing Miroden Silverblade to destroy the Sapphire of the Weave. Now Anorrweyn Evensong controls the Mythal.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In open combat, you defeated Kya Mordrayn, allowing her soul to be claimed by her dark masters.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Finally, you slew the great dracolich Pelendralaar, and used the Gauntlets of Moander to destroy the Pool of Radiance, ending the Cult's threat to all the free peoples of the Realms.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One of the nagas has a neck pouch. Inside it, you find a scrimbone - a bone that nagas write on, by holding the bone with their tongue and chiseling into it with a sharp fang.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: On the bone, you can make out a name - 'Preybelish' - and a strange word. As you look at the word...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The naga's scrimbone teaches you the Word of Venom.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Among all the residue of old magics, you sense new power emanating from this ancient mirror.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This door appears to be barred from the inside.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You know where you are - even after hundreds of years, the powerful aura of magics is unmistakable.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You have entered the Speculum - Myth Drannor's celebrated Hall of Wizards - abandoned ever since the city fell.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: An unseen presence haunts the shade of this tree...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Woe, woe to Myth Drannor! Hachaam Selorn is no more, and his baneblade Faervian - dark elves caress it deep in the Catacombs....
keys.speaker: knghost

keys.dialogue: You feel the presence sink back down out of the light.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: After Pujik dies, the axe he bears shatters to pieces! And you sense a spell has been broken.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: With its talisman gone and its minions destroyed, the Spawn Pool retreats underground, back to the deadly Pool of Radiance that spawned it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The sturdy door is barred on this side. With some difficulty, you lift the bar.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Chill air pours out - you recognize the stale odor of the deep dungeons.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You recognize this bridge! A famous ballad sings of how Hachaam Selorn and a handful of heroes held this little bridge...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...against companies of flinds, gnolls and ogre-kin, blocking the way with a mountain of burning bodies.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Of those great deeds, nothing remains.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A human voice calls out to you from somewhere out of sight.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The one speaking is the human sorcerer Malgi Hi.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Both the naga's totem and the Spawn Pool radiate malice. Hate flows out at you in buffeting waves.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your blow shatters the naga's totem, and breaks the aura of protection it gave to the Spawn Pool.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Seething, the Spawn Pool retreats into the deeps, back to the Pool of Radiance that sent it forth.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The sturdy door is barred on this side. With some difficulty, you lift the bar.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Chill dungeon air pours out - flavored with the rank smell of the lizardfolk.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The sturdy door is firmly blocked on the other side.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The grass around it is overgrown and it appears no one has opened this door in a long time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You peer in the keyhole of this door and notice it's blocked with something - possibly the key.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It is useless trying to open the door from this side.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The runes carved into these sturdy doors are ancient, but they seem to be wards that protect against evil.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You suspect that this was once a cache-hold of the legendary Knights of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A small chamber lies behind the door. A well-made, cut-stone, dusty crawlway leads up out of the chamber.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You crawl through the stone passage to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You enter a short, steeply-descending tunnel. A slight, but steady stream of fresh air flows up from below.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You descend a short tunnel to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You enter a short, gradually descending hallway. The air inside is stale.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You descend a hallway to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door opens into a winding lateral passageway. The way is unlittered, but dusty from years of disuse.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You follow a winding passage to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Behind the door is a level, rocky mining tunnel. All is quiet; the digging and production ceased years ago.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You scramble the length of the rocky tunnel to reach the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You enter a narrow chamber, out of which climbs a ladder cut into the stone. You ascend carefully, as the rungs are worn from repeated use in years past.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb the stone ladder to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door opens onto a very steep stairway. After several switchbacking flights, you reach the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb several short flights of stairs to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Behind the door is a steadily climbing, dirt-floored tunnel. The many sets of tracks you see were made long ago.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You ascend the dirt-floored tunnel to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Several short ramps climb back and forth to the surface. As you ascend, your armor and weapons clang-echo off the old stone walls.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb several short ramps to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A cobwebbed stair climbs up immediately beyond the door. After many flights, you reach the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb a cobwebbed stair to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Behind the door is a lengthy, spiral stair, climbing up into the blackness. The air is cold, but stagnant, and you reach the surface without incident.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You ascend a long sprial stair.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Beyond the door a narrow stair rises up, up, up out of sight. After a long climb, you reach the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You ascend a long, narrow stair.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Before you lies a well-made stone stair. You ascend several hundered steps to the surface.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb several hundered steps.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The door opens onto a partially caved-in tunnel, littered with bones and debris.  The stench is heavy and the going slow, but you reach the surface safely.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You pick your way through the length of the partially caved-in tunnel.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you reach the top, you find a makeshift scaffold of immense beams supporting a rock-and-mortar wall.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your dwarf quickly sizes up the structure, kicks aside one of the beams, and jumps back.  The wall wobbles for a second, then tumbles down.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The dwarves in your party talk amongst themselves, and reach a quick consensus. They lift a single beam out of the structure, and the wall crashes down.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Several heavy blows smashes one of the beams, and the wall collapses under its own weight.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You climb over the stones and lumps of sand-and-clay and emerge in the fresh air of Stillwater.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You emerge in the fresh air of Stillwater.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In return I steal from you just a little kiss...
