keys.dialogue: Say, what is this? Friends of yours? If you've sold me out, Nottle, I swear by the Lord of Shadows, you'll pay. The treasure's mine!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ahhh - now it's YOUR treasure, is it? Yar crockin' our deal, Tudo, ya blarsted hothead.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: None of your business. It's mine and it'll stay mine.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Hoho! We'll see about that, ya younking natterjack of a rogue.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: What do you think? We killed them, heh heh.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: WE? I killed them, more like. Which is why the scroll belongs to me. So tell your bunch of strongarms here to get lost, or else.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: If I wanted that scroll, I'da have it now. I don't need no bunch o' strongarms to pluck a plum off a baby like you.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: If'n you don't believe me, ask them.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: All right, strangers, what are you doing here, jinxing up our racket? Did Nottle put you up to this? Speak up, and be quick about it!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ahh, that's right, these are the ones I told you about, Tudo. The Pool of Radiance and all.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ahh, no, don't believe them, they're lying!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: These are the ones I told you about, Tudo. The Pool of Radiance and all.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: You best listen to them, Tudo! These are the ones I told you about - the Pool of Radiance and all.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: You want it? Too bad.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Now nobody gets the scroll. You happy now?
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Agh, Tudo, you hotheaded clummitoad! These are the ones I told you about - the Pool of Radiance and all.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Yeah, well, thanks for that. But you still ain't getting my treasure without a fight! Look at the dead mages! I can take care of myself!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ahhh now - hold on, Tudo, don't you recognize these folks? This is the 'small band' in the Song of Faerun!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ah, right - here you are in Myth Drannor, prizes dripping off you, and you don't want treasure.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ahhh now - hold on, Tudo, don't you recognize these folks? They're not after treasure, heh heh. They are the 'small band' in the Song of Faerun!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ah - ah - you are the ones the Bard of Kara-Tur sings about! Tell me, what is your secret? By Oghma's Beard, I wish the Bard would place MY deeds in the Song of Faerun!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Why, the Song of Faerun is the great tale of the world - as the Bard writes it, so it comes to be. To be in it is to breathe the air of immortality!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ah, great things! Your exploits fire the blood! Listen...
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: 'The Pool! The Pool! It grows, and yet...'
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: '...One small band against it set.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ahh, 'tis marvelous. You have heard it? We heard it in the ruins of the Nightingale Court, at the column of the Whispering Wind!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ah, great things! Your exploits fire the blood! Listen...
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: 'From out the blackness, up to light...'
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: '...Came one small band of growing might.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ahh, 'tis marvelous. You have heard both verses? We heard them in the ruins of the Nightingale Court, at the column of the Whispering Wind!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Will you merit a third verse? No one knows. But if you do - by Ibrandul's tongue, I would like to help you earn it!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Him? Great deeds? Aha ha ha.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Then filchin' purses is a great deed, and coobilking maids, and muggling marks for coppers!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: I've been held down by the low company I've kept. Until now! This is my moment! Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you back!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Well now, here's your chance at glory, Tudo. Hahar! A chance to roast in a Cult firestorm, more likely, heh heh.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Shows what you know, you hardhead skinnuck, and why you'll always be a miserable old trader, carping for coppers. Glory and the firestorm, it's all the same.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Travelers! This is my moment! Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you from your destiny!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Not without me, you don't!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Yes! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! Our deeds will be worth a song, and then some! So long, Nottle, you old boot.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Tudo joins your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Hahar! That's a polite way of sayin' to get lost, Tudo.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Shut up, you old boot. I know what it means. But they'll come around, mark my words! Hit a trap, or bump a lock, they'll reconsider.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: When you do, look me up! You'll find me at Nottle's wagon. Until then, fare thee well!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Well, you got no rogue in your company. And the lad does know how to tickle a lock and fuddle a trap.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Just make him promise to shut his yap, and he might do you well.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Oh, I promise, I promise!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Well, you got a rogue already. But why not give the lad a chance? He tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Ahh, forget it, Tudo, their company is big enough already. Gets way too much of the wrong kind o' attention, heh heh.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Then it is simple. One of them must stand aside, and I will take their place.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Yes! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! We'll do deeds worth a song, and then some!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Let me know when you have decided who is to remain behind.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Brave words - but you'll come around, mark my words! Hit a trap, or meet a lock, you'll reconsider, and quickly.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Well, you got rogues among ya already. But this lad tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many...
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: ...and he's got spirit, I'll give him that! Why not give one o' your company a breather, a rogue maybe, and give him a chance instead?
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Heyya, brave heroes, my name is Tudo, I am a rogue of no little renown! You need someone of my skill if you're going to uncover all this fabulous city has to offer.
keys.speaker: Tudo
keys.desc: spoken, slick and smooth (text change) 5-2-01, lines combined

keys.dialogue: Let the clumsy one of your company stand aside! I am ready to join with you, and let the good times begin!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you from the treasures you so richly deserve.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ah, heroes! I am so glad to see you again!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: You big liar. You lost a gross of gold pieces to me when they beat the Cult, heh heh.
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: A bet I'm glad I lost, Nottle!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Without him among you, he was sure you were doomed, the lordy strutabout!
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: But now, the Cult is no more! And all the treasures of Myth Drannor lie at your feet - if you have a shrewd enough rogue with you, that is, ahem.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Ah, friends-in-arms, you have returned, huzzah! To take me away from this stinging gnat of a trader, I have no doubt.
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: Argh, I hope so! For if I hear once more how you single-hand slew the dracolich...
keys.speaker: Nottle

keys.dialogue: Single-handed! No! I used both hands. Oh, how I hope I can be one of you once again!
keys.speaker: Tudo

keys.dialogue: You are deep below New Phlan, in the cavern where the Pool of Radiance has reawakened, threatening the city. The four people here are a sample adventuring party. Use them to explore this area, and you'll learn how to master this game. (click the left mouse button or press the space bar to continue.)
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: I am the Dungeon Master, the DM. Whenever you see lines like these, explaining game events or mechanics, the DM is telling you what is happening with your characters.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: How do you get a character to do something? Look in the lower right corner of the screen. There are four colored bars - blue, green, purple, and yellow. Each character has been assigned one of these colors.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Let's tell your 'green' character to walk to a certain spot, and continue the tutorial from there.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To do that, try this: left-click on the green bar to select the green character. Then click on the ground near the opening at the end of the fence. Click the left mouse button or press the space bar when you're ready to begin.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You don't have to move characters one at a time. To move your party as a group, use the round button in the lower right corner of the screen.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Click the button so that three people appear on it. When you do that, the characters will group themselves together, ready to travel as a party...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...and if you click on the ground, the party leader will move there, and your other characters will follow.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Try it out. As a party, go through the opening at the end of the fence, then head east, over to the purple signpost. We'll continue the tutorial from there.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now let me tell you about the icons that appear along the bottom of the game screen - you've probably figured out most of them already.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: From left to right: the Game Options and Quest Log buttons, the Time of Day display, and the Map button, and, on the right side, the Party-At-A-Glance bars, the little Party Formation and Rest buttons, and the big Group/Ungroup Party button.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If you want a full explanation of each feature, you can get it at any time from this signpost, Playing the Game. The sign can also tell you how to take some common game actions.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To read what is posted, just click on the sign. When you are finished, select the last item in the talk menu. Now, I will display the information on the signpost.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's time to learn about the characters -- who are these people, anyway?
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Just like what you learned at the Playing the Game signpost, most of what is here you can figure out by experimenting with the game yourself.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Except for the most important part:
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To learn about a character or an object in the game, right click on him, her, or it.  This will bring up a small menu, which includes a name, a few statistics (HP means Hit Points, AC means Armor Class), and some menu choices.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But before we go on: after you are done reading, right click on a character or object.  Notice the sort of information you get.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Then, after you've looked around the interface some, left click on the signpost, All about Characters, to bring up a list of choices to learn more.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: An icy draft penetrates your armor, and a chill creeps into your heart. You're in the dungeons now.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But it's only a single room, and not a very threatening one at that.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Notice the objects in this room: some barrels to the west and a couple of treasure chests to the east.
keys.speaker: DM
keys.desc: (text change) MAB, 04-27-01: removed ', a table north of you'

keys.dialogue: To investigate an object, first approach it with one of your characters. This is stealthy work, so you may want to choose your rogue...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...after all, when's the last time YOU saw a barbarian pick a lock?
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Choose a character, and approach each object in turn. To get out of here, move down into the bottom corner of the room.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Here are three barrels. One of them has a key in it - the key to one of the chests on the other side of the room. Your job is to get that key. There are a couple of ways to do it...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You could just reach your hand in. To do that, you'll move the mouse cursor over a barrel and, when the hand icon appears, click. For barrels, or other open containers, a click means you search for and grab whatever's inside.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But maybe you're too cautious to grab. In that case, you could right-click on the barrel. This would bring up a menu of everything you can do with that object - options such as 'search' and 'smash.'
keys.speaker: DM
keys.desc: (text change) MAB, 04-27-01, edited out reference to 'move.'

keys.dialogue: 'Search' would be the same as grabbing. If you choose 'Smash,' however, your character tries to break open the container. If it breaks, anything inside will spill out, and appear as a pile of treasure on the ground...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To get treasure out of a pile, click on it - and then drag whatever you want off the grid onto whichever character you want to have it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In short, all objects in the game work this way: if you move the mouse cursor over something, and it turns into a hand, a left click means 'do the most common thing'; a right click means 'give me a list of everything I can do.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now, go ahead and check out those barrels!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Looks like you didn't get the key you need.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Did you investigate the barrel in the back?  Did you click-drag the key off the grid into a character's inventory? Is there a treasure pile lying around that you haven't gone through?
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Looks like you've done everything there is to do here.  Head down into the bottom corner of the room to be transported back to the cavern under New Phlan.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now it's time to use that key you found. Head across the room to the two chests.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You've already found the key. Why don't you head across the room to the chest on the right?
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There are two chests here. You'll find one opens (with some difficulty) and one doesn't.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But don't let that stop you - click on each one anyway, just to see what happens.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Then head across the room to the barrels. They hold something you need.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You'll need a key to open the chest on the left.  It's hidden in one of the barrels on the other side of the room.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Oops, you forgot to pick up the key.  The barrel in the back has a key in it; you won't be able to open one of the chests without it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now let's clean out some treasure chests!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To do that, you'll click on each one, and see what happens. Don't forget to put anything you find into inventory - click-drag it off the treasure grid and onto one of your characters.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If you really want to do this right, use rogue skills on the chests. To do that, right-click on your rogue character, and select (S)kills. 'Search,' 'Open Lock,' and 'Disable Device' can be lifesavers in situations like this.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Before opening that chest on the right, you might want to try out some of your rogue's skills on it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Right click on your rogue, then select (S)kills.  Search, Open Lock, and Disable Device can all be particularly useful.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You've done everything there is to do in here.  Go down into the bottom corner of the room, and you'll be transported back to the cavern under New Phlan.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Monsters.  Deep in the dungeons of Myth Drannor, there are monsters everywhere, eager to take your treasure and your lives.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Of course, this is only the tutorial, so the threat is very small. Only a single orc, unaware as yet of your presence.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Let's learn about combat - starting with what happens before the fighting starts. Sometimes you spot the enemy before he sees you. This gives you a few options...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can try to move away before you are noticed - very advisable if the monsters look too strong for you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can try to sneak past the creature. It might not notice you. Of course, the closer you get, the greater the chance you will be detected.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can approach the creature. Not all creatures you meet are enemies - and even some enemies will talk rather than fight.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Or you can attack. If, when you put the cursor over a creature, it turns into a sword, a click will begin combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Go ahead and deal with this orc - walk up to it, or click on it to start a fight.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Okay! You've triggered combat. Now each character and adversary take their actions one at a time, in order from fastest to slowest.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the upper left corner of the screen, a row of colored icons will appear - the initiative bar. This bar graphically displays the order in which the combatants will take their actions.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: In the initiative bar, each character is represented by a gem of his or her color, and the monsters are represented by red creature faces. But let's get on with how to fight!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A pulsing circle underneath one of your characters means it's his or her turn to act. To attack the orc, click on it. Your character will approach the orc and strike it - or, if holding a missile weapon, will fire it at the orc.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To cast a spell, right-click on your character, choose 'arcane spells' or 'divine spells,' then pick a spell and a target. Now go to it!
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now that the orc is dead, you may want to loot its body. Once the monsters are dead, if they have treasure, it's all gathered into one treasure-pile object; click on it to get the loot.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You also may want to rest. Rest heals your characters and restores the spells they used up during the fight. To rest, click on the tent in the lower right corner of the screen. But be careful...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If the tent is green, you are in a place where resting is safe. If it is yellow, monsters may interrupt your rest. And if it's red, it's not safe for rest at all.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Go ahead and rest here. Then move the table (or smash it), and click on the door to open it... although you may want to right-click on it and (L)ook through its barred window first.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One orc down, a few more to go!  Don't forget to collect the booty.  Click on the treasure pile.  When the grid pops up, click and drag the items you want to the characters you want to have them.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Now, as you clash with these orcs, pay attention to the cursor. The icons on it can help you plan your movement.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Each character's combat turn is divided into two halves. During the first half, you can move, or attack, or cast a spell. During the second half, you can move - and attack, unless you've attacked already.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: As you move the cursor around to potential destinations, if there is a '+' sign, you know it will take only half a move to get there - leaving some time to attack. If there is no '+', it will take your entire turn to get there.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you are done with a character's turn, and want to move on to the next one, hit the space bar.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One more thing: from time to time your party catch the monsters off guard, surprising them.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When this happens, the initiative bar -- the colored gems in the upper left corner of the screen -- will appear for only your characters: there will be no red monster icons.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This means that for the the first round of combat, each character in your party may take a single action before the any monster can react.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But be careful: a SINGLE action is NOT a full combat turn, it is only a half turn.  A character may either move OR attack, but not both.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: So, you can make a ranged attack (with a bow, sling, or spell) OR move, but not fire AND THEN move.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Lastly, the monsters also sometimes surprise your party.  If you see a single red monster icon in the upper left hand corner, that's what happened.  They all get to take an action, before you can do anything.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Sometime you beat them to the punch, and sometimes they get the jump on you.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Three more orcs down. Don't forget to take their treasure - find the treasure pile and click on it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your next combat is off to the southwest. But you will notice that there doesn't seem to be any way into that chamber.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: That's because the way in is hidden -- a secret door. To find it, select your rogue, and move him near the wall dividing these rooms.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: He will apply his powers of observation automatically, and look for the door.  If he doesn't find it right away, you may have to use his search skill.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When he does find the door, it will become visible.  Open it and go into the next chamber.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: By now you know the basics of moving and attacking. When you fight your next adversary, try some more advanced combat options.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When it's your character's combat turn, right-click on him or her, and choose 'combat options.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can probably figure out each option by its name, or by using it a few times. To learn more, click on the Combat Commands signpost in front of you, or read the full description in the manual.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To fight your last adversary, go past the signpost. After you defeat him, move down to the south corner of this room to exit.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You have defeated everyone here in the tutorial dungeon. To go back to the main cavern, walk into the corner south of here.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Don't forget: you can return here any time to practice manipulating objects. Just go through the door that brought you here the first time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Don't forget: you can return here any time to practice combat. Just go through the portal that brought you here the first time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Please move the party closer to the signpost to continue the tutorial.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To learn about a character or object in the game, right click on him, her, or it.  This will bring up a small menu, which includes name, a few statistics (HP means Hit Points, AC means Armor Class), and some menu choices.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The options below discuss each of those menu choices.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you right click on one of your characters, the first menu option (underneath the HP and AC line) is Character Sheet.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This selection brings up a graphical information page for the individual you clicked on.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One of the features of this page is a grid containing the character's equipment.  To equip or swap weapons, armor, rings, amulets, gauntlets, or boots, click-drag and then drop.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Also on the Character Sheet are tabs for spells, skills & feats, and stats.  Click on a tab to see the associated list for the character.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Unlike the inventory display, these lists are not interactive: they only display information about the character.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Also: You may not cast spells from the Character Sheet; that can only be done from the pop-up menus (see casting arcane or divine spells).
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There are number of non-player characters (NPCs) in Pool of Radiance II.  You may wish to add some of them to your party.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: However, the party may not have more than six characters in it at any one time.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If your party is full, and you want to add an NPC, you will have to 'make room.' To do this, right click on the character you want to kick out, and...
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: ...then select 'Remove from Party.' This will free up a slot in your party, and leave the removed character behind.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But take care: Although single characters have been known to turn up at various places in Myth Drannor, not everyone you leave behind will find his or her way to safety.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you select '(I)nventory' after right clicking on a character, a second menu appears: Magic / Weapons / Armor)
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Select one of these to see a list of this character's items for that category.  For example, choosing 'Weapons' will display a menu of all swords, axes, daggers, hammers, and so on.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To equip a weapon, select it. It appears in the character's hand, and any other weapon he or she was using is put back into inventory.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Some of the items under the 'Magic' heading don't equip -- such as potions and scrolls. When you select one these, the character uses it: drinks the potion, or reads the scroll.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One more thing: if one of the selections -- Magic / Weapons / Armor -- is gray, that means you cannot select it.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Either the character has no items of that category, or equipping or using items of that type cannot be performed at that time during the game.  For example, armor may not be taken off or put on during combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Lastly, notice that this menu choice is '(I)nventory.'  The 'I' is in parentheses, because you can press the 'i' key to bring up the inventory directly, without going through the right click menu.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A click on the '(S)kills' selection lists the character's special skills.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To direct the character to apply one of these, select it.  The DM will explain whether the skill was successfully executed or not.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There are two sets of spells in Pool of Radiance II: arcane and divine.  Sorcerers can cast only (A)rcane Spells.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you select 'arcane spells,' a spell level menu will appear.  It looks something like this: 'Cantrips / 1st Level / 2nd Level' and so on.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If a level is gray, that means the character has no spells of that level, or has already cast all he or she can, and must rest to regain them, or may not cast any of the spells of that level outside of combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To cast a spell, you must know what level it is.  Select the appropriate level; a list of spells will appear.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Select the spell you want to cast.  The menu will vanish.  Next select a target, and the character will animate and launch the spell.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Final note: to help with spells which can affect multiple targets, as you move the cursor to target the spell, the characters and monsters that will be hit by the spell turn red.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: There are two sets of spells in Pool of Radiance II: arcane and divine.  Clerics (and Paladins and Rangers) can cast only (D)ivine Spells.
keys.speaker: DM
keys.desc: (Text Change)MAB, 06-08-01: added '(and Paladins and Rangers)' to list of characters who can cast divine spells

keys.dialogue: When you select 'divine spells,' a spell level menu will appear.  It looks something like this: 'Orisons / 1st Level / 2nd Level' and so on.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If a level is gray, that means the character has no spells of that level, or has already cast all he or she can, and must rest to regain them, or may not cast any of the spells of that level outside of combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To cast a spell, you must know what level it is.  Select the appropriate level; a list of spells will appear.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Select the spell you want to cast.  The menu will vanish.  Next select a target, and the character will animate and launch the spell.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Final note: to help with spells which can effect multiple targets, as you move the cursor to target the spell, the characters and monsters that will be hit by the spell turn red.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The final choice on the character right-click menu is (C)ombat Options.  These will be gray and unavailable, unless the party is in combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The combat options will be discussed in the Chamber of the Sword, later in the tutorial.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you are ready, continue onward to the right, past the signpost, and up the screen a little.  Continue moving right until you see a portcullis in the wall.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When it's a character's turn, right click on him or her to pop up a menu, then choose 'combat options' to bring up a list of different attacks or actions this character may perform this turn.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When reviewing the list below, keep in mind that different character classes have different combat options, and not every character will have available every option.  Also, characters gain more options as they go up in levels.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Choose 'Full Attack' when you want your character to focus this turn entirely on attacking an enemy.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: A full attack uses up both halves of the combat turn in an effort to execute the maximum number of attacks against an opponent.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The 'power attack' trades accuracy for damage.  You character will focus all his or her energy on damaging the opponent, but will also miss the target more often.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Select 'defend' when you want your character to stand ready, but take no other action this turn.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Delay alters the initiative order for this entire combat by delaying the character's combat turn until after all other characters and monsters have acted.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This can be useful, if you want to wait to see what action a monster takes or how much damage another character does before deciding what to do.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When you choose 'delay,' the character's diamond in the intiative bar moves to the from its current position to the right end.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: If you rest when the rest indicator is yellow, wandering monsters may interupt your recovery.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When this happens, one character will be on watch, but the others in the party will still be asleep.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Choose 'awaken party member' to wake up everyone else.  This will use up your character's entire combat turn, but it will likely be worth to get others to help you fend off the wandering monsters.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Clerics have the power to repell or even destroy undead monsters.  To attempt this action, choose 'turn undead.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Keep in mind that turning undead is not a sure thing, and that powerful monsters are more difficult to turn than weaker ones.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Barbarians can turn themselves into extra-powerful fighters for a short duration during a combat.  Choose 'rage' to do this.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your character will hit his or her target more frequently, and will do more damage on each hit, but at the cost of his or her own defensive capability.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Use rage selectively.  A barbarian can only rage once per combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Approach certain characters, and look what happens. They speak to you.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: After they speak, you choose a response. Careful! What you choose matters.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: For now, my business is my own. You will find out who I serve soon enough.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: I admire your persistence. But do not expect the people you meet to tell you everything you want to know - unless it serves their interests.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: If you take the time to talk to people, you'll learn things to help you on your journey. Secrets may be divulged. Enemies may become friends.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: If you parley with your enemies, you may gain the advantage of surprise. But be watchful! Or else they may surprise you instead.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Merely approach the person. Usually they speak up, if they have something to say.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Some characters may also be storytellers. The cursor will change to a PROFILE SPEAKING icon when it passes over them. Click to hear some of the rumors and legends they know now, and visit them again to learn more.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Over other characters, the cursor will change to TWO HANDS. If the hands are one above the other, click to buy or sell items. If the hands are side by side, click if you wish to have that character join your party.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: You will meet people who believe in your quest. If you ask them, they may be willing to join your ranks. After you talk to them, TWO HANDS side-by-side will appear when you move the mouse cursor over them.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: In time, I may be one of these people - if you prove yourselves worthy.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Doors closed to you will be opened. That which was lost will be found. Friends unexpectedly appear. And everywhere you will hear of the thread of evil, undoing all your hopes.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Enough of your questions! Instead, a test. Let's see if you've been paying attention.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Now, no more talk! Do not expect people to stand around and jaw with you all day. Here's a little test - to see if you've been paying attention.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: You did not ask how your responses can shape your progress in the game! Ah, you will find out soon enough.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Remember, just approach a person, or click on them, if you want to talk to them.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Goodbye? You think so? I don't think you can get rid of me that easily.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: To show you a mild example, I'll stop talking - let's see if you can figure out what to do next.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Have you been paying attention? Let's find out.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: You may call me Kellan... I am a fighting sorcerer for the group called the Silver Fire.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: But I used to wield sword and spell for someone else. My name was different then... it would have killed you to hear it.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: If we meet, we will meet in Myth Drannor. I might be friend to you when friends are rare indeed.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: We are here in New Phlan. Enjoy its peaceful streets while you can!
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Soon you will join me in Myth Drannor, the City of Song - a magnificent ruin that is anything but peaceful.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: I am under the orders of the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer. There is someone in Myth Drannor she bids me to destroy...
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: You will have your own quests, many of them - but I know not what they are.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: When you meet characters, approach them closely. Often they will speak to you, if they have something to say.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Also, roll your cursor over them, even after you've talked with them. A PROFILE SPEAKING cursor means 'click to learn more,' or 'to hear stories and legends'...
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: The TWO HANDS side-by-side cursor means 'click if you want me to join your party' and TWO HANDS one over another means 'click if you want me to buy or sell items.'
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Do not be too quick to attack characters that don't attack you! If you approach them, they may parley with you, and you might learn something valuable.
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Ah, you do not waste time jawboning! I like that. I hope we meet again, and raise swords together...
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. I hope we meet again, and raise swords together...
keys.speaker: Kellan

keys.dialogue: And now I must go. Goodbye - or maybe, until we meet again.

keys.dialogue: These are keyboard shortcuts you may find handy. The first five are general game functions; the next four pertain to the highlighted (active) character.
keys.speaker: DM
keys.desc: (Text Change) There are two text changes here, one on 4-24-01, and one on 06-08-01: 'five' to 'four'

keys.dialogue: Press the ESCape key to bring up the Game Menu, to load or save a game, change the game settings, or quit back to Windows.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's the same as clicking on the round blue button in the lower left corner of the screen.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the RIGHT SHIFT key to switch your characters from walking to running mode. Press it again to switch back.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When walking, your characters move slowly and carefully; they are quicker to notice enemies or things hidden in the environment. When running, they concentrate on getting from here to there as fast as they can, not on noticing things.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Underneath each character and monster are one to three colored circles.  These tell you at a glance how healthy that character is: the more circles, the healthier.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Normally, only the active character (the one whose turn it is) has his or her circles visible. To see all character and monster circles, press the LEFT ALT key; to see only the active character's circles, press LEFT ALT again.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To group or ungroup your party, press the ENTER key on the lower right corner of the keyboard, near the number keypad. This is the same as clicking on the round button in the lower right corner of the screen.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: When grouped, you click to move or act with the party leader, and the party's other characters follow your leader. When ungrouped, you click to move or act with only the active character.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the BACKSLASH (' \ ') key to call up the Character Sheet for the active character.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'Character Sheet.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the 'i' key to bring up an inventory menu for the active character. The menu has dropdown lists of the character's Magic items, Weapons and Armor. Your character can choose which items to equip from these lists.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting  'Inventory'.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the 'a' or 'd' key to call up a spellcasting menu - 'a' for 'arcane' spells (for sorcerers) and 'd' for 'divine' spells (for clerics).
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting either 'arcane spells'  or 'divine spells'.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the 's' key to use one of the active character's skills. It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'skills'.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the 'c' key to select one of the active character's combat options. It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'combat options'.  Remember, these options are only available during combat.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: One last tip: you may want to save your game right here. That way, you can easily return and review these keyboard shortcuts.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To save your game, press ESCape to bring up the Game Menu, and select Save Game. Label it something like 'keyboard shortcuts.' Then press Resume Game.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Press the 'F1' key to bring up a list of the game's hotkeys.

keys.dialogue: This signpost, Playing the Game, can teach you about elements of the interface, or you can ask about things you want to learn how to do.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Playing the Game.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: The round button in the lower left corner breaks away from the game action to mundane bookkeeping functions.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Click on the Game Options button to bring up a menu, from which you can load or save games, quit the game, and change the game settings.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: When you are done talking to me, try saving your game. Then, whenever you want to ask me a question, all you have to do is load that saved game.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: In the box at the lower left corner of the screen, you'll find a book, a sun, and a map icon. These are the Quest Log, Time of Day, and Map functions, respectively.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Click on the Quest Log book to remind yourself about quests you've heard of, but haven't yet fulfilled.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Check the Sun display for time of day. As night falls, a full sun will wane to dark. Be more careful then, because some creatures only come out at night.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Click on the map to see an overhead view of the area you are exploring. You can drag flags from the right to label areas of the map to remind you where certain things are.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find some colored bars, one for each character in the party.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Clicking on a bar selects a character, just as if you had clicked on the character directly. You'll see the highlight box jump to the character you've selected.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: The height of the bar indicates the health of the character. When you are in combat, keep your eye on those bars, so you can heal wounded characters or pull them out of danger.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: The colored rings underneath a character match that person's colored bar, both in appearance and in function.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Three rings means the character is healthy; with two, they're damaged; if there is only one, the character is hurting.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Red rings appear under enemies, and follow the same system: three means the monster is healthy, two damaged, and one in bad shape.  Watching the red rings under opponents can help guide your combat strategy.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: One more thing: the small triangle points to your current party leader. If you want to change leaders, click-drag the triangle to point at a new character.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find two square buttons, one on top of the other. The top one is the Party Formation button; the bottom is the Rest button.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: To set your party's marching formation, first arrange the characters the way you'd like them. Then click the Party Formation button.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Tip: it's generally a good idea to have your party leader at the front of your formation.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Click the bottom button when you want your party to rest and relearn their spells. You can learn more about resting elsewhere in the tutorial.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: The round button in the lower right corner of the screen is the Group/Ungroup button. To group all your characters together, and move them in formation, click the button so that it displays three little figures.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: If you click on a character or its colored bar, this button will change to a single large figure. You can now move that character independently of the others, to scout for traps or secret doors, smash objects, and so on.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: To move again as a group, click on the Group/Ungroup button so that it again displays three little figures. But heed this: you can't group your characters when you are in combat.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: When you move your characters as a group, everyone follows the 'party leader.' You select your leader using the small triangle below the colored bars in the box in the lower right corner of the screen.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: The leader not only heads up the party, but speaks for the party to characters you meet, and interacts with objects when the party is acting as a group.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: To change the party leader, click on the triangle and, while holding down the mouse button, slide the triangle underneath another colored bar.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Sometimes you may find that one of the icon boxes covers up a part of the screen you would like to see.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: To make the icon box pop down out of the way, click on the small diamond at the bottom center of the icon box. To bring it back up, click on the small diamond at the top center, the only part still showing.
keys.speaker: infowell

keys.dialogue: Goodbye. To review this information, come back here and click on this signpost.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Your elf also sees that the stair south of you winds down the slope to the Glim-Garden, through a ruined dwarf-made temple.

keys.dialogue: Along the arch is written, in the languages of elves, dwarves, humans and wizards, 'Speculum - Great Hall of Wizards.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Through the arch, you see the Spire of Mythanthor, where you first came up from the Dungeons. And, rising behind it, you see the Speculum, which once was the seat of power for Myth Drannor's magical elite.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: To the north, a narrow path switchbacks its way up a steep cliff.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Up at the top, you see the trees and elevated walkways of the Windrider Glade.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Faint runes run across the arch, announcing the entrance to the 'Noble House of Omberdawn.'
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: But the runes no longer tell the truth. Instead, beyond the archway, you see the expanse of soggy ground known as Sullymarsh.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The stone path continues to the west. At its end, you can make out one of Myth Drannor's great city squares, the Nightingale Court.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The proud buildings and public spaces are still elegant, even in ruin.
keys.speaker: DM

name: whil2010
selections: Ask what this column is
Ask what treasures it knows about
Say you are not citizens of the city
Take your leave
Ask about a necklace or a ring
Ask about a wand or scroll
Ask about a weapon or armor
Ask about other treasure
Ask to hear Song of Faerun
Take your leave
Ask to hear the first stanza
Ask to hear the second stanza
Ask to hear them both together
Ask to hear the victory refrain
Ask to hear the whole song
Don't listen to the song
Ask about rumors of treasures

keys.dialogue: O Citizen of Myth Drannor, what thing do you seek?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Treasures pass from hand to hand, from hoard to hoard, yet I hear where they go. Ask me.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: O Citizen of Myth Drannor, what manner of thing do you seek?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: O Citizen, now what treasure do you seek? Ask - but hurry! For I have not much time.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: O Citizen, I have no more stories to tell. A hush has fallen over the City, and words fail me.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I am the Ear of the City. I listen and remember.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: In happier days I listened for glad tidings, and repeated them so all would be happy. I helped citizens find things that were lost...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...now I listen to the wails of the dying, and repeat the evil mutterings of monsters clutching their treasures down in the dark.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: You think not? Yet all the city talks about you - the stones themselves whisper your names as you pass.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: You are the best citizens the city could hope for in these dark days, and all the city's treasures are yours, if you wish them.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I hear about powerful things of magic - such as rings, wands and scrolls. I hear about arms and armor, and other weapons of war. And I hear about jewels, books and other treasures.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But be quick! For I cannot talk for long.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I am sorry. The Whispering Wind speaks no more of rings or necklaces.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard, long ago, a dwarf woman speak of an amulet - Onglore's Amulet of War. She said...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'Here ya go, my husband. It was yours in life, so shall it be yours in death.' And the Amulet hummed as she laid it down.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: The voice wafted up to me from the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Not so long ago a voice spoke over a locket - it was Tyr's Locket of Justice. The voice said...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'You will summon the Nightmare Gate here. This scroll bears the Word of Constriction. When the time comes, it will dispel the Gate. In the meantime, use this.' And the Locket clinked as the mage put it on.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: That little clinking sound skittered down the Stone Halls of the Dungeons, and crawled into my ear.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Again and again over the centuries, I hear voices curse at Aasirak's Ebony Ring Of Power.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'Aaaagh! I cannot lift it!' they all say, and with sorrow they leave it behind.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Some drow were the last to say it, before their souls went dark, deep in the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Why, there are drow talking about the Eye Of The Witch, right this moment!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: One is saying, 'For priest or mage, it is a boon. Let us return immediately with this charm! I sense a reward!'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And now another says, 'The glory of Freth is reward enough. Come, let us go.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And now the whisper of drow boots on stone, as soft as a caress, in the deepest chambers of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I recall hearing a dwarf voice boom out above a necklace - the Onyx of the Richest Wort. This was hundreds of years ago.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'The city be surrounded,' the voice said. 'Dumathoin aid us, we must hide what we can, destroy what we must, and drink the rest.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Then I heard the tink-clink of valuables being hidden away. All has been silent ever since, down in the Brewer's Chambers of the Halls of Light, in the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I will tell you what I heard several days ago, with the Pendant of Fresh Kills.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: The thunder of battle magic fades away. A woman gasps her dying breath. Clutching the Pendant, she utters these words: 'Bright fire, white fire, Silver Pyre, let this body burn.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: A roar erupts - mages scream - and she and her Pendant are nothing but ashes whispering through the air.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This is what I heard many centuries ago, from the wearer of the Ring of Equilibrium.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: He said, 'Watch out, ya clummoxy hamhand! If I hadna been wearing this Ring, ya might have killed me with that.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Today, however, the Ring is scorned by its owner, and lies quiet and forgotten in a chest, in the uppermost part of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: O, I know of a necklace, the wonderful Necklace of Odoacer. Let me listen now...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Yes, it is underwater. It has been underwater for centuries now. Out of the roaring flames it flew, into the cool silence of deep water...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Now once again I hear the Watersong of Plinshree. Do you know of her, the naiad of this place? She is the only one who could retrieve this necklace for you, from its watery grave.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: No more of that. You know all you should of the city's objects of magic.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Ah, there is a wand, Terrilan's Crimson Wand - an accusing voice follows this wand wherever it goes.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'Terrilan, you killed your brother,' the voice whispers. 'Terrilan Grandirons, where is your brother Herunga?' Because of the voice, the nagas who possess it do not use the wand.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: These sounds floated up to me from the upper reaches of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Wait, I hear the crinkle of paper. Someone has taken a scroll out of a leather pouch...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Now a harsh voice says, 'Look at this. It's a Word of Power!'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And now another voice says - but no! It screams! A death cry... clicking mandibles... a magic Gate, closing...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...and now the sounds of beasts feasting, far away and down deep, below the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: So wands interest you? I heard someone speak in the presence of the Sceptre Of Leogans.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: He said, 'Of course you are right, Mistress. Someone gives them aid. But who?' And then, 'Fanraet is very capable. The witches must have used some trick.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And then finally he said, 'Of course, Mistress. Yes. At once.' His voice, stammering with fear, echoed up from the middle depths of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I can tell you what I heard about the Scroll of Memory, writ by Shyael Ildacer, a High Court Mage, just before the fall of Myth Drannor.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: When the Army of Darkness invaded the city, the scroll was lost beneath some rubble. But a year ago dark nagas found it, and used its Remembering Word to bring back forgotten magics.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: They might have learned some ancient spells of incalculable power! But a fortnight ago Pelendralaar came and killed them all, and ruined their lair, and utterly destroyed the Scroll of Memory.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I know of a scroll - Kiaransalee's Scroll of Claim - let me listen to what is going on around this scroll.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: A man is speaking. He has a dead voice! He is berating someone for their failure. They have not found a book he seeks... He shakes the scroll at them!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I hear the quick harsh breath of lizardfolk! They hiss. Now they go away, leaving the man in silence... This I hear clearly, even though it is happening far off to the west.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Hmmm... here is a stick, Roderick's Walkingstick! Let me open my ears to it...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: No, no, all is quiet where it lies. Except - a rustling noise, such as rats might make, or some other creature more stealthy.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This staff lies barely underground, some distance to the west.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: No, no, the winds blow ill. We must talk no more about things of war.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Oh, there is a shield, and terrible sounds surround this shield!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I hear the slavering howls of the undead, and the snap-tattoo of cruel traps, and the insane shrieking of victims caught in barbs or liquid fire.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: The shield is Gnome's Shield of Invulnerability, and its sounds echoed up from behind a secret door in the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Silence, silence surrounds the Sword of Marshbane, as it has for years uncounted.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Only the faintest rustling in the old armory, the sound of a haunt endlessly pacing.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: These sounds drift on the winds to me, from the dark place that once was called the Halls of Light.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard someone carrying magical mail armor - this was many years ago. And they laid it gently into a chest, and whispered a benison, and closed the lid.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Oh! That armor laughed as they laid it down! It sounded like water falling! It must be excellently made.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard this sound very clearly. It was near at hand, and only a spear's length or two underground.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I remember hearing about a staff - the famous Guulstav Of M'raelhorrid.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: It was a woman's voice, lovely and low. She said, 'And I have reserved the best for my loyal Mage Captain. Here - this is reward for your excellent work regarding our ally, the Baelnorn.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Her voice echoed up from the deepest chambers of the Catacombs under the Castle.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I have heard a sound related to Quimbee's Armor Of Many Pockets.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: A drow woman is speaking - her voice is thrilling. 'Box it up,' she says in the drow tongue. 'The Matron Mother will be most pleased.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Her voice rang along the hard stones and gloomy halls of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Here is a fearsome weapon - which some call the Deathspike. I hear sounds around it...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...the tramp of lizardy feet, and grumbling voices. 'I do not care what we promised,' the leader says. 'This is strong magic - it must go to Malgi Hi.' And now the feet tramp on, up stairs of stone and into the light.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This sound wafted over to me from the ruins to the north.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Here is something I heard, said in the presence of the Muttering Axe.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'My Mistress bids you receive this as a token of her esteem. She hopes it aids you as you rise in stature among the Ormyrrs.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This voice floated up from the Marshes to the south, about a fortnight ago.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Now I have heard the song of Prince Antonae's Stormbow - which makes arrows sing with delight!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But that was in the past, when Lord Derrose wielded it in Myth Drannor's final days, and when Jada Moonglamaer took it up, after Derrose fell.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Now the bow listens sadly as mandibles clack and bones split, down in an arraccat's lair deep in the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I know the Wraithmael Of Drenofiend has been laid to rest.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Drenofiend was a half-ogre, bane of elves... He died, praise Corellan, in the final assault on the city, and his ancient armor tumbled into deep places and was lost.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But naught that is buried is buried for ever. The drow have brought the Wraithmael back up from the deeps, and hold it in a secret chamber in the center of their stronghold.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'Wait here,' they whisper to it in their language. 'One is coming, worthy of you. Be patient.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I remember sounds I heard, extraordinary sounds, associated with the axe called Wroth's Executioner.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Wroth, who styled himself Wroth the Indestructible, was killed at last by the dwarf-captain Artoth Freyhammer, with one mighty blow that shattered his knee. Wroth died from the pain...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...and the wail of his passing was mortifying to behold! Yet Artoth withstood it, and claimed the Executioner for his own...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...and was buried with it, down in the Royal Tombs reserved for dwarves, deep in the silent Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I have said all I should about such things. Do not ask me for more.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard the sound of a pen writing in a book. Every day I heard it - oh, this was many many years ago.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And then the writer spoke. She said, 'It is a terrible risk, to strike the spark of life among the dead! But I must try it - or the City will be lost!' And she never wrote in that book again.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: That was deep, deep down in the Catacombs, but yet I heard it distinctly.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard someone talk about a pair of boots...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: He was quite upset. 'Ozama, you have tricked me!' he shrieked. 'Nothing for the neck - nothing! Your powerful magic is on your feet! What good is that to me? Snakeskin - pah!'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And he threw the boots out the door, into some garbage, and the sound they made sailed out of the Dungeon's Main Halls and into my ears.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Well, very recently I heard a man running and dodging.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: He was cursing under his breath. He said, 'Sammaster, aid me!' And all the while I could hear zombies moaning and the foul jeering of orcs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: And then at last he screamed and died, and the boots he was wearing stayed with his body, far in the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Maybe you are interested in a lamp. I know of one, and can hear the sounds around it...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: ...margoyles jeering at some creature, and baiting it cruelly, as margoyles do.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'Come out into the light!' they say. 'Oh, does that bother you? Does this hurt? Does this hurt even more? Oik oik ik ik ik!'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: These sounds, and many more besides, traveled up from the second floor of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Here is an unusual thing - the Boots of Beguiling Gait.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I hear a woman's voice, ghostly and wan. She laments that none but evil creatures come to her tomb. Her boots go unused, and she, like her beloved city, is dishonored and unmourned.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Her voice drifted up to me from deep down in the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Near here I sense a very precious thing - one of the Starstones of old.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I remember long, long ago, I heard a dwarf say, 'Ya must take it out! The enemy is almost here. The Circle must be closed.' And then the sound of beautiful metal wrenched apart.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: That was long ago. Today, the Starstone rests in the House of Gems - in silence, but for a sad and faint heartbeat.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I heard something spoken over some very handsome boots, the Boots of Stalking.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: A lieutenant of the Cult said it, not very long ago: 'You two! Let them be, they're dead, can't you see that?'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Take the Captain's body with us, leave the others behind. And you! Fetch me the boots off that Orog assassin. Amazing what that one Orog could do, with those boots on.'
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This voice wafted up to me, out of the middle depths of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Hush! I will listen close to those magic gauntlets, the Daemonclaws Of Gr'zak.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Over its short life, hundreds have died for them. But what is this? All is quiet, where they are.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: No! Wait! I hear the faintest of rustling, like cobwebs in moonbreeze. And this faintest of sounds emanates from the very deepest part of the Catacombs.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Oh, I will tell you what I heard spoken near the Gauntlets of Moander.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: The man Athan no longer holds them! They were seized by emissaries of the Cult, and passed from hand to hand to Kya Mordrayn herself.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'That is well,' she said when she got them. The only way to destroy a Pool of Radiance, and it falls into her hands!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: 'That is well,' she said. Her voice echoed up dark tunnels, all the way from a deep cavern beneath Castle Cormanthor.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I know of some gauntlets - the Gauntlets of Light Burden.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I was listening when the elves that bore them were overcome by gargoyles... how the elves screamed before they died! It almost made me stop up my ears.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But now, let me listen... gargoyles still hold the gauntlets, I hear their cruel sniggering. Now I hear wings - they have taken flight - now they land on some tower, and squabble and curse as they perch there.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: These sounds came from not too far away, north and east of here.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: I will tell you about a curious prize, the Stone Mouth.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Once it belonged to Odelinde, the serpent - have you met her? She dwells west and north of here, in the Wind Rider's Shrine.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But I was listening when two thieves pilfered it from her shrine. Drunk on their cleverness, they made their way to the southeast... and came quite close to me...
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But then came such a sound, as if the earth had swallowed them up! And ever since then, the Stone Mouth has lain in quiet darkness.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But hush now! The beasts cry out - can you hear it? I must go.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But I am out of time. Goodbye for now.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But that is all I can tell you now. Come see me again.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But now I can say no more. Goodbye.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But that is all I will say, until we meet again.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But now - the wind falters - the chaos returns. I must go.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But hush! I hear the Song of Faerun. And the Bard of Kara-Tur is singing about you! Two stanzas! Do you wish to hear them, as you walk away?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: O Citizen, which part will you hear?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Very well... what manner of treasure do you seek?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Very well then! Listen to the Song of Faerun.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Shall I tell you what I heard about the treasures of Myth Drannor?
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Oh, there is a weapon, a sacred weapon, the Helm Cleaver. Much talk surrounds it!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Orogs come and demand it. But human voices say 'No, no, not yet. You have not earned it yet.' And orog voices protest in anger and go away, muttering and scheming.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This I have heard in the uppermost halls of the Dungeons.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Oh, I hear a woman wailing, she cries out for a token, a parchment, a blazoned shield, a medallion - any proof that her goddess is remembered!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But evil hisses drown out her cries and deepen her sorrows.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: This I have heard echoing down the ruined ways here in the Nightingale Court.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: Now I hear two people at prayer, their voices mumbling together the name of Mystra.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: He humbly asks the Goddess of Mystery to look with favor on those she has marked to pursue the vital quest.
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! She slaps a medallion down on the table!
keys.speaker: Whisper

keys.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! And the old man raps his staff on the table, to quiet her.

keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The elves' holy book teaches you Alahnmalyr, the Word of Mystra. This Word of Power will speak itself to unseal the glyph of Mystra.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: Kehelben, the Word of Necessity, unseals the Glyph of Safekeeping.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You can tell the magic seal in front of this door is both ancient and elvish. But you do not know the Word of Power that will unseal the Glyph.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: The Word of Redemption summons Miroden Silverblade.
keys.speaker: DM
keys.desc: spoken, this is a big deal & a bit of a surprise

keys.dialogue: The Rivening Word, Frakkun, unseals the Glyph of Moon.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: This sigil of the moon is famous: it represents Corellon Larethian, the protector-god of the elves.
keys.speaker: DM

keys.dialogue: You sense you would need strong magic to open this seal.
